item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
First-Ever Kanda Express to Reach Agartala to Strengthen Onion Availability in the North-East
Over 2,800 MT of Buffer Onion Dispatched Across the North-East through Two Kanda Express Rakes and 44 Truck Consignments
Buffer Onion Consignment of Around 440 MT Expected to Reach Agartala by 18th October 2026
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening onion availability and ensuring affordable prices ahead of the festive season, the Department of Consumer Affairs is expanding the distribution of buffer onions under the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF), with the first-ever Kanda Express movement to Agartala, Tripura. The consignment, carrying approximately 440 MT of onions, is expected to reach Agartala by 18th October 2026.

The initiative marks a further expansion of the Government’s onion distribution network in the North-East, following the successful movement of buffer onions to Assam through Kanda Express. The dispatch to Agartala reinforces the Government’s commitment to expanding supply outreach, improving last-mile availability and ensuring timely access to affordable onions across consumption centres in all regions of the country.

Kanda Express to Strengthen Onion Distribution Across Tripura

The intervention is expected to enhance market coverage across seven of Tripura’s eight districts: Dhalai, South Tripura, Khowai, Unakoti, West Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala.

So far, two Kanda Express rail rakes, carrying 840 MT and 452 MT of onions, respectively, and 44 truck consignments carrying a total of 1,513.46 MT have supplied buffer onions across the North-East. The distribution has covered key locations in Assam, Tripura and Nagaland, including Kamrup, Guwahati, Gomati, Dimapur, Sepahijala, Kohima, Niuland and Chumoukedima.

The expansion of rail-based and road-based distribution is aimed at improving the reach of buffer stocks and supplementing market supplies in key consumption centres across the region.

Fresh Kharif Arrivals Improve Market Availability; Mandi Prices Moderate

With fresh Kharif arrivals gathering pace, onion mandi prices have moderated across major markets. The All-India average mandi price declined from a peak of approximately ₹3,600 per quintal in September to around ₹3,300 per quintal in October.

The calibrated releases from the onion buffer continue to supplement market supplies, improve availability and help moderate retail prices. The Department of Consumer Affairs is continuing these interventions in response to prevailing market conditions to support consumer access to onions at affordable prices.

Retail Onion Prices Decline in 211 Cities; Regional Price Differences Narrow

Over the past two weeks, 211 cities have reported a decline of ₹1–₹13 per kg in retail onion prices. The moderation has been observed across major consuming States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Odisha, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

In Assam, retail onion prices have also moderated in recent weeks, with around 12 centres in the State recording a decline ranging from ₹1 to ₹8 per kg.

The disparity between Assam’s average retail onion prices and the All-India average has narrowed significantly over the past two years. Two years ago, the average retail price in Assam stood at ₹61.96 per kg, compared with the All-India average of ₹54.13 per kg, representing a difference of ₹7.83 per kg. Currently, Assam’s average retail price is ₹54.30 per kg, while the All-India average stands at ₹53.07 per kg, reducing the difference to ₹1.23 per kg.

This convergence indicates a substantial narrowing of the regional price differential, with retail onion prices in Assam now broadly aligned with the national average.

Onion Buffer Disposal to Continue Based on Market Conditions

The Government continues to closely monitor onion prices, market arrivals and supply conditions across the country. Disposal of onions from the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) buffer stock is guided by prevailing market conditions, price trends and availability requirements.

Further releases will be undertaken, as required, in accordance with approved operational decisions to ensure adequate market availability and help moderate undue price volatility.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Polish Youth Delegation Completes Second Edition of Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi

The second edition of the Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme was held from 7 to 14 October 2026. A 19-member Polish youth delegation visited Gujarat, Maharashtra and New Delhi. The programme comprised of visits to sites of shared historical significance, cultural engagements, visits to institutions showcasing India’s scientific, economic and cultural development and interactions with senior Indian leadership.

The programme was announced by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during his State visit to Poland in August 2024 and forms part of the Five-Year Action Plan (2024–2028) for the India–Poland Strategic Partnership. It envisages an annual exchange of Polish youth to India, providing participants with opportunities to explore the country’s history, culture, institutions and contemporary development.

A major highlight of the programme was the visit to the Balachadi Polish Children’s Camp Memorial in Jamnagar, Gujarat, which commemorates the humanitarian contribution of Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja. During the Second World War, the Maharaja provided refuge, education and medical care to Polish children displaced by the war. His compassion earned him the enduring recognition of Dobry Maharaja, or the Good Maharaja, in Poland. The visit offered the delegation an opportunity to learn about this remarkable chapter of shared history and the enduring bonds between the two countries.

Thereafter, the delegation visited the Valivade Polish Refugee Camp Memorial in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, which commemorates the refuge provided to thousands of Polish refugees during and after the Second World War.

The visits to Balachadi and Valivade highlighted India’s humanitarian support to the Polish people during a difficult period and reinforced the historical foundations of India–Poland friendship.

In New Delhi, the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, hosted the Polish youth delegation for an interaction over dinner. The engagement provided an opportunity for the visiting youth to interact with the Minister, exchange perspectives and learn about India’s approach to youth development and participation. The interaction underscored the importance of people-to-people exchanges in fostering mutual understanding and strengthening ties between India and Poland.

The delegates expressed their gratitude for the opportunity to explore India’s rich history and cultural heritage over the course of seven-days. Visits to the Jamsaheb and Valivade camp memorials, Dandi Kutir in Gandhinagar and Kirti Mandir in Porbandar, the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, were among the memorable experiences of the programme. The delegates appreciated the warm hospitality extended to them and described the visit as an enriching experience that had deepened their understanding of India and strengthened their connection with the country.

The delegation also had the opportunity to call on External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and interact with him on matters relating to India–Poland relations and the role of youth exchanges in strengthening bilateral ties.

The successful completion of the second edition reinforces the importance of youth diplomacy in advancing India–Poland relations. By connecting young people with shared history and contemporary India, the programme carries forward the legacy of Maharaja Jam Saheb and strengthens the enduring friendship between the two countries.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Navigating India’s Waterways: Building a Safer, Smarter Network
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:07PM by PIB Delhi

India is building a safer and smarter inland navigation ecosystem as waterway traffic expands. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance keep channels navigable, while India’s first riverine lighthouses on the Brahmaputra add long-range support for 24×7 navigation. Digital platforms provide real-time depth, route and weather information. Together, these interventions are strengthening navigation safety, improving predictability and supporting the growing movement of cargo across India’s waterways.

 

 Strengthening Navigation as Waterways Expand

India’s rivers and waterways are gaining a larger role in the country’s transport network. They are being energised as a force multiplier for the economy, offering a cost-efficient and cleaner mode for transportation. Moving a tonne of freight by water costs roughly one-third of road transport and half of rail. It also generates a fraction of the carbon emissions. This eases pressure on highways and reserves them for passengers and time-sensitive goods.

The country has 111 National Waterways (NW) to promote shipping and navigation. The total length of these waterways is 20,187 km, spread across 23 States and 4 Union Territories. Of these, 32 National Waterways are currently operational. The growing economic value of waterways is reflected in their rapidly increasing freight movement. Cargo movement on inland waterways rose from 29 million metric tonnes (MMT) in 2014–15 to 218 MMT in 2025–26. This represents a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 20.13%. The growth has already surpassed the target of 200 MMT set under Maritime India Vision 2030. Inland waterways are therefore moving from potential to performance.

This expansion of waterways is making it necessary to provide for safer and smarter navigation support and infrastructure that help understand river conditions and navigability across routes. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance are being done to help vessels navigate changing river conditions. Digital platforms are providing information on depths, routes, vessel movement and weather. New navigation infrastructure, including India’s first riverine lighthouses, is adding further support for round-the-clock movement.

 

 Hydrographic Surveys: Knowing the Rivers

A river may appear unchanged from the surface, but the structure of its navigable channel is not visible from outside. Water levels also vary across seasons and river stretches. These changes can affect the route available to vessels. For this reason, inland waterway development requires continuous knowledge of river conditions.

 

Hydrographic surveys

Hydrography involves measuring and describing water bodies and their physical features, like structure of the bed, water depth, flow direction and possible hazards. The purpose is to support navigation and other activities like offshore operations, scientific research, environmental protection and forecasting services. A key objective of hydrographic surveys is to produce navigation charts and maps that provide a clear, comprehensive and updated picture of the surveyed area.

The Inland Waterways Authority of India conducts hydrographic surveys across National Waterways. These surveys measure and analyse river depths, bed profiles, shoals, flow characteristics and morphological changes affecting navigability. These include thalweg surveys that identify and monitor the deepest navigable channel along the river stretch. Terminal & jetty surveys assess depth and approach conditions near terminals and jetties, etc. Continuous hydrographic assessment supports navigational channel (fairway) development, dredging plans, navigational safety and informed decisions for inland water transport (IWT) infrastructure development across the country.

Dredging is the process of removing sediments from the bottom of water bodies. Dredging work is carried out across stretches of National Waterways in order to improve their navigability.

 

River conditions can change rapidly in some stretches. Survey frequency therefore varies according to the requirements of individual waterways. As of September 2026, regular thalweg surveys covered 22 National Waterways. Surveys are conducted weekly, fortnightly or monthly, depending on the waterway. The Indian portion of Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route was also covered under this monitoring system. This is an inland water transit network that enables cargo movement between India and Bangladesh through designated river routes.

Least Available Depth: A Critical Navigation Parameter

One of the most important outputs of hydrographic surveys is the Least Available Depth (LAD). LAD refers to the minimum depth of water available in a navigation channel. It is assessed for a particular stretch and a specific period. LAD directly influences vessel operations and navigation planning. It determines the permissible vessel draft and influences cargo-carrying capacity. It also supports route scheduling and seasonal navigation decisions.

 

 Aids to Navigation: Guiding Vessels Safely

Safe navigation depends on reliable systems that help vessels identify routes, hazards and changing conditions. Under the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021, these systems are formally recognised as Aids to Navigation (AtoN).

An AtoN is a device, system or service external to vessels that is designed and operated to enhance safe and efficient navigation of individual vessels and vessel traffic. These include lighted buoys, radar beacons, lamp posts, channel markers, lighthouses, lightships, etc.

 

Buoys- Floating objects anchored at a definite location to guide or warn mariners, to mark positions of submerged objects, or to moor vessels in lieu of anchoring. Type of buoys include lateral marks, cardinal marks, isolated danger marks, safe water marks, special marks, emergency wreck marking buoy.

Radar beacon (Racon)- Highly responsive, single piece device used by ports and harbor authorities to help mariners easily identify the location of fixed or floating Aids to Navigation. The device transmits in almost any type of weather, unaffected by fog or poor weather and sea conditions.

 

The Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL) is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of general AtoN along India’s coastline. It also serves as the national authority for training on AtoN and Vessel Traffic Services (VTS). India is a signatory to the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), which requires contracting governments to develop and operate appropriate aids to navigation. India also follows the recommendations and guidelines on Aids to Navigation (AtoN) issued by the International Organization for Marine Aids to Navigation (IALA).

Across the national waterways, IWAI maintains a robust system of AToN. Different waterways use different combinations of these aids based on navigation requirements. National Waterway-3 is a strong example of this infrastructure. NW-3, located in the State of Kerala, forms a critical component of the country’s inland water transport network. The West Coast Canal system, connects Kottapuram to Kollam and extends through the Champakkara and Udyogamandal Canals. The entire navigable stretch is equipped with AtoN to support 24×7 navigation. A total of 312 solar-powered lighted FRP (Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic) buoys and 17 beacon lamp posts are deployed along this waterway.

 

 

 Riverine Lighthouses: Bringing 24×7 Navigation Support

India’s inland navigation system entered new territory in March 2026. India announced its first four riverine lighthouses on the Brahmaputra, designated as National Waterway-2. The development marks a significant step in strengthening Aids to Navigation on inland waterways. The four lighthouses are being established at Pandu, Bogibeel, Silghat and Biswanath Ghat. The ₹74-crore project will combine navigational guidance with modern monitoring capabilities.

  • The lighthouses will rise 20 metres above ground, providing prominent navigational reference points.
  • Their geographical range will extend to 14 nautical miles, supporting wider navigational visibility.
  • Their luminous range will extend between 8 and 10 nautical miles, aiding night-time vessel movement.
  • Powered entirely by solar energy, it will provide a clean and reliable source for lighthouse operations.
  • Weather-observation sensors will provide additional information relevant to navigation and safety.
  • The complexes will also feature museums, amphitheatres, cafeterias and landscaped public spaces.
  • Children’s play areas and souvenir shops will add public and tourism-oriented facilities.

Why This Matters for the Brahmaputra

The initiative marks the first deployment of lighthouse infrastructure on an inland waterway in India. It brings a new navigation-safety mechanism to a river corridor with growing transport activity. NW-2 connects Assam's Dhubri to Sadiya across a navigable length of 891 kilometres. It is the longest navigable stretch of any Indian waterway.

The waterway supports movement of cargo, passengers and tourists across the region. It also serves supply chains associated with tea, coal and fertiliser. Cargo movement on NW-2 increased from 0.90 million metric tonnes (MMT) in FY 2024–25 to 1.29 MMT in FY 2025–26. This reinforces the need for stronger navigational infrastructure along the waterway. The new lighthouses will support 24×7 navigation. The project therefore combines navigation safety, technological support and tourism development along the Brahmaputra.

 Digital Navigation & Real-Time Information

Technology is transforming how vessels navigate India’s inland waterways. Digital platforms bring together information on waterways, vessel movement, depth, weather and traffic. This enables mariners and authorities to access critical information when and where it is needed.

Digital Hydrographic Charts: Putting River Information on Screen

Navigation information is provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety through modern hydrographic charts. As of September 2026, Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs) have been prepared for 18 operational and tidal waterways. They are uploaded on portals like PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker. Before 2014, this facility was available only on NW-1 (the Ganga - Bhagirathi - Hooghly river system between Haldia and Prayagraj). Its expansion represents a significant widening of digitally accessible navigation information. The charts complement physical surveys by translating river information into a navigation-ready format.

 

PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker: Connecting Navigation with Real-Time Information

Navigation involves more than knowing channel depth. The Portal for Asset and Navigation Information (PANI) brings river navigation and infrastructure information on a single platform. PANI provides details about National Waterways and associated assets. These include fairways, infrastructure facilities and cross-river structures. The portal also provides jetty connectivity and emergency services for facilitating transportation of cargo.

The IWAI Vessel Tracker and PANI Portal together form a web and mobile-based e-navigation system. It provides real-time vessel tracking, updated navigation routes and depth information. These features support safe and efficient movement on inland waterways.

Naudarshika: Towards Integrated River Traffic Management

Naudarshika, the National River Traffic and Navigation System, has been launched in 2025 for safe, efficient and sustainable vessel movement. The system incorporates real-time Least Available Depth (LAD) information to support navigation. Alongside existing digital platforms such as PANI and LADIS, Naudarshika adds a dedicated system for river traffic and navigation management.

River Information Services: A Traffic Information Network

River Information Services take digital navigation a step further. RIS combines vessel tracking technologies, weather and water sensors and information technology systems. It provides real-time data to vessel operators and authorities. It also supports communication between vessels and control centres. This exchange supports better traffic management and faster operational decisions.

 

RIS on the Ganga

RIS has been implemented on National Waterway-1 (Ganga) across three stretches. These are Haldia–Farakka, Farakka–Patna and Patna–Varanasi. The system includes 4 control stations and 13 base stations. It incorporates Automatic Identification System (AIS)equipment and Very High Frequency (VHF) communication. Meteorological sensors are also part of the network. RIS consoles have been provided on 30 departmental vessels. Together, these components create a real-time traffic-monitoring system along NW-1.

 

 A Connected Approach to Safer Navigation

Safe navigation on India’s waterways is built on continuous knowledge, reliable infrastructure and timely information. Hydrographic surveys help understand changing river conditions, while navigation aids provide visible guidance on the water. Digital platforms are adding another layer of precision through real-time depth, route, weather and traffic information. Together, these systems are making inland navigation more predictable and responsive. As waterway traffic expands, this integrated approach helps create a stronger foundation for safe, efficient and round-the-clock vessel movement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
APEDA Facilitates Export of 1.755 MT of Organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder from Tamil Nadu to Bulgaria
India’s Traditional Palmyra Jaggery Powder Enters Bulgarian Market
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 12:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, facilitated the flag-off of the maiden export consignment of 1.755 MT of NPOP- and EU-certified organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder (Palmyra Blossom Nectar) from Gobichettipalayam in Erode district of Tamil Nadu to Varna, Bulgaria, on 15 October 2026.

The consignment marks an important step towards introducing India’s traditional Palmyra-based products to international markets and diversifying the country’s organic export basket.

The consignment, manufactured and exported by M/s Wellbeing Foods, Erode, in collaboration with M/s Chetty Exports Private Limited, Chennai, will be shipped by sea through Chennai Port. The overseas importer and distributor is M/s Sow Life Ltd, Bulgaria, based in Bulgaria.

The initiative aims to strengthen market linkages for Tamil Nadu’s traditional Palmyra-based products and create new opportunities for producers engaged in organic cultivation. The initiative covers 137 acres under organic cultivation and is expected to benefit farmers through improved market access and export-oriented value chains. The reported price realisation is approximately 15-22% for farmers and 17% higher for the manufacturer, as compared to the domestic market, thereby offering an opportunity to improve returns for participating farmers and support sustainable livelihoods.

Palmyra Jaggery Powder, derived from Palmyra blossom nectar, is a traditional Indian sweetener with potential for value addition and wider international market acceptance. As an alternative to refined sugar, it offers potential nutritional benefits, including vitamins and minerals.

The ceremony was graced by Chairman, APEDA, Shri Abhishek Dev, who also flagged off the consignment. The ceremony was also attended by Secretary, APEDA, Dr. Saswati Bose; senior APEDA officials; representatives of the exporting companies; international partners; progressive farmers; and other stakeholders associated with the export value chain. Their participation highlighted the collaborative efforts to strengthen India’s agricultural exports.

Palmyra-based products are associated with traditional production practices and the use of the Palmyra palm, which has long been part of the agricultural and cultural landscape of Tamil Nadu. Developing export-ready products from this resource offers scope to expand market opportunities while supporting producers and the wider value chain.

APEDA continues to facilitate the export of certified organic and value-added agricultural products by supporting market development, quality compliance and linkages between Indian producers and overseas buyers. The maiden export of organic Palmyra Jaggery Powder to Bulgaria is expected to open avenues for further market expansion and strengthen the presence of India’s traditional products in international markets.

The workshops aimed to promote responsible e-waste management, strengthen cyber security awareness and encourage safe…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Organized Workshops on Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal and E-Waste Management Awareness under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 16 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi

As part of Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Textiles organised workshops on E-Waste Management Awareness and Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal on 15 October 2026, with the participation of over 85 officials, including all Nodal Officers. The workshops aimed to promote responsible e-waste management, strengthen cyber security awareness and encourage safe digital practices in the workplace.

A dedicated Cyber Security Awareness Session was organised to familiarise officials and staff with emerging cyber threats, including phishing attacks, malware, fraudulent WhatsApp messages and digital arrest scams. The session highlighted the importance of identifying suspicious emails, links, attachments and messages, particularly those impersonating known contacts or seeking money, one-time passwords (OTPs) or personal information.

Participants were advised to exercise caution while handling digital communications, refrain from clicking on unknown links or downloading unverified files, avoid sharing sensitive information, and verify the authenticity of suspicious communications before taking any action. The session also emphasised the importance of cyber hygiene, vigilance and the timely reporting of cyber incidents to safeguard official and personal information.

 

The E-Waste Management Awareness session sensitised officials to the adverse environmental impact of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and the release of hazardous substances that may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. They highlighted the importance of resource conservation through the reuse, refurbishment and recycling of electronic equipment, wherever feasible, to recover valuable materials, reduce the demand for raw materials and minimise the volume of waste sent to landfills. Officials were also made aware of the need for proper segregation, safe handling and disposal of obsolete electronic and electrical equipment through authorised channels, in accordance with applicable e-waste management rules.

The sessions encouraged the adoption of sustainable office practices, emphasising that responsible e-waste management contributes to environmental protection, efficient resource utilisation and the promotion of a circular economy.

These initiatives reflect the Ministry of Textiles’ commitment to promoting a cleaner workplace, ensuring responsible resource management and fostering a secure digital environment. By integrating environmental sustainability with cyber security awareness, the Ministry continues to advance the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through improved workplace practices, resource conservation and enhanced digital safety.

The Ministry has also undertaken initiatives for the collection and proper management of e-waste generated within its premises, emphasising the responsible disposal of obsolete and discarded electronic and electrical equipment in accordance with applicable guidelines.

Electronic and electrical equipment that has reached the end of its useful life, including desktop computers, keyboards, photocopiers (Xerox machines), air purifiers and electric hot cases, requires proper handling and disposal in accordance with applicable e-waste management regulations.

    

The initiative highlights the importance of identifying obsolete electronic and electrical equipment, ensuring its appropriate segregation and facilitating its disposal through authorized channels. Responsible e-waste management helps prevent environmental pollution, supports the recovery of valuable materials and promotes the efficient use of resources.

The Ministry encourages awareness among officials and staff regarding sustainable office practices and the importance of proper e-waste disposal. Such efforts contribute towards a cleaner working environment and the broader national objective of sustainable development.

Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Textiles reiterates its commitment to responsible resource management, environmental sustainability and digital safety. The activities reinforce the objectives of Special Campaign 6 by promoting cleanliness, proper disposal of obsolete equipment, efficient resource utilisation and a secure digital environment across its offices.

Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 9:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, observing the Special Campaign 6 and organised a workshop on E-Waste Disposal at Kartavya Bhawan-II, New Delhi, on 15th October, 2026, under the guidance of Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice. The workshop was led by Shri G. Panmei, JS&LC, along with officers and staff members of the Department, including its attached offices, i.e. Official Languages Wing and Vidhi Sahitya Prakashan.

During the workshop, Smt. Archna Srivastava, General Secretary, INDIA-AIDS NGO, along with her team, highlighted the importance of the proper disposal and management of electronic waste (e-waste), emphasising its adverse impact on the environment and the need for responsible handling of obsolete and unusable electronic equipments. The session also underscored the importance of adopting environmentally sustainable practices and preventing the indiscriminate disposal of electronic waste.

Shri G. Panmei, JS&LC, expressed his sincere gratitude to Smt. Archna Srivastava and her team for their valuable contribution towards creating awareness among the officers and employees about the responsible management and disposal of e-waste. He urged all officers and employees to ensure that obsolete electronic equipment is disposed of in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures. He further emphasised that effective e-waste management is essential for environmental protection, resource conservation and fostering a cleaner and more sustainable workplace.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Inaugurates ‘TAKSHANAM’, An Exhibition Bringing Together 150 Artists and Over 250 Sculptures at NGMA
Exhibition celebrates India’s rich sculptural heritage and contemporary practices; introduces the sale of artworks at NGMA for the first time to support artists
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 9:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated TAKSHANAM, a major exhibition featuring over 250 sculptures by 150 participating artists representing diverse generations, artistic backgrounds and approaches to sculptural expression, at the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, was also present on the occasion. Conceived as a shared platform for artistic encounter and exchange, the exhibition explores the continuities, transitions and new possibilities shaping the evolving landscape of Indian sculpture.

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, said, “Art is an important expression of India’s cultural identity and creative spirit. Initiatives such as TAKSHANAM bring artists and audiences closer while encouraging greater appreciation of our artistic traditions and contemporary expressions. By creating space for both established and emerging talent, the exhibition reinforces the importance of nurturing creativity and expanding public engagement with art.”

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, said, “The Ministry of Culture remains committed to encouraging artistic excellence and creating meaningful opportunities for artists across the country. TAKSHANAM brings together diverse artistic voices and provides a platform for their work to reach wider audiences. The initiative to offer artworks for sale is also a noteworthy step towards strengthening engagement between artists, collectors and art enthusiasts.”

Speaking about the exhibition, Dr. Sanjeev Kishor Goutam, Director General, National Gallery of Modern Art, highlighted India’s longstanding sculptural tradition and the need to recognise and support contemporary practitioners. He said, “India has an extraordinary sculptural heritage that reflects its history, cultural achievements and artistic vision. From the Harappan and Mohenjo-daro civilisations, with their terracotta and metal objects and iconic works such as the Dancing Girl and the Priest-King sculpture, to the magnificent sculptural traditions associated with temple architecture and sites such as Ajanta, Ellora and Khajuraho, sculpture has played a significant role in expressing India’s cultural identity. This legacy continues in contemporary practice, with Indian artists such as Anish Kapoor and Subodh Gupta achieving international recognition for their work.

Inspired by the Sanskrit root takṣ (तक्ष्), meaning to carve, shape and fashion, TAKSHANAM reflects on sculpture as an evolving process shaped by the interplay of thought, experience, material and form. Bringing together works by artists across generations and artistic practices, the exhibition highlights the dynamic relationship between India’s rich sculptural heritage and contemporary innovation.

The exhibition features two distinct sections. The first, Eminent Artists, showcases works by experienced and veteran artists whose practices have contributed to the development of Indian sculpture. The second, Open Call Artists, presents works by approximately 80–90 artists selected by a jury following an open call. The exhibition also includes artworks from NGMA’s collection, creating opportunities for dialogue between established practitioners and artists exploring new creative possibilities.

A significant highlight of TAKSHANAM is the first-time initiative to offer artworks for sale at NGMA. The initiative aims to create opportunities for artists to reach collectors and art enthusiasts while encouraging wider engagement with sculptural art. By facilitating greater visibility and potential avenues of financial support, NGMA seeks to contribute to the sustainability of artistic practice, particularly in a medium that often involves substantial material costs, specialised skills and long production timelines.

Through TAKSHANAM, NGMA seeks to celebrate the depth of India’s sculptural heritage while recognising the contribution of contemporary practitioners to its continuing evolution. By bringing together veteran artists, jury-selected participants and works from its collection, the exhibition creates a space for artistic exchange, public engagement and greater appreciation of sculpture as an important medium of cultural expression.

The exhibition will remain open to visitors until 15 November 2026 at the National Gallery of Modern Art, Jaipur House, India Gate, New Delhi.

About the National Gallery of Modern Art

The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, is a premier institution dedicated to the preservation, promotion and appreciation of modern and contemporary Indian art. Through exhibitions, educational initiatives and public engagement programmes, NGMA works to foster a deeper understanding of India’s artistic heritage and its evolving creative expressions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participates in the 114th meeting of the Development Committee Plenary of the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, today
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated as the Governor of the World Bank in the 114th Meeting of the Development Committee Plenary in Bangkok, Thailand, today. The agenda for the meeting was “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”.

The Union Finance Minister delivered the following speech as India’s intervention on the topic of “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”:

“We welcome the continued focus on mobilising private capital and creating jobs. At a time of growing energy market stress, trade fragmentation, climate pressures, and rapid technological change, productive and better-paid jobs remain the most effective pathway to poverty reduction and shared prosperity.

I wish to make six brief points.

First, jobs require ecosystems, not isolated interventions. Sustainable job creation requires high-quality and inclusive economic growth, which in turn needs macroeconomic stability, efficient infrastructure, simple and certain regulations, and broad-based access to finance and skills. Our experience shows that last-mile connectivity to energy and job markets, large-scale physical and digital public infrastructure, financial inclusion, and regulatory trust in market forces are critical for improved productivity and jobs at scale.

Second, the private sector must remain at the centre of the development agenda. Most jobs will be and should be created by private enterprises MSMEs and startups will play a big role. Mobilising private investment is therefore essential. At the same time, success should be measured not by the volume of financing mobilised, but by outcomes: jobs created and rise in productivity.

We encourage stronger collaboration among IBRD, IFC, and MIGA, and faster operationalisation of the WBG Guarantee Platform. Developing economies are constrained by a shortage of risk capital. Guarantees and risk mitigation instruments are among the most effective tools to accelerate risk-capital formation and crowding in private capital.

Third, competitive financing must remain a core priority.  The World Bank must remain a development partner through competitive pricing, tapping tools like local currency financing, stronger guarantee products, and lower transaction costs. Affordable, predictable, and accessible financing must remain and at the core of the Middle-Income strategy.

Fourth, the Knowledge Bank must help address market failures. The most effective interventions from the World Bank Group would be in addressing market failures in critical areas like urbanisation, tourism, agricultural exports and critical minerals. Developing countries stand to benefit greatly from the boost to state capacity that can come from AI: it deserves much greater attention in the Bank's operational and knowledge agenda.

Fifth, we reiterate our longstanding concerns regarding Worldwide Governance Indicators and similar composite assessments. Given their far-reaching implications, there is a need for a comprehensive review and revision of existing methodologies to ensure that they are transparent, objective, evidence-based, and better aligned with current realities and the diverse development experiences of member countries. This will be essential for preserving the integrity of the Bank's knowledge products.

Finally, evolution must strengthen voice and development impact.  The ultimate measure of success is whether reforms help countries create jobs, raise productivity, reduce poverty, and improve living standards. We also reiterate the importance of strengthening the voice and representation of developing countries in the governance architecture of the Bank.

Our constituency stands ready to work with fellow shareholders, management, and development partners to advance these objectives.”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
National Workshop held on “Strengthening Digital Data Systems and Evidence-Based Learning” under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission at Gurugram, Haryana on 12th and 13th October, 2026
“What gets measured gets done; what gets measured gets improved”: Secretary, Rural Development calls for robust, member-level data to drive the next phase of DAY-NRLM
LokOS to evolve from a reporting platform into trusted community-finance infrastructure, backed by a stronger monitoring, evaluation and learning framework
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, held a two-day National Workshop on “Strengthening Digital Data Systems and Evidence-Based Learning” under DAY-NRLM, on 12th and 13th October 2026, at Gurugram, Haryana. Representatives of State Rural Livelihoods Missions, NITI Aayog, the World Bank, GIZ, J-PAL, Gates Foundation, 3ie, BRAC, NABARD, NPCI, financial institutions and development partners participated in the workshop.

In his keynote address, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, GoI, said that around 10 crore women organised into nearly 92 lakh SHGs have leveraged formal credit of about ₹14 lakh crore. The next phase must strengthen around 87 lakh enterprises and track the progress of Lakhpati Didis towards the target of six crore. He said “what gets measured gets done; what gets measured gets improved,” and called for LokOS to become an operational platform integrated with banking portals for a seamless digital credit journey. He urged that data be complete, consistent, current, correct and verifiable, and that the Mission move from monitoring dashboards to decision-support systems.

Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, Department of Rural Development, GoI, outlined three strategic shifts for DAY-NRLM i.e. from inclusion to prosperity, from credit access to quality credit, and from supported to self-reliant institutions. He said LokOS can build a digital record of credibility for each woman based on her saving and repayment behaviour. He stressed that this data belongs to the women who generate it and must be used in their interest.

The Ministry has been closely working with the State Rural Livelihoods Missions and technical partners to systematically resolve operational and system-related issues, assign clear responsibilities and timelines, strengthen the training and handholding of field functionaries and community cadres, and facilitate cross-learning through the replication of State best practices. Progress in digitising SHG, VO and CLF profiles and recording their financial transactions on LokOS was reviewed during the workshop. Validation of member and institution data was stated to be the foundation for transactions, credit histories and programme analysis. The workshop will strengthen the monitoring framework by moving to household, institutional and enterprise outcomes, using LokOS as an evidence base, connecting administrative datasets across schemes, and investing in State capacity to generate and use evidence

The workshop was also attended by Shri Amit Shukla, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, GoI; Dr. Monika, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, GoI; Smt. Rangoli Pathak, Joint Director, Ministry of Rural Development, GoI; Shri Suraj Bhan, CEO, Haryana SRLM; Shri Himanshu Sharma, CEO, Bihar SRLM; and Shri Sumit Kumar, CEO-ZP, Gurugram, Haryana.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India’s Ramsar Site tally reaches 103 with addition of Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP)
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today announced that India’s Ramsar site tally has reached 103, with the designation of Sukhna Wetland in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh as the latest additions to the list.

India’s Ramsar site tally reaches 103 🇮🇳🌿 India continues to strengthen its commitment to wetland conservation, with Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh becoming the latest additions to the list of Ramsar Sites. This milestone highlights the importance PM Shri @narendramodi ji’s government has been laying on wetlands in conserving biodiversity, enhancing water and climate security, and sustaining local livelihoods. These additions reaffirm India’s ongoing efforts to conserve its rich wetland ecosystems and strengthen the ecological, climatic and livelihood benefits they provide. 🌏💧 I congratulate Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh for this feat. Dear travellers, do visit Sukhna and Sauj next time you have a couple days at hand. #AmritDharohar

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) October 15, 2026

In a social media post, Shri Yadav said that India continues to strengthen its commitment to wetland conservation. He highlighted the importance being accorded to wetlands by the Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, particularly for conserving biodiversity, enhancing water and climate security, and sustaining local livelihoods.

The Minister said the latest additions reaffirm India’s ongoing efforts to conserve the country’s rich wetland ecosystems and strengthen the ecological, climatic and livelihood benefits they provide. Congratulating Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh on the achievement, Shri Yadav invited tourists to visit Sukhna and Sauj to explore their natural beauty.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
12th session of India – Japan Joint Working Group (JWG) on Roads and Road Transportation Sector
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

The 12th session of India – Japan Joint Working Group (JWG) on Roads and Road Transportation Sector was held on 15th October, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Ministry of Road Transport and Highways organized the meeting with the participation of representatives from the Government of India and the Government of Japan, along with relevant institutions and industry stakeholders.

The meeting provides an important platform for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the road transportation sector between the two nations, with particular emphasis on advanced construction technologies, tunnel and bridge engineering, sustainable infrastructure development, and the application of new and digital technologies in road management.The deliberations facilitated the exchange of technical knowledge, experience and best practices between the two countries, while exploring opportunities for enhanced collaboration in the planning, construction, operation and maintenance of road infrastructure.

The meeting aligns with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 articulated by Shri Narendra Modi, Hon’ble Prime Minister, which envisages India as a developed nation by the centenary of its Independencesupporting economic growth, improving connectivity, strengthening logistics efficiency and facilitating access to opportunities across regions. Shri Nitin Gadkari, Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, has emphasised on the development of world-class, safe, efficient, sustainable and technology-driven road infrastructure including bridges & tunnels that supports India’s economic growth and enhances the convenience and quality of life of its citizens.

 

Under whole of Government approval, Ministry of Railway and Ministry of Power also actively participated in the Meeting.

Experts and representatives from the Indian and Japanese technical institutions and industry also shared their knowledge and experiences during the technical presentations and interactive question-and-answer sessions. The deliberations provided an opportunity to exchange perspectives on the adoption of innovative technologies and sustainable practices for improving the quality, efficiency and management of road infrastructure.

The meeting reaffirmed the importance of India–Japan cooperation in advancing road and transport infrastructure through technological innovation, sustainable construction practices and the exchange of technical expertise.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
14th High Level Meeting Between Indian Coast Guard and Korea Coast Guard Held at Incheon
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The 14th High Level Meeting (HLM) between the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and the Korea Coast Guard (KCG) was held at Incheon, Republic of Korea, on 14 October 2026. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation and further enhancing strategic engagement between the two maritime security agencies.

During the meeting, both sides reviewed existing operational frameworks and discussed roadmap strategies to further enhance cooperation in key areas, including Maritime Search and Rescue (M-SAR), Marine Pollution Response (MPR), Maritime Law Enforcement (MLE), capacity building and operational coordination.

Reaffirming their commitment to the existing Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), both Coast Guards agreed to further strengthen professional exchanges, joint training exercises, bilateral ship visits and real-time information sharing.

The 14th HLM reaffirmed the shared commitment of the Indian Coast Guard and the Korea Coast Guard to deepen operational synergy and contribute towards maintaining a safe, secure and environmentally sustainable maritime ecosystem in the region.

The Indian Coast Guard delegation, on an official visit to the Republic of Korea from 13 to 16 October 2026, was led by Inspector General T. Sashi Kumar, while the Korea Coast Guard delegation was led by Senior Superintendent General Im Myeong Gil.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with the contingent of Indian athletes who participated in Asian Games 2026
Our Asian Games champions have made the Tricolour fly high and enhanced its honour and pride: PM
The pride of the Tricolour in every arena, India’s new identity in sports, New champions in every sport, And new records in our name; We will do it: PM
India is all set to become a global sporting powerhouse: PM
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Games 2026 today. He remarked on the wonderful atmosphere created by gathering with so many medal-winners in one place. "All of you young athletes are examples of how when passion turns into victory, it brings a glow to faces along with medals,” remarked Shri Modi.

Praising the athletes for bringing immense pride to 140 crore citizens, the Prime Minister emphasized that the ultimate achievement lies in elevating the honor and glory of the national flag. He congratulated the players, their coaches, support staff, and families for this collective national triumph. "Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is also the success of crores of citizens of the country,” affirmed PM Modi.

Remembering former President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam on his birth anniversary, the Prime Minister paid rich tributes to the late statesman. He highlighted how Dr. Kalam's remarkable life and visionary outlook continue to guide the nation. "His life and his vision are an inspiration for all of us,” remarked Shri Modi.

Recalling the historic milestones achieved at the Asian Games, the Prime Minister celebrated the double Gold victory of the men's and women's hockey teams, with the women ending a 44-year wait, alongside consecutive medals for both cricket teams and dual Golds in Kabaddi. He also lauded the five Golds in archery, stellar displays in shooting, boxing, and wrestling, new athletics records, a weightlifting medal after 28 years, and the first marathon success since 1982. "This time the Asian Games have been memorable for us in many ways,” noted PM Modi.

Applauding the extraordinary contribution of female athletes who secured 38 of India's 85 total medals, including 11 Golds, the Prime Minister stated that their tally represents far more than mere statistics and reflects an empowered New India. He also highlighted how Indian players scripted history by winning maiden Asian Games medals in disciplines like mixed martial arts, soft tennis, and specific sailing events. "Today India is winning medals even in those sports in which we had never won a medal in the history of the Asian Games before,” observed Shri Modi.

Calling upon the athletes to scale even greater heights in the sporting arena, the Prime Minister led an energetic pledge where the contingent chanted "We will Do it!" in unison. He rallied them to uphold the Tricolor's glory on every field, forge a new sporting identity for the nation, and create new champions across every discipline. "More new records in our name, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.

Drawing attention to the venue of the gathering, the Prime Minister reminded the athletes that the stadium is named after the legendary Major Dhyan Chand, who famously practiced hockey for hours into the night. He pointed to the icon's relentless dedication to illustrate that grand resolutions require years of sustained patience and hard work. "This hard work of his reminds us time and again that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day,” remarked Shri Modi.

Contrasting the past dozen years of diligent work on the sports ecosystem with an earlier era when India won only a handful of medals and remained unaware of many disciplines, the Prime Minister recalled how the nation previously had zero representation in over half the Olympic events. He questioned how the country could ever expect to win laurels without first stepping onto the field of competition. "If we do not even compete, how will we bring medals?” remarked PM Modi.

Highlighting a decisive shift in national sporting policy, the Prime Minister emphasized the government's firm determination to eradicate this historic apathy and self-doubt. He celebrated the resulting surge in Indian athletes competing across international arenas today. "We took this resolution that we will remove this pessimistic mindset!” asserted Shri Modi.

Attributing this transformation to a far-reaching vision and sincere effort over the last 10 to 12 years, the Prime Minister detailed the creation of a transparent, modern sports ecosystem anchored by the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and the expanded Khelo India initiative. He pointed out that the government has committed massive financial resources to strengthen sports federations and grassroots programs across the country. "To expand Khelo India and strengthen sports federations, more than 36 thousand crore rupees were allocated,” noted PM Modi.

Detailing the rapid expansion of grassroots infrastructure across over a thousand Khelo India Centers, the Prime Minister listed thousands of new stadiums, multi-purpose halls, athletics tracks, football and hockey grounds, and swimming pools being built across cities of all sizes. He also highlighted direct financial support to athletes, including a 50,000-rupee monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance under TOPS and funding for international coaching stints. "If there is a need to go outside the country for coaching in any sport, the government is facilitating that too and providing financial assistance for it,” observed Shri Modi.

Underscoring the drive to maximize competitive exposure through the Winter Games, Sansad Khel Pratiyogitas, and the new 'Khelo Bharat Niti', the Prime Minister also praised Divyang athletes for bringing laurels to the nation. He noted that the athletes' own triumphs prove what happens when players know the entire nation backs their journey. "Today every player has this confidence that the country stands with them throughout their entire journey,” affirmed PM Modi.

Spotlighting the remarkable performances of 15-to-17-year-old athletes in the contingent as proof that starting young provides an added advantage, the Prime Minister outlined a targeted focus on identifying and training children aged five to fifteen through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India. Looking ahead to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, India's hosting of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, and the aspiration to host the 2036 Olympics, he recalled his Red Fort announcement of a nationwide village-level talent hunt. "These very players will bring medals for India in the times to come,” asserted Shri Modi.

Expressing unwavering confidence in the nation's grand resolutions, the Prime Minister led another spirited "We will Do it!" chant with the athletes. He rallied them around the shared goals of hosting major global sporting events, joining the ranks of top sporting nations, building world-class infrastructure, and becoming a global sports hub. "A champion from every corner of India, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.

Connecting the Asian Games triumph to the broader aspirations of Indian youth, the Prime Minister noted how young innovators have propelled India into the world's third-largest startup ecosystem while pioneering breakthroughs in space, satellite technology, defense, and Artificial Intelligence. He emphasized that just like in sports, youth from small towns and villages are driving this entrepreneurial wave, backed by a decade of systemic reforms that assure them of the nation's full support. "They have the trust that to take their dreams forward, the entire capability of the country stands with them,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Expanding on the broader economic impact of the sporting boom, the Prime Minister pointed out that government initiatives are benefiting far more than just on-field competitors. He highlighted the rapid emergence of diverse professional fields such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. "This has created new avenues of employment and enterprise for the youth,” noted PM Modi.

Urging the internationally experienced medalists to shoulder the responsibility of mentoring the next generation, the Prime Minister asked them to visit schools, return to their original playing grounds, and engage with children in their home villages and cities. He emphasized that sharing their hard-earned experiences could profoundly inspire young aspirants dreaming of following in their footsteps. "Perhaps, a small word from you might give a child the courage to move ahead in sports,” remarked Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the deeper value of athletics beyond the playing field, the Prime Minister stated that sports instill lifelong discipline, adaptability, steadfastness toward long-term goals, and the resilience to rise after a defeat. He noted that these foundational qualities naturally integrate into daily life to guide individuals through every challenge. "This very sportsperson spirit comes in handy throughout life,” observed PM Modi.

Concluding his address with his signature maxim that "one who plays, will flourish," the Prime Minister praised the athletes' enthusiasm as New India's greatest strength and led a final "We will Do it!" chant encompassing the goals of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, a top-three economy, an Aatmanirbhar Bharat, a global manufacturing hub, technology leadership, space exploration, and hosting the Olympics. He extended his best wishes for all their future tournaments and endeavors. "With this very self-confidence, we have to take India to new heights,” asserted Shri Modi.

 

Our Asian Games champions have made the Tricolour fly high! Their achievements show what passion, perseverance and belief can achieve. https://t.co/m3gOPecQCo

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026-Mysuru
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale Visits SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 in Mysuru
Highlights Government Initiatives for Economic Empowerment
Mela Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
12 States And Union Territories Partcipating in the Mela
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Nine-day SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026, organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is continuing at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, in Karnataka since October 11. The Mela will conclude on October 19 Monday.

A Senior Official in the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) said the Mela provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.

He said the Mela has been jointly organized by three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.

Union Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale during his visit to SHILP SAMAGAM MELA highlighted the Central Government’s commitment to the economic and social empowerment of socially disadvantaged and vulnerable sections.

The Minister was informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.

The Minister visited and inspected stalls with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

Addressing a press conference at the Government Guest House in Mysuru earlier, Shri Athawale said that the Central Government has introduced various welfare and development schemes to promote the economic and social empowerment of Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, sanitation workers, transgender persons and persons with disabilities, including persons with visual impairments. He highlighted the role of the National Development Corporations in extending concessional financial assistance, with loans ranging from ₹1.5 Lakh To ₹35 Lakh under various schemes, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and scheme provisions.

 

Emphasizing the Government’s commitment to social welfare, the Minister stated that ₹1.98 Lakh Crore had been allocated for social welfare schemes in the Union Budget, out of a total budget of ₹ 57 Lakh Crore.

Shri Athawale also referred to the constitutional provisions for reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the provision of 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes following the recommendations of the Mandal Commission, and the subsequent introduction of 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections.

Highlighting the reach of flagship welfare initiatives, Shri Athawale referred to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, under which around four crore beneficiaries have received benefits across the country, including approximately 10 lakh beneficiaries in Karnataka. He also highlighted the contribution of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana in expanding financial inclusion, stating that 2,22,23,000 bank accounts had been opened in Karnataka under the scheme.

Referring to educational assistance in Mysuru district, the Minister stated that approximately 13,000 students studying in Classes I to VIII and 31,000 post-matric students had benefited from educational support. He further noted that nearly 75 per cent of the 7,000 students residing in 84 government hostels in the district belonged to Scheduled Castes. Eligible beneficiaries were also receiving monthly stipends of ₹1,850 for college students and ₹1,750 for high school students, he said.

The Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills.

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.

The Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

In addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.

The Ministry has been organizing SHILP SAMAGAM MELAS since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.

The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first SHILP SAMAGAM MELA of the financial year 2026–27.

The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati, Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 will continue at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans. Through such initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address during interaction with the participants of Asian Games 2026
Posted On: 15 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Sports Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji, Minister of State for Sports Sister Raksha Khadse ji, all of you young athletes, coaches, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Coming among all of you fills me with energy as well. So many medal winners gathered together, and meeting all of them at once, is no ordinary thing. It is a very pleasant feeling. All of you young athletes are examples of how, when passion is transformed into victory, it brings not only medals but also a glow on the face. And, of course, it makes the nation shine as well.

Friends,

You have given 1.4 billion countrymen an opportunity to feel proud. Because the greatest achievement, if there is one, is to enhance the honour of the Tiranga. You have enhanced the pride of the Tiranga, you have increased its honour. Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is the success of millions and millions of citizens of this country. On behalf of all the people of India, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you. At the same time, I also wholeheartedly congratulate your coaches, your support staff, and your families.

Friends,

Today is also the birth anniversary of our former President, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. His life and his vision are an inspiration to all of us. I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.

Friends,

In many ways, these Asian Games have been memorable for us. Both our men’s and women’s hockey teams are present here today. Both teams won gold medals this time. And especially our women’s hockey team, you ended a long wait of 44 years by bringing home the gold medal. In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time and, in fact, repeated their own record. In kabaddi too, both our men’s and women’s teams won gold medals. Likewise, five gold medals in archery, and where there are five, there is the grace of the Almighty. Outstanding performances in shooting, major successes in boxing and wrestling, new records in athletics, a medal in weightlifting after twenty-eight years, and India’s success in marathon events for the first time since 1982. All this is truly a matter of great joy.

Friends,

I especially want to appreciate our daughters. Out of the 85 medals won by India, 38 medals were won by our women athletes. Among them were 11 gold medals as well. And these medals are not merely numbers; they represent a powerful image of New India. Today, India is winning medals even in sports where, in the history of the Asian Games, we had never before won a medal. In Mixed Martial Arts, Soft Tennis, and certain sailing events, our players created new history by winning medals for the first time.

Friends,

Now we must reach even greater heights in sports. We have to, don't we? We have to achieve even more, don't we? I want to place a few resolutions before you. And all of you must respond with full enthusiasm: We will Do it! So, repeat after me:

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

A new identity for India in sports, We will Do it!

New champions in every sport, We will Do it!

More records in our name, We will Do it!

Friends,

The stadium in which we are gathered today is named after Major Dhyan Chand ji. His dedication towards hockey was so great that he would practise for hours even at night. His hard work repeatedly reminds us that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day. They require years of patience and sustained effort.

Friends,

Over the past 12 years, India too has worked with great patience and dedication on its sportspersons and its sports ecosystem. There was a time when India could win only a handful of medals in major tournaments. In many sports, people in the country did not even know that such sports existed. There used to be huge events such as the Olympics, yet India had no representation in more than half of the sports. Just think about it. If we do not even compete, then where will the medals come from?

Friends,

We took a pledge that we would remove this pessimistic mindset. And the result is that today, our representation is increasing on every global platform.

Friends,

How did this transformation happen? It happened through the same spirit that helped you achieve success. Over the past 10–12 years, the country worked continuously with dedication and sincerity, pursued a long-term vision, and built a transparent and modern ecosystem for sports. As all of you know, we launched the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). We launched the Khelo India Scheme. Over time, its scope was expanded further. As Mansukh Bhai mentioned earlier, more than ₹36,000 crore has been allocated for expanding Khelo India and strengthening sports federations.

Friends,

Today, more than one thousand Khelo India Centres have been established across the country. Stadiums, mini-stadiums, and multi-purpose sports halls have been created. Athletics tracks, football grounds, hockey grounds, swimming pools, and thousands of such sports infrastructures are being built in both small and large cities. Under this scheme, direct assistance is being provided to athletes as well. They are being given Out-of-Pocket Allowances. Under the TOPS scheme, athletes receive ₹50,000 per month. If any sport requires training abroad, the government is facilitating it and providing financial assistance.

Friends,

To ensure that young people get maximum opportunities to play and compete, events such as Winter Games have been launched, and Members of Parliament Sports Competitions have been started. The country created a new Sports Policy and a new Khelo Bharat Policy. Our para-athletes are also enhancing the nation's pride through their talent and capabilities. For them too, better opportunities and modern facilities in sports are being ensured. And that is why every athlete today feels confident that the nation stands beside them throughout their journey. And when an athlete feels that support, what they can achieve for the nation is something all of you yourselves are excellent examples of.

Friends,

This time, many players in Team India at the Asian Games were only 15 to 17 years old. At such a young age, they enhanced the nation’s pride through their outstanding performances. They won the hearts of the people of the country. This shows that age is no barrier to success. In fact, in sports, starting young is an added advantage. That is why our effort is to identify sporting talent from an early age. We are giving special focus to identifying talent among children aged five to fifteen and training them properly. In the coming years, thousands of new athletes will receive opportunities through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India programmes. We must strengthen our preparations for future sporting events. The Los Angeles Olympics will take place in 2028. India will host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. And hosting the Olympics in 2036 is also India’s aspiration. Keeping this in mind, from the Red Fort I spoke about launching a Talent Hunt campaign. Today, talent is being identified in villages across the country and nurtured. These very athletes will bring medals for India in the years ahead.

Friends,

Our dreams are big. Our resolutions are also big. And today, India has the confidence to achieve them. Every Indian has that confidence. Therefore, with complete conviction, I say: 

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

India among the top sporting nations, We will Do it!

India as a global sports hub, We will Do it!

World-class sports infrastructure in India, We will Do it!

A champion from every corner of India, We will Do it!

Friends,

Our success at the Asian Games is also an example of India’s changing mindset. It shows how today’s youth are impatient to scale every height. There is no summit higher than the determination of India’s youth. There is no goal beyond the capability of our youth power. The limitless sky of possibilities lies before us, and India’s youth are themselves deciding the destination. That is why, in a short span of time, India has become the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Our youth are building companies in the space sector. They are working on satellite technology. The same youth are developing new technologies in the defence sector. They are conducting new experiments in Artificial Intelligence. And this transformation is not limited to big cities. Just as talented individuals from remote areas are now getting opportunities in sports, similarly, in startups, research, and other ventures, young people from small cities and villages are coming forward with new ideas. Behind this confidence lies a deep trust. The systems developed by the country over the past decade have given young people confidence that they can dream big. They know that the full strength of the nation stands behind them to help them realise those dreams.

Friends,

The benefits of our efforts are not limited only to athletes who compete on the field. New career opportunities are being created for youth in areas such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. As sports develop, many related professions are also advancing. This has opened new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for young people.

Friends,

Whatever field we may be in today, we must work hard for our own success. At the same time, we must also take responsibility for shaping the next generation. Now you possess the experience of international tournaments. Therefore, I would request that you devote some time to those children who dream of progressing just as you did. You must water their dreams with the sweat of your own efforts. That is how success comes. Whenever you get an opportunity, meet children in your village and your town. Visit different schools. Be sure to visit the grounds where you first began playing. Your experiences can be extremely valuable to those children. Perhaps a single word from you may give a child the courage to move forward in sports.

Friends,

The youth of the country do not draw inspiration from you only in sports. Because the role of sports extends beyond the playing field. Sports teach us discipline in life. They teach us how to rise again after falling. They teach us how to win after losing. Sports teach us how to stay committed to a goal for a long time and how to adapt ourselves to changing circumstances. These lessons become part of our everyday lives. And this sporting spirit serves us throughout our lives.

Friends,

I always say: The one who plays, blossoms. So keep playing, keep blossoming. Once again, my many best wishes to all of you for the upcoming competitions and for all your future efforts. Your enthusiasm and your confidence are the greatest strengths of New India. With this confidence, we must take India to new heights.

So come, once again, with full energy, say with me:

Viksit Bharat, We will Do it!

Viksit Bharat at Twenty Forty Seven, We will Do it!

We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!
