item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to honor top-performing States/UTs, District Police and Police Stations for recovery of lost mobile handsets through Sanchar Saathi
Awards to be presented in upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT
Number of handsets traceable and recovered are to be key performance parameters
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India will recognize and award the best-performing States/Union Territories (UTs), Police Districts and Police Stations for their exemplary efforts in recovering lost/stolen mobile handsets traced through the Sanchar Saathi portal - a citizen centric initiative of DoT to empower mobile subscribers, strengthen their security and increase awareness about citizen centric initiatives of the Government. The awards will be presented during the upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT.

The initiative aims to acknowledge the significant contribution of State/UT Police authorities in tracing and recovering lost or stolen mobile handsets and returning them to their rightful owners. It also seeks to encourage greater coordination between DoT, its License Service Area (LSA) field units, police authorities and telecom operators, promote the adoption of effective recovery practices, and improve recovery outcomes for citizens across the country.

The awards will be based on measurable performance parameters, i.e based on accuracy (i.e handsets recovered against trace generated) and total number of handsets recovered etc. These parameters will help recognize the scale, accuracy and timeliness of recovery efforts undertaken by States/UTs, Police Districts and Police Stations. The detailed evaluation methodology and applicable assessment period will be finalized by DoT.

The State/UT-wise data on mobile handsets traced and recovered through the Sanchar Saathi portal is publicly available on the portal’s dashboard, which also provides visibility into recovery trends. This data will serve as an important reference for assessing performance and identifying high-performing jurisdictions and police units.

Sanchar Saathi portal facilitates the blocking and tracing of lost or stolen mobile handsets through the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) facility. When a reported handset is subsequently detected on a telecom network, traceability information is generated and made available to the respective Police authorities, supporting police efforts to locate and recover the device. An alert regarding the traceability is also sent to the citizen through SMS and email.

The initiative reflects the importance of close coordination among DoT, its LSA field units, Telecom Service Providers and State/UT Police authorities in strengthening mobile security and protecting citizens’ digital assets. The proposed awards will provide a platform to recognize outstanding work, encourage healthy performance-driven competition and promote the sharing of successful practices across jurisdictions.

DoT reiterates its commitment to strengthening the Sanchar Saathi ecosystem and supporting law-enforcement agencies in improving the recovery of lost and stolen mobile handsets. Citizens can access the portal at www.sancharsaathi.gov.in or use Sanchar Saathi Mobile app to report lost or stolen mobile handsets and avail following citizen centric services.

Services at the fingertips of every citizen

Sanchar Saathi brings the following citizen-centric services on a single platform:

Chakshu – Report suspected fraud communication and spam: Report suspicious calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages – such as fake KYC or bill- payment alerts, impersonation of Government, police or bank officials, and fraudulent investment, job or loan offers – in a few simple steps.

Know mobile connections in your name: Check all mobile connections issued on your identity and report those which you have not taken or no longer require, so that they cannot be misused.

Block your lost or stolen mobile handset: Block the handset across the networks of all telecom operators so that it cannot be used anywhere in India, enable its tracing, and unblock it once it is found.

Know the genuineness of your mobile handset: Verify a handset through its IMEI number before buying a new or second-hand phone.

Report incoming international calls with Indian numbers: Report calls from abroad that are disguised as domestic (+91) numbers, helping the Government act against illegal telecom set-ups.

Trusted Contact Details: Verify the genuine customer care numbers, email IDs and website links of banks and financial institutions before sharing any information.

Keep Yourself Aware: Access awareness material on prevailing fraud trends such as fake loan apps, investment scams, fake job calls and fake traffic challans

DoT is fully committed to ensure safety of citizens through its proactive actions for curbing misuse of telecom resources for cybercrime and financial frauds. Sanchar Saathi is also available as mobile app and can be downloaded from:

  • For Android:: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dot.app.sancharsaathi
  • For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/app/sanchar-saathi/id6739700695

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes (HLCDC) Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar (Retd.) launches official Portal to Enhance Public Engagement and Scientific Data Gathering
The web portal is available at https://demography.mha.gov.in and fully operational and open for public access, stakeholder submissions, and data interaction
This portal facilitates the Central Ministries/Departments, State/UT Government, NGOs & individuals to give inputs on un-natural demographic changes, it’s causes and underlying factors behind these changes
The inputs will help the Committee to analyse and identify the causes of demographic changes and to recommend a well-organised and permanent operational system for the legal, fair and time bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes (HLCDC), Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar (Retd.) has launched the Committee’s dedicated digital web portal in New Delhi.

The web portal is available at https://demography.mha.gov.in and fully operational and open for public access, stakeholder submissions, and data interaction.

The portal facilitates the Central Government Ministries/Departments, State/UT Governments, NGOs/Institutions and individuals to give inputs/ data/information on un-natural demographic changes, it’s causes and underlying factors behind these changes, abnormal settlement pattern etc. These inputs will help the Committee to analyse and identify the causes of demographic changes and to recommend a well-organised and permanent operational system for the legal, fair and time bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants residing in the country.

The committee was formally constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on May 26, 2026.

The terms of reference of the Committee are as under: -

  1. To undertake an extensive consideration of the challenges arising from demographic changes, including due to illegal immigration.
  2. To study the possible causes of such demographic changes, such as variations in fertility, cross border movement (including illegal immigration), economic opportunities, and other socioenvironmental factors.
  3. To identify the underlying factors behind these changes, including illegal immigration, abnormal settlement patterns, and planned migration.
  4. To analyze structural population changes at the level of religious or social communities, especially those diverging from uniform trends.
  5. To recommend a well-organized and permanent operational system for the legal, fair and time bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants already residing in the country.
  6. To recommend an appropriate institutional mechanism to strengthen border management, population stabilization, and identification systems for sustained monitoring of such trends.
  7. To propose a comprehensive policy framework to enhance coordination between Central and State Governments in matters related to illegal immigration and resultant demographic imbalance.
  8. The Committee may recommend any other measure it deems appropriate to address the challenges arising from demographic changes, including due to illegal immigration.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications DoT and ITU organise AI for Good Build-a-thon 5.0 at India Mobile Congress 2026 Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU inaugurates the Build-a-thon 5.0 in the august presence of senior DoT leadership and distinguished experts Build-a-thon 5.0 focuses on building Agentic AI solutions complied with Indian policies in the domain of telecommunications Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
DoT and ITU organise AI for Good Build-a-thon 5.0 at India Mobile Congress 2026
Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU inaugurates the Build-a-thon 5.0 in the august presence of senior DoT leadership and distinguished experts
Build-a-thon 5.0 focuses on building Agentic AI solutions complied with Indian policies in the domain of telecommunications
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in collaboration with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), organised the Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Good Build-a-thon 5.0, a hands-on capacity-building event that brought together teams from across the country to develop Agentic AI solutions for the telecommunications sector on the last day of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.

The event, themed “Creating innovative agents in 5G”, was inaugurated by Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU, in the august presence of senior DoT leadership and distinguished representatives from academia, industry, international organisations and the technology ecosystem.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jamoussi underscored the importance of Agentic AI solutions that are contextualized to the country, compliant with international standards and governed by local policies. He stressed that, to fully realize the benefits of integrating AI into workflows, policy gaps must be identified through real AI solutions and then addressed in regulation.

Strong leadership from Shri Prabhat Dikshit, DDG(Satellite) and Shri Bishnu Dubey, Director (AS-II), DoT along with support from C-DoT and the organizing teams was critical for the success of this event. The judges panel also included Shri Amit Shrivastava, DDG(MT), TEC, Dr. Brajesh Mishra, Executive Director, C-DoT and Shri Prachish Khanna, DDG(Media), DoT.

From Kick-off to Prototypes

The Build-a-thon 5.0 opened in early July with more than 25 registered teams, each with an average of four members. During the preparation phase, ITU and DoT experts held five online mentoring sessions covering the Build-a-thon problem statements, the ITU-T Y.3172 standardized machine learning pipeline, the ITU AI Readiness 2.0 report (a global benchmark for AI Ready use cases) and open-source data sources.

More than 10 hours of mentoring resulted in 16 well-designed AI prototype submissions. The entries featured a range of agent types, including knowledge-base agents that solve domain-specific problems, policy and legal adviser agents that play an institutional role within the solution, and coordinator agents that orchestrate multiple agents.

Standout Solutions

Several submissions distinguished themselves:

  • Multi-agent network analysis with policy mapping: One solution combines a country-specific 5G/telecom knowledge base with multi-agent AI analysis, progressive network-error scenarios, policy and standards mapping, gap identification, human supervision and auditable evidence.
  • Unified traffic and security controller: Another proposes an AI agent-based controller that manages traffic priority and security together, based on three inputs: service intent, available network resources and data sensitivity.
  • Law inside the control loop: A third embeds regulation directly into network operations. Three optimizer agents (Spectrum, Energy and Slicing) propose actions, while a Regulator agent with veto power checks each against ten rules grounded in Indian telecom law, citing the official text. A Policy & Legal Adviser answers questions drawn from 16 official documents, and a gap analyzer reports where Indian law is silent.

Judges noted the energy and dedication of the participating teams, and lively discussions took place between judges and teams during the interaction session. Presentations clearly set out each use case’s problem statement and its mapping against policy, standards and global benchmarks, and were accompanied by live demonstrations showing concrete evidence, including error scenarios and policy gaps.

The engaging session wrapped up with an exciting prize distribution by ITU and DoT dignitaries.

The 1st prize went to Team Netaxis, RVCE Bangalore, for “Context Aware Agentic Orchestration of QoS and Adaptive Security in Resource Constrained 5G”.

The 2nd prize was presented to Team SNR, for “knowledge-grounded retrieval, deterministic constraint validation and multi-agent arbitration”.

The 3rd prize went to team Agentnet for “TeleAgent: Collaborative Multi Agent Framework Using a Fine Tuned Small Language model for Automated Private 5G Network Troubleshooting”.

A special women’s prize was awarded to team Orbitflow (SNU Chennai) & team Handshake protocol for “Predictive Traffic-aware Beam Hopping for LEO Non-Terrestrial Networks” and “Law-aware AI agents for 5G emergency response”.

Lastly, the judges’ prize was presented to team Nethealers for “Autonomous Self-Healing 5G Radio Access Network Agent with Foundation-Model Diagnosis and Digital-Twin Pre-Validation”.

Build-a-thon 5.0 demonstrates India’s strong potential to lead in AI solutions for the telecommunications domain and in the policy design that governs them.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Releases ‘Dancing with Joy’, an Inspirational Memoir by Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant
Awareness, Early Detection and Timely Treatment Are Key to Saving Lives from Cancer: Vice-President
Expansion of Cancer Care Facilities Is Bringing Specialised Treatment Closer to Patients: Vice-President
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released Dancing with Joy, an inspirational memoir by renowned classical dancer, author and former Indian Railway Traffic Service officer Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant, at Uprashtrapathi Bhavan.

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described the book as much more than a story about dance and joy, calling it a powerful account of passion, hard work, resilience and the extraordinary strength that comes from discovering and nurturing one’s talent.

Highlighting the book’s account of Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant’s journey through cancer, the Vice-President said that it was not merely a book about cancer, but a story of life beyond cancer. He observed that a deeply nurtured passion could become an anchor during life’s most difficult moments and help transform adversity into an opportunity for self-discovery.

Referring to the book’s message that the ‘D’ in DANCER helped its author overcome the ‘C’ in cancer, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that dance, nurtured through years of discipline, learning and dedication, had become Dr. Ananda’s core strength in confronting one of life’s greatest challenges.

The Vice-President highlighted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Bharat is strengthening preventive healthcare, awareness and early screening through initiatives such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases. He noted that the expansion of cancer care facilities across States was bringing specialised treatment closer to patients, with over 700 District Clinics and 500 Day Care Cancer Centres established, and 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres approved for operationalisation. He also highlighted the ₹5 lakh annual health coverage for eligible families under Ayushman Bharat and the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in February 2026, which aims to protect approximately 1.2 crore young girls against cervical cancer, with over 50 lakh girls already vaccinated.

Drawing lessons from Dr. Ananda’s experience, the Vice-President said that success and failure were two sides of the same coin and that every setback offered an opportunity to learn, reflect and return with renewed determination. He urged people facing cancer and other serious challenges not to lose hope, emphasising the importance of courage and a positive mindset.He emphasised that awareness, early detection and timely treatment could save lives.

The Vice-President also acknowledged the vital role played by families and volunteers in supporting cancer patients. He observed that families provided essential emotional strength, encouragement and care during the most difficult phases of a patient’s life, often making considerable personal and financial sacrifices.

The Vice-President said that talent, while a gift, could be transformed into excellence only through sustained learning, practice and commitment. He observed that passion was not a luxury but a source of strength, and that the abilities and interests nurtured during ordinary times could become invaluable resources when extraordinary challenges arose.

Congratulating Dr. Ananda Shankar Jayant on the publication, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan expressed the hope that 'Dancing with Joy' would inspire young people to discover and develop their talents, touch countless lives and remind readers that, whatever rhythm life offered, it was possible to meet it with courage, grace and joy.

Chairman, Sangeet Natak Akademi, Dr. Sandhya Purecha; Chairman, Ushalakshmi Breast Cancer Foundation, Dr. P. Raghu Ram; and Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion. Doctors, cancer specialists and cancer survivors also attended the event.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Education: A Pathway to Opportunity and Empowerment
Ajay Kumar Ahirwar’s Journey Through the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely financial assistance help students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds pursue higher education and research.

Ajay Kumar Ahirwar’s journey reflects the importance of fellowship support in reducing financial barriers and enabling continued academic and professional development.

Ajay Kumar Ahirwar, a 37-year-old Scheduled Caste beneficiary, is working as a Guest Faculty member while pursuing his academic and research aspirations. Coming from a financially constrained family background, he faced difficulties in managing educational expenses, study materials, fieldwork, research-related requirements and daily living costs. Balancing his academic responsibilities with his professional commitments as a Guest Faculty member also presented challenges. Despite these constraints, he remained committed to higher education and research.

The National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) provided crucial financial assistance to Shri Ahirwar, helping him continue his higher education and research without major financial interruptions. Under the scheme, he receives fellowship assistance of ₹31,000 per month, which supports his educational and research-related expenses and essential living costs.

The fellowship has helped reduce the financial pressure associated with higher education and enabled Shri Ahirwar to devote greater attention to his academic responsibilities and research activities. The support has also helped him balance his professional commitments with his continued academic pursuits.

At present, Shri Ajay Kumar Ahirwar is working as a Guest Faculty member and remains engaged in academic and research activities. The fellowship has contributed to improved financial stability and supported the continuity of his educational journey. His experience demonstrates how targeted financial assistance can help students from disadvantaged backgrounds pursue research and work towards their professional aspirations.

Shri Ahirwar’s journey highlights the role of the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students in promoting educational empowerment and supporting research. By easing financial constraints, the scheme helps eligible students pursue higher education and build opportunities for academic and professional advancement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
The Flight of Courage, the Identity of Self-Reliance
Alappuzha Kerala’s Sunithamol’s Journey Towards Financial Independence
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely financial assistance and opportunities for entrepreneurship can help women overcome economic challenges and build independent livelihoods.

Smt Sunithamol P.S.’s journey from a decade of unemployment to running a successful bakery reflects the transformative potential of livelihood support.

Smt Sunithamol P.S., a resident of Mararikulam in Alappuzha district, Kerala, had completed her education up to the 12th standard. While raising her two children and managing household responsibilities, she remained unemployed for nearly ten years. Despite these responsibilities, she continued to aspire to become financially independent and contribute to her family’s well-being.

In 2023, Smt Sunithamol received a loan of Rs 2.85 lakh under the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC)’s Mahila Aajeevika Yojana (MAY), through the Kerala State Women’s Development Corporation (KSWDC). She used the financial assistance to purchase the necessary materials for a bakery and rented a shop in her town, turning her entrepreneurial ambition into reality.

With dedication and hard work, Mrs. Sunithamol built her bakery into a successful business. The venture gradually became a reliable source of income, allowing her to manage her responsibilities while pursuing her goal of self-reliance.

Today, after meeting her loan repayment obligations, Smt Sunithamol earns approximately Rs 20,000 per month from her bakery. Her business has strengthened her financial independence and enabled her to contribute meaningfully to her family’s livelihood. Her progress demonstrates how access to credit, combined with determination and enterprise, can open new opportunities for women.

Smt Sunithamol’s experience highlights the role of targeted financial assistance in supporting women’s entrepreneurship and economic empowerment. Through the NSFDC Mahila Aajeevika Yojana, she has transformed a long period of unemployment into a journey of confidence, enterprise and self-reliance.

The journey of Ranjit Das (name changed), a 31-year-old resident of Nagaon district, Assam, reflects the importance of comprehensive de-addiction services in promoting recovery, restoring…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Recovery to Self-Reliance – A Journey Towards a Healthier Life
Nagaon Assam’s Ranjit Das’s Journey Towards Recovery and Financial Independence
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely counselling, rehabilitation and psychological support can help individuals overcome substance-related challenges and rebuild their lives.

The journey of Ranjit Das (name changed), a 31-year-old resident of Nagaon district, Assam, reflects the importance of comprehensive de-addiction services in promoting recovery, restoring confidence and enabling individuals to move towards self-reliance and a dignified life.

Ranjit Das, belonging to the Scheduled Caste community, had studied up to the high school level and faced several socio-economic challenges. Financial difficulties, limited educational opportunities, unemployment and a lack of vocational training affected his ability to secure a stable livelihood. Limited access to healthcare and counselling services, coupled with social stigma, low self-confidence and inadequate awareness of available support systems, further compounded his difficulties.

Despite the challenges, he aspired to recover, become self-dependent, support his family financially and lead a healthy and socially fulfilling life. Although his family remained supportive, financial constraints and a lack of guidance made it difficult to access appropriate assistance.

On 3 March 2026, Ranjit received support from the District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC), Nagaon, Assam. The centre provided comprehensive assistance focused on his recovery, psychological wellbeing and rehabilitation. The support included counselling services, medical referrals, psychological assistance, awareness sessions and life-skills education. Family counselling and regular follow-up services helped strengthen the support system essential for sustaining recovery. Emotional support and motivational counselling further encouraged him to regain confidence and work towards a healthier and more independent future.

With continued support and determination, Ranjit successfully recovered and regained his confidence. He is now self-employed and earns at least ₹10,000 per month. This improvement in income has contributed to greater financial stability for his family and enabled him to move towards his goal of self-reliance. His progress reflects how appropriate counselling, rehabilitation, family participation and continued encouragement can help individuals overcome challenges and rebuild their lives.

Ranjit Das’s journey highlights the important role played by District De-Addiction Centres in facilitating recovery, strengthening self-confidence and promoting the social and economic reintegration of individuals affected by substance use. Through comprehensive support and continued follow-up, he has made meaningful progress towards a healthier life, a stable livelihood and greater financial independence. His experience demonstrates how access to institutional support, combined with personal determination and family encouragement, can help individuals move towards dignity, wellbeing and a more secure future.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
29 Nursing Cadets Commissioned as Lieutenants into Military Nursing Service at Army Hospital (R&R) Delhi
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi

29 nursing cadets of Batch IX of the College of Nursing, Army Hospital (Research & Referral) , Delhi Cantonment, were formally commissioned as Lieutenants into the Military Nursing Service (MNS) at the commissioning ceremony held at Army Hospital (R&R) on October 14, 2026. Commandant, Army Hospital (R&R), Lieutenant General Avinash Das reviewed the parade. 

In his address, Lt Gen Das congratulated the meritorious cadets who were felicitated during the ceremony for their outstanding performance and academic achievements and urged all the newly commissioned Nursing Officers to render exemplary service to serving personnel and their families, while upholding the rich ethos, values, culture and glorious traditions of the MNS. He also commended the Military Nursing Service for its 101 years of dedicated, compassionate and selfless service to the nation.

       

The newly commissioned officers successfully completed four years of rigorous training and intensive academic instruction. Following the conferment of their ranks, the officers took a solemn oath to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct and place “Service Before Self” in the discharge of their duties. The ceremony was attended by senior military officers, nursing officers, faculty members, and the proud parents and relatives of the newly commissioned officers.

item.title: Central Government approves India’s accession to Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA)
item.category: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
item.description: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Central Government approves India’s accession to Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA) Accession to strengthen India’s presence in High Seas fisheries, expand access to high-value marine resources and enhance participation in global fisheries governance Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi Central Government has approved India’s accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA) , representing a strategic milestone that reinforces India’s position in global fisheries governance.…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Central Government approves India’s accession to Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA)
Accession to strengthen India’s presence in High Seas fisheries, expand access to high-value marine resources and enhance participation in global fisheries governance
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi

Central Government has approved India’s accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA), representing a strategic milestone that reinforces India’s position in global fisheries governance. Subsequent to Guidelines for High Sea Fisheries issued in December, 2025 by Government of India, this initiative would provide a regional framework to expand India’s fishing fleet into international waters. Consequently, India will be positioned to safeguard its strategic interests, broaden economic opportunities, and establish legitimate rights for the sustainable harvesting of high-value marine resources under the SIOFA framework. Furthermore, it affirms a recognized presence on the high seas and advances India’s Blue Economy in alignment with national economic, scientific, and strategic priorities.

With India’s accession to SIOFA, Indian-flagged fishing vessels and enterprises will be able to undertake authorised fishing of squids, toothfish, alfonsino, and other non-migratory fish stocks within SIOFA's jurisdiction.

Accession to SIOFA will further enable India to collaborate with other Cooperating Parties to advance the objectives of the Agreement, namely, scientific understanding and sustainable harvest of High Seas resources, participation in the scientific assessments of the resources covered under the Agreement, and prevention of illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing.

Accession will also advance India's strategic regional priorities and strengthen national coastal security through active involvement in the High Seas Boarding and Inspection (HSBI) Scheme, which has been adopted and is set to be implemented under the SIOFA.

Currently, India, as a Cooperating Non-Contracting Party (CNCP) to the SIOFA, has limited participation in decision-making, including in key bodies such as the Scientific Committee and the Compliance Committee. Accession as a Contracting Party would enable India to participate fully in these bodies and provide access to scientific data, research programmes, and stock assessments. It will open up new fishing opportunities for the Indian fishers and entrepreneurs. India's active contribution to sustainable fishing practices in the SIOFA region will also play a key role in preserving marine resources, ensuring their long-term viability and supporting the livelihoods of Indian fishing communities.

Backgrounder:

The High Seas constitute approximately 65% of the global ocean and are currently dominated by five countries/regions: China (21%), Taiwan (13%), Japan (11%), South Korea (11%), and Spain (8%). There are two major Regional Fisheries Management Organizations (RFMOs) in the Indian Ocean, viz. the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC) and the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA). India has been a Contracting Party to the IOTC since 1996, which regulates highly migratory tuna and tuna-like species.  

India has been a cooperating non-Contracting Party (CNCP) of SIOFA, since 2022. With this membership, India secures legitimate fishing rights, access to marine resources in the High Seas under the SIOFA’s area of competence, and the opportunity to establish a recognized presence alongside existing global fleets. This Agreement covers fishery resources including fish, molluscs, crustaceans, and other sedentary species within the area, but excludes highly migratory species (Annex I of UNCLOS) and the sedentary species which are subject to the fishery jurisdiction of coastal states (Article 77(4) of UNCLOS).

Indian fishing vessels currently operate largely within 60–80 NM of the EEZ, and India needs to develop and expand its fishing capacity across all possible High Seas areas, including through access agreements in other countries' EEZs, thereby contributing to the national exchequer.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Swachhata Se Sabhyata Session Held At Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
Swachhata Campaign 6.0 Focusses on Cleanliness, Inner Values and Jan Bhagidari
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, organized a special awareness session titled Swachhata se Sabhyata in collaboration with the Brahma Kumaris at the Ministry, in the National Capital here.

The session was held as part of the Swachhata Campaign 6.0 observed across the country with its focus on Jan Bhagidari.

Addressing officers and staff, Sister Vidarthi of the Brahma Kumaris spoke about the connection between inner values and the cleanliness of one’s surroundings.

 

Citing the principle Jaisi Awastha, Waisi Vyavastha, she explained that a person’s state of mind shapes the order they create around them, whether at home, in the workplace or in the wider community.

 

Referring to the maxim Cleanliness is next to Godliness, Sister Vidarthi encouraged participants to regard cleanliness as a practice rooted in self-respect and inner purity, alongside their civic responsibilities.

She emphasised respect for nature, social sensitivity and simple living, and observed that lasting physical cleanliness is supported by cleanliness in thought, speech and conduct.

Sister Vidarthi also highlighted recycling as a practical habit that promotes responsible use of resources and contributes to better waste management.

At the conclusion of the session, officers and staff of the Department reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining cleanliness in their workplaces and communities throughout the year.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Strategic Restructuring of IDBI Bank Ltd.
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

Q1.  Who is the Strategic Buyer for the IDBI Bank Ltd.?

Answer: M/s 10955230 Canada Inc. (parent entity M/s Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.) has been approved as the Strategic Buyer for the IDBI Bank Ltd.

Q2.  What is the size of this Transaction?

Answer: The purchase consideration for this transaction is Rs.52,878.0806181 Crores (in words Rupees Fifty-Two Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy-Eight Crore Eight Lakh Six Thousand and One Hundred Eighty-One only).

Q3.  How will it be split between the Government of India (GoI) and the Life Insurance corporation of India (LIC)?

Answer: 60.72% stake out of the total shareholding of the IDBI Bank Ltd is being sold through this transaction, comprising 30.48% shareholding held by the Gol and 30.24% shareholding held by the LIC. The proceeds will be divided in the same proportion.

Q4.  How many entities were involved in the bidding process?

Answer: Of the five parties who initially submitted their Expression of interest, four parties qualified as per the eligibility criteria and disqualification conditions prescribed in the Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM), of which, two finally submitted their techno- financial bids and became Qualified Bidders (QBs) for this transaction.

Q5.  What methodologies were used for the valuation of IDBI Bank Ltd.?

Answer: The fair value of the enterprise was determined using two alternate methodologies, namely the Market Multiple Method and the Asset Valuation Method.

Q6.  Who carried out the valuation exercise?

Answer: The valuation of enterprise was carried out by two independent, professional valuation agencies appointed for the purpose. Their names cannot be disclosed due to confidential guarantees enshrined in the process.

Q7.  What role did the stock market price play in the valuation of the IDBI Bank?

Answer: The volatile stock market price of the narrowly traded IDBI stock fluctuated both above and below the bid offer price (low high range of Rs.61.01 to Rs.118.38 over the valuation period). It was disregarded, as it tended to misalign the valuation with the intrinsic value of the enterprise, and instead, relative valuation by the market multiple method, which overcomes this problem, was used to determine the fair market value of the enterprise based on the 31st March, 2026 closing accounts for all public sector banks.

Q8.  How have the assets, including land and properties, been valued for the IDBI Bank?

Answers: The Asset Valuation Method, which considered both tangible and intangible assets, including land and properties, along with the liabilities, was used to determine the fair net asset value of the enterprise as per the 31st March, 2026 audited accounts of the IDBI Bank.

Q9.  What was the benchmark price used for this transaction?

Answer: The average of the two independent valuations (Rs.75.99 per share) served as the benchmark price for the evaluation of the qualified bids. The winning bid was found to be higher than the benchmark price as well as the fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies.

Q10.  How was the benchmark price determined?

Answer: The benchmark price was the average of the fair market value determined by the Market Multiple Method and the fair net asset value determined by the Asset Valuation Method.

Q11.  What is the further course of action?

Answer: The Successful Bidder would now present its credentials to the RBI in accordance with the ‘Fit & Proper’ assessment conducted at the EoI stage and submit a roadmap for the compliance of regulatory conditions prescribed therein.

Q12.    What is the residual equity stake left with the GoI and the LIC?

Answer: GoI will retain 15% residual equity stake while the LIC will retain 19% equity stake. Both of them will withdraw their nominees from the Board and become public shareholders.

Q13.    How will the GoI and LIC dissolve their residual shareholding in the IDBI Bank?

Answer: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has delegated powers to the Alternative Mechanism to undertake minority stake sales of the residual GoI shareholding through the open market in accordance with the standard operating procedure. The LIC will be free to manage its residual shareholding in accordance with its internal procedures while ensuring compliance with the direction of its regulators.

Q14.    What impact will it have on the banking sector and the economy at large?

Answer: It will have a significantly positive effect on the banking and financial sector of our economy. The IDBI Bank, post-privatization, would be able to generate funds without any dependence on government assistance as has been the experience in the past. It is expected that the strategic buyer will infuse private capital, bring-in new technology and better management practices, which will help enhance its business potential and make it more competitive for both credit and deposit growth.

Q15. What impact will it have on India’s external sector at the time of geo-political strain?

Answer: It will be the largest FDI in the financial sector of our economy so far, and will help generate a positive sentiment for economic reforms, while improving the investment climate in the country at large.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR to Organise Curtain-Raiser and Media Interaction Ahead of ESTIC-2026
Dr. M. L. Jat to Address ICAR’s Role in ESTIC-2026 at Curtain-Raiser Event in Karnal, Haryana
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 1:01PM by PIB Delhi

 

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) will organise a curtain-raiser event and media interaction on 15th October 2026 at the ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, Haryana, ahead of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC)-2026, scheduled to be held from 27 to 29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan, New Delhi.

Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), will address the curtain-raiser event of ESTIC-2026 and speak on ICAR in ESTIC-2026.

The programme will feature a media interaction on Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition, providing a platform for discussions on emerging developments in agricultural technology, food systems and nutrition.   

ICAR in ESTIC 2026

Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), is a member of the Steering Committee of ESTIC-2026, alongside the heads of several major scientific and technology departments of the Government of India. ICAR is directly associated with the thematic session on “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition,” one of the 12 major thematic sessions of ESTIC-2026, scheduled for 29th October 2026. The session will be chaired by the Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, and the Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI). It will feature a keynote address, presentations by a deep-tech startup CEO, a woman entrepreneur and science and technology (S&T) leaders, followed by a panel discussion. The session will provide a platform to highlight the contribution of agricultural research, innovation and emerging technologies to India's broader science and technology landscape. Several ICAR scientists, including researchers from ICAR–Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), ICAR–National Institute for Plant Biotechnology and ICAR–National Rice Research Institute, are also listed among the speakers at ESTIC-2026. ICAR's participation will highlight advances in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, digital agriculture, advanced crop improvement, gene editing and sustainable agricultural systems. In addition, ICAR will showcase its innovations under the theme “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition” at the ESTIC-2026 exhibition.

ESTIC-2026

ESTIC-2026 is a flagship platform for science, technology and innovation, bringing together Ministries and Departments of the Government, researchers, innovators, deep-tech start-ups, industries, policymakers, funding agencies and global experts. Organised by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, Government of India, with the National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST) as the Organising Partner, the three-day event will provide a platform for showcasing cutting-edge research, emerging technologies and deep-tech innovations and fostering collaboration in emerging and critical areas of science, technology and innovation towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Conclave will feature participation from the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), Ministry of Ayush, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Defence/DRDO, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), ICAR, Department of Health Research (DHR)/Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Space/ISRO, and Department of Telecommunications (DoT), along with Nobel Laureates, global experts, industry leaders, policymakers and emerging science & technology leaders, researchers, innovators, deep-tech start-ups, industries, funding agencies, policymakers and global experts.

ICAR’s participation in ESTIC-2026 will contribute to strengthening collaborative efforts towards sustainable and technology-driven agricultural and food systems in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB signs agreement with ideaForge for ₹151 crore RDI support to develop YETI heavy-lift autonomous aerial logistics vehicle
Indigenous VTOL platform designed to transport payloads of up to 200 kg, with a targeted range of 200 km, to advance towards TRL-9
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 12:50PM by PIB Delhi

Strengthening India's capabilities in autonomous aerial systems and next-generation logistics, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with ideaForge Technology Limited, Mumbai, Maharashtra for financial support of ₹151 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

The project, with a total project cost of ₹302 crore, focuses on the development of YETI, a heavy-lift, long-range autonomous aerial logistics vehicle, with the objective of advancing the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9. The financial support will be provided through debt financing.

Designed for demanding operating environments, YETI is an autonomous vertical take-off and landing, fixed-wing hybrid unmanned aerial vehicle (VTOL-FW UAV) intended to transport heavy payloads over long distances. Its proposed capabilities are aimed at addressing logistics requirements in areas where conventional transportation can be difficult, time-consuming or operationally constrained. The platform is designed to carry payloads of up to 200 kg, with a targeted range of up to 200 km and an operating altitude of up to 6,500 metres above mean sea level. Its weather-resistant design is intended to support operations in challenging environments, including high-altitude regions, deserts and marine conditions.

A key feature of YETI is its ability to take off and land vertically while retaining a fixed-wing configuration for longer-range operations. The vehicle is designed to operate from relatively small, unprepared landing areas measuring approximately 15 metres × 15 metres, enabling deployment in locations with limited ground infrastructure.The platform incorporates distributed and redundant propulsion and power architecture to improve fault tolerance. Its proposed capabilities also include GNSS-denied navigation, a communication link of up to 200 km, swarm operations and containerised transportation for rapid deployment. The design is intended to enable the vehicle to be transported and set up quickly, supporting logistics missions across geographically challenging locations.

The development of heavy-lift autonomous aerial platforms has growing relevance for applications requiring the movement of essential supplies across difficult terrain. By combining vertical take-off and landing with long-range flight capability and substantial payload capacity, YETI is being developed to address a distinct segment of the unmanned aviation and aerial logistics market.

The RDI-supported programme will facilitate further technology development, engineering, integration, testing and validation required to progress the platform towards TRL-9, subject to the applicable technical, safety and regulatory requirements. The project falls under the Deep Technology sector, with Intelligent Systems and Robotics as the sub-sector. It reflects the growing importance of indigenous autonomous systems that integrate aerospace engineering, propulsion, navigation, communications and intelligent control.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “The development of advanced autonomous systems is opening new possibilities for addressing complex operational and logistical challenges. Indigenous heavy-lift aerial platforms can play an important role in improving access to remote and difficult-to-reach locations. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting technology-intensive projects that require sustained investment to progress from advanced development towards deployment. The agreement with ideaForge reflects our commitment to strengthening India's capabilities in autonomous systems, robotics and next-generation aerospace technologies.”

Speaking on this development, CEO and Co-founder of ideaForge Technology Ltd., said, “YETI represents a generational leap in what India can design, build, and operate autonomously. Our armed forces and our logistics networks face the daily reality of reaching where roads end, and weather doesn’t cooperate. YETI is our answer to that challenge, which is engineered not just to fly, but to deliver, reliably and repeatably, in the conditions that define the toughest operational environments. The government’s confidence in ideaForge through the RDI framework is a reaffirmation that Indian deeptech players are now ready to carry the weight of national capability-building.”

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
BHAVYA: Creating Investment-Ready Manufacturing Ecosystems
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 12:29PM by PIB Delhi

 

Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA) is a ₹33,660 crore initiative to develop 100 plug-and-play industrial parks across India. The parks will provide modern industrial infrastructure, reliable services, and faster approvals, reducing the time needed to set up new industries. The scheme aims to attract investment, support MSMEs, strengthen supply chains, create jobs, and drive industrial growth across regions.

 

A New Phase in Manufacturing Policy

India's manufacturing sector is undergoing structural change. It now contributes about 16–17 percent of GDP and employs over 27 million workers. The National Manufacturing Mission aims to raise this share to 25 percent by 2035. The composition of industries is also changing, with medium- and high-technology industries accounting for 46.3% of manufacturing value addition. This reflects a shift towards higher-value and technology-intensive manufacturing.

As industries grow, they need reliable infrastructure, efficient logistics, and predictable approvals. Global supply chains are also diversifying, making well-connected industrial locations more important.

Plug-and-play parks bring these requirements together by providing essential infrastructure and common facilities before industries begin operations. This reduces the time and cost involved in setting up new manufacturing units. To expand this approach nationwide, the Bharat Audyogik Vikas  Yojna (BHAVYA) was approved by the Cabinet in March 2026 and notified on 10 April 2026 with an outlay of ₹33,660 crore. BHAVYA is being implemented in partnership with States and private developers. The scheme emphasises increasing manufacturing capacity in the country and ease of doing business through streamlined approvals, effective single-window systems and investor-friendly reforms. The plug-and-play industrial ecosystems will reduce entry-level barriers and help industries move from investment to production quickly.

Policy Evolution: From Pre-2020 to Plug-and-Play Ecosystems

India's approach to manufacturing growth has evolved over time. Each phase has expanded the country's capacity to support industry and create new economic opportunities.

The first phase focused on industrial estates and Special Economic Zones (SEZs). These provided industrial land, common infrastructure, and regulatory incentives. As of February 2026, India had 370 notified SEZs. These zones attracted investments worth ₹7.82 lakh crore and generated employment for over 31.7 lakh people.

The approach then expanded from individual industrial zones to larger manufacturing hubs across the country. As of 14 October 2026, 4,164 industrial parks have been mapped on the India Industrial Land Bank (IILB). At the same time, the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) moved beyond providing industrial land. It combined manufacturing zones with utilities, logistics, and urban services, creating more integrated industrial locations.

Industrial nodes such as Dholera Special Investment Region (Gujarat), Shendra-Bidkin Industrial Area (Maharashtra), Vikram Udyogpuri (Madhya Pradesh), and Integrated Industrial Township Greater Noida (Uttar Pradesh) demonstrated the advantages of integrated planning.

Period

Policy Approach

What it Added

Pre-2020

Industrial estates and SEZs

Fiscal incentives; export-oriented regulatory perimeter

NICDP

Smart industrial cities with integrated infrastructure

Planned nodes, multimodal connectivity, plug-and-play pilots.

Budget 2026-27

Sector-specific plug-and-play parks (chemical parks, PM MITRA).

Cluster-based model in specific sectors.

BHAVYA (2026)

 

Nationwide rollout: 100 proposed plug-and-play parks nationwide.

Scale, coverage, and reform-linked delivery at national level

Inside the BHAVYA Framework

BHAVYA provides financial assistance of up to ₹1 crore per acre for developing industrial parks. The scheme covers essential components such as internal roads, power supply, water networks, drainage systems, common effluent treatment facilities, value-added infrastructure and Information & Communication Technology (ICT)-enabled administration. Underground utility corridors will enable a no-dig environment for efficient maintenance and uninterrupted industrial operations.

Parks will also feature ready-built factory sheds, built-to-suit units, testing and certification facilities, and warehousing. To improve worker welfare and productivity, provisions have been made for worker housing, healthcare facilities, skill development centres, and other social amenities. The scheme supports up to 25% of approved funding to be allocated for external infrastructure such as road, rail, and last-mile logistics connectivity, ensuring seamless integration with the wider transport network.

The scheme will be implemented over six years, from FY2026–27 to FY 2031–32. In the first phase, up to 50 industrial parks will be selected through a challenge mode across two selection rounds. The remaining parks will be selected in subsequent phases, taking the total number of parks supported under BHAVYA to 100. The selection will consider project readiness, land availability, and industrial potential. Each park will span 25 to 1,000 acres depending upon mandatory criteria of land sizes as per the Scheme guidelines. Projects will be implemented and managed through dedicated Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs), which will oversee development, operations, investor facilitation, and long-term maintenance.

Manufacturing firms, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, and investors can access common facilities and streamlined approvals under BHAVYA.

In June 2026, the BHAVYA Portal was launched for the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. The portal supports project submission, appraisal and evaluation while enabling a transparent and competitive selection process.

 

Plug and Play Industrial Parks: Concept and Features

Trunk infrastructure is the higher-order infrastructure development with the primary purpose of serving ‘catchment’ areas to be shared between developments, commonly provided by local governments. It includes the development of the main line of infrastructure, such as water supply, drainage, sewerage/septage, roads, streetlights, electricity, etc.

 

Plug-and-play industrial parks are pre-developed industrial ecosystems where land, trunk infrastructure, utilities, and common facilities are made available beforehand. In many cases, approvals and basic clearances are streamlined through single-window systems. This allows enterprises to move faster from financial decisions to production, while reducing upfront costs and implementation delays.

Such models are becoming more relevant as supply chains diversify across locations and manufacturing becomes more time-sensitive. Investors increasingly seek locations where land availability, connectivity, utilities, and regulatory processes are predictable.

The plug-and-play model is already gaining traction in India. In the Union Budget 2025–26, ₹2,500 crore was allocated for the development of plug-and-play industrial parks. India currently has 260 plug-and-play industrial parks, reflecting the growing adoption of infrastructure-ready manufacturing ecosystems across sectors and states.

The plug-and-play model is also being extended to sector-specific industrial facilities. In July 2026, the Government approved the BHAVYA-Rasayan Scheme for three Chemical Parks. These parks will provide common facilities and environmental safeguards for chemical manufacturing.

 

Dholera SIR: An Integrated Industrial City

Dholera, Gujarat is emerging as a new-generation industrial city. Wide roads, reliable utilities, digital networks, and modern urban services were planned from the start. Power, water, gas, and drainage systems run through a common underground network, creating a plug-and-play environment for industries.

The region is developing as a hub for advanced manufacturing sectors. Semiconductors, aerospace and defence, solar manufacturing, green hydrogen, biotechnology, and heavy engineering are among the focused sectors. Strong links to ports, airports, expressways, and the Dedicated Freight Corridor connect Dholera to domestic and global markets. Outcomes include: 

  • 495 acres allotted across 11 plots
  • Investment potential: ₹97,328 crore
  • Employment potential: 6,000+ jobs

Land has been allotted for major projects, including Tata Electronics' semiconductor facility and Renew Power solar module manufacturing plant.

 

Towards a New Manufacturing Ecosystem

India’s manufacturing landscape is evolving with greater emphasis on integrated industrial development. The shift from industrial estates to planned manufacturing hubs reflects this changing approach. BHAVYA represents the next step in this transistion. Alongside other initiatives for industrial development, it forms part of India’s broader effort to strengthen its manufacturing base and enhance its role in global manufacturing.

item.title: India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests & pursue development in peace: Raksha Mantri at 1st ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence
item.description: Ministry of Defence India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests & pursue development in peace: Raksha Mantri at 1st ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum “Need to build trust, respect each other’s sovereignty, follow international law & keep channels of dialogue open to tackle borderless challenges” Strengthening maritime domain awareness, interoperability & underwater cooperation is key to a stable, rule-based maritime order, says Shri Rajnath Singh “Self-reliance does not mean working in isolation; it can create opportunities for trusted…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests & pursue development in peace: Raksha Mantri at 1st ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum
“Need to build trust, respect each other’s sovereignty, follow international law & keep channels of dialogue open to tackle borderless challenges”
Strengthening maritime domain awareness, interoperability & underwater cooperation is key to a stable, rule-based maritime order, says Shri Rajnath Singh
“Self-reliance does not mean working in isolation; it can create opportunities for trusted partners to design, build, maintain & improve equipment together”
“Co-development, co-production, MRO, training and long-term technical support can build local skills, support industry & make supply chains more reliable”
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 11:44AM by PIB Delhi

“India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries - large and small - make their own choices, protect their interests and pursue development in peace,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh as he called for building trust, respecting each other’s sovereignty, following international law and keeping channels of dialogue open to tackle both emerging and conventional “borderless challenges”. He was addressing the maiden Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) - India Defence Think Tank Forum at Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA) in New Delhi on October 14, 2026.

Raksha Mantri asserted that India and ASEAN share a clear interest in peace, stability, prosperity and an open & inclusive Indo-Pacific. He emphasised that India’s Act East policy and the vision of SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) advocate for an open and multipolar cooperation, and the nation aligns them through ASEAN-led mechanisms that are central to its Indo-Pacific vision. He noted that the region is witnessing rapid changes in the face of growing strategic competition and pressure & uncertainty created at times through actions at sea, in addition to threats such as terrorism, cybercrime, piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing, climate-related disasters and risks to vital supply chains. No country alone can address these challenges, he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the need to discuss differences early and peacefully, before they become disputes, and pitched for a regional order where countries work together without being forced to choose sides. “India believes that security is strengthened when countries build capacity together, respect international law and maintain trust through dialogue,” he said.

Raksha Mantri highlighted the centuries-old close ties between India and Southeast Asia rooted in shared history, culture, trade & ideas, reiterating that the Act East Policy is a long-term commitment to working with the region as an equal partner. “India’s approach and ASEAN’s outlook on the Indo-Pacific can complement each other. We should strengthen cooperation, not create competition between regional forums,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh stated that keeping the Indian Ocean and the waters of Southeast Asia safe is a shared responsibility as they are part of one connected maritime space, crucial for trade, energy, people and essential goods. Strengthening maritime domain awareness, interoperability, and collaboration in underwater awareness will be key to ensuring a stable, rule-based maritime order, he said.

Raksha Mantri stressed that as 2026 has been designated as ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, it is an opportunity to turn shared interest into practical action. “We should improve the sharing of maritime information, strengthen cooperation among our navies and coast guards, and build the ability to respond together to emergencies. We should also work against piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing and other threats, in accordance with international law,” he said.

Terming defence technology as another crucial area, Shri Rajnath Singh pointed out that Artificial Intelligence, drones, cyber capabilities and space-based systems are becoming increasingly important, with recent conflicts demonstrating that relatively low-cost drones can challenge expensive defence systems. He underscored the need to respond with practical, affordable and adaptable solutions.

“India believes that innovation should not remain limited to a few large organisations. Start-ups, universities, research institutions and smaller companies can all contribute. India’s initiatives like Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) and Technology Development Fund (TDF) have created a way to collaborate with innovators for our defence needs,” stated Raksha Mantri as he called for exploring ways for innovators to work together on clearly defined problems, such as counter-drone systems, cyber defence, maritime surveillance and disaster response.

Shri Rajnath Singh called for joint research projects, shared testing opportunities, exchanges among young researchers and carefully designed innovation challenges, emphasising that such cooperation must also protect sensitive information, respect intellectual property and ensure that technology is shared responsibly. “The aim should be to develop useful capabilities while strengthening trust between our countries,” he said.

On defence industrial cooperation, Raksha Mantri asserted that India is ready to explore cooperation with ASEAN partners in areas such as patrol vessels, radars, air-defence systems, helicopters, drones and other technologies, according to each country’s needs and priorities. He said the ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ initiative focuses on building stronger domestic capabilities, but self-reliance does not mean working in isolation. It can create opportunities for trusted partners to design, build, maintain and improve equipment together, he said.

Underlining the importance of co-development, co-production, maintenance, repair and overhaul, training and long-term technical support, Shri Rajnath Singh said these arrangements can build local skills, support industry and make supply chains more reliable.  “Our researchers need to look closely at what makes such partnerships work: clear requirements, reliable after-sales support, appropriate technology safeguards, fair sharing of responsibilities and benefits, and opportunities for local companies and skilled workers. Our goal should be lasting partnerships, not one-time transactions,” he said.

Calling for enhanced cooperation to deal with natural disasters, Raksha Mantri stated that Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) should be a regular part of defence dialogue as cyclones, floods, rising sea levels and extreme weather can damage ports, disrupt trade and threaten lives and livelihoods. “We can learn from one another, share best practices and improve coordination before a crisis occurs,” he said.

On the crucial role of Think Tanks, Shri Rajnath Singh said Governments need good analysis, but they also need ideas that can be put into practice. He suggested some practical outcomes from the forum, including development of a joint India-ASEAN research agenda on maritime security, cyber threats, emerging technologies, disaster response and defence-industry cooperation; regular exchanges among researchers, including young scholars, through fellowships, visiting programmes and joint publications; Identification of a small number of pilot projects such as a tabletop exercise on maritime disaster response, a joint study on counter-drone solutions, or a research project on secure maritime information sharing; Promotion of Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues for researchers, practitioners and policymakers to continue their discussions between formal meetings; and preparing a concise set of recommendations, identifying institutions that could take them forward, and reviewing progress at a future meeting.

In his welcome address, Director General, MP-IDSA Amb Sujan R Chinoy expressed gratitude to Raksha Mantri for his vision and support in strengthening India’s defence and security partnerships with ASEAN. Welcoming participants from all eleven ASEAN member states and India, he described the forum as an important institutional milestone in the evolution of ASEAN-India defence engagement. He expressed confidence that the forum would institutionalise enduring dialogue between India and ASEAN’s strategic communities and help identify practical areas for deeper defence and security cooperation.

About ASEAN - India Defence Think Tank Forum

Being held on October 14 & 15, 2026, the forum aims to strengthen strategic dialogue, promote joint analysis and identify practical avenues for enhanced defence and security cooperation between India and ASEAN. The initiative follows the announcement made by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh during the second ASEAN-India Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Kuala Lumpur on October 31, 2025, on the sidelines of the 12th ADMM-Plus.

Across a two-day programme, the forum will deliberate on strategic stability, regional geopolitics, maritime security, grey-zone challenges, HADR, maritime domain awareness, defence technology, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, space, unmanned systems, defence industry collaboration and resilient supply chains. The discussions are expected to contribute to a stronger and more forward-looking ASEAN-India defence partnership.

Prime Minister shares article on moving governance from welfare to empowerment
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has shared an article written by Union Minister, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia.

The article highlights how India’s approach to governance is moving from welfare to empowerment, enabling citizens to become active participants in the development process. It notes that initiatives spanning sanitation, gas connections, healthcare and access to credit focus on last-mile delivery and creating opportunities for people to improve their lives. This approach is central to the vision of a Viksit and Sashakt Bharat by 2047.

The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X;

“Union Minister Shri @JM_Scindia writes that India's approach to governance is shifting from welfare to empowerment. It is enabling citizens to become active participants in the development process.

From sanitation and gas connections to healthcare and access to credit, the focus is on last-mile delivery and creating opportunities for people to improve their lives. This approach is central to the vision of a Viksit and Sashakt Bharat by 2047.”

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
item.description: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises India’s Coir Sector: Creating Livelihoods, Promoting Entrepreneurship and Driving Sustainable Growth Over 21,000 coir units are registered on the Udyam registration portal, generating employment for 2.3 lakh people Exports of coir products witnessed an increase of 305% in the last 10 years Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 10:09AM by PIB Delhi India, the world’s largest producer and exporter of coir, is rooted in tradition and driven by innovation. The coir sector is emerging as a vibrant, eco-friendly and sustainable driver of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
India’s Coir Sector: Creating Livelihoods, Promoting Entrepreneurship and Driving Sustainable Growth
Over 21,000 coir units are registered on the Udyam registration portal, generating employment for 2.3 lakh people
Exports of coir products witnessed an increase of 305% in the last 10 years
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 10:09AM by PIB Delhi

India, the world’s largest producer and exporter of coir, is rooted in tradition and driven by innovation. The coir sector is emerging as a vibrant, eco-friendly and sustainable driver of economic and social progress.  It not only promotes the productive use of coconut husks but also generates livelihoods and supports the growth of rural and traditional communities. With its strong focus on sustainability, value addition and inclusive growth, the Coir sector is playing a crucial role in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. 

Made from coir, eco-friendly and sustainable products like mats, mattresses, ropes, brushes and other utility items are increasingly becoming a part of our everyday lives. But what exactly is coir?

Coir is a natural, fibrous material extracted from the outer, tough husk of coconuts. These natural fibres are processed and transformed into a wide range of commercial products. The Coir Sector, one of India’s oldest and traditional industries, represents an eco-friendly manufacturing sector that extracts, processes and converts coconut husk fibres into value-added products.

Coir sector in India:-

  • India is the world’s largest producer and exporter of coir and coir products, accounting for about two-thirds of global production. The Indian Coir Industry has a turnover of approximately ₹16,000 crore and contributes close to 1% to India’s GDP.

  • In FY 2025-26, India’s exports of coir and coir products were valued at ₹6,614.40 crore, with the US, China, Netherlands, Spain and the UK being the major export destinations. Coir pith, fibre, yarn and tufted mats are the major coir products exported by India.

  • The Indian Coir Sector has more than 21,000 coir units and provides direct and indirect employment to over 7 lakh workers, with 80% being women from rural households.

  • The Ministry of MSME runs a central sector scheme, “Coir Vikas Yojana (CVY)”, aimed at promoting the sustainable development and growth of the Coir Sector and providing support to coir artisans and the coir industry.

  • The CVY focuses on:

    • Development of new technologies, machines & products for Coir Industry.

    • Conducting skill training and promotional programmes

    • Promotion of sales of coir and coir products in domestic as well as international markets.

    • Creating awareness through publicity activities and participation in trade fairs, expos, etc.

    • Providing financial assistance to promote sales.

    • Facilitating the participation of coir exporters in international exhibitions.

    • Compiling and publishing statistics on the coir sector.

Key achievements during last 12 years (since 2014-15):
 

  • More than 21,000 coir units are registered on the Udyam registration portal employing 2.3 lakh persons making them a part of the formal MSME policy ecosystem.

  • Export of coir and coir products has more than quadrupled, from ₹1,630.33 crore in FY 2014-15 to ₹6,614.40 crore in FY 2025-26, registering an increase of 305.70%. 

  • Over 68,000 persons have been trained under various training programmes with more than 80% being women.

  • More than 150 innovative machines, technologies and value-added coir products in the coir sector.

  • Facilitated participation of more than 1,000 exporters in International Exhibitions abroad and financial assistance of more than ₹20 crores given to more than 850 entrepreneurs under Export Market Promotion.

  • 1,400+ promotional programmes organised and 950+ exhibitions participated across India.

Coir Giving Wings to Dreams: Inspiring Stories of Enterprise & Success

    

    1. Smt. Ranjana Ramchandra Kadam, from Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra, turned her entrepreneurial dream into reality under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), which enabled her to establish a coir unit with guidance from the Coir Board. She constructed a shed and procured the necessary machinery and equipment to start her business, with significant support from the Coir Board office. Her factory currently manufactures coir ropes, pillows and doormats. Through this venture, she has provided full-time employment to six people.

 

 

    1.  Sampoorna Plus Agro Fertilizer Enterprises, Kozhikode, Kerala, under Shri Surendran P., was strengthened through the training and technical guidance provided by the Coir Board, Sub-Regional Office, Kannur and the Central Coir Research Institute (CCRI), Kalavoor. He actively participated in hands-on training programmes, demonstrations, and awareness sessions on the production and effective utilisation of coir pith bio-fertiliser. Within a short period of one year, his enterprise has successfully built a customer base of more than 500 customers. The unit has also recorded impressive sales of more than 20 tonnes of coir pith bio-fertiliser. The enterprise currently provides employment to 5 workers, including 2 women workers.   

       

3.   Smt. Allam Gowthamy from East Godavari District, Andhra Pradesh, five years ago underwent training at the Coir Board Training Centre. Motivated by the technical guidance she established her own enterprise, Adigo Coir Products. She availed financial assistance under the PMEGP. Today, the unit has achieved an annual turnover of approximately ₹35 lakh and generates an annual profit of around ₹10 lakh. The enterprise has also created employment for six women. She also actively conducting training programmes with the support of the Coir Board Regional Office, Rajahmundry and Mandal Parishat authorities, and nearly 120 women have been trained in coir mat weaving, rope making and handicraft production.

 

       

4.  Shri G. Sabu, from Alappuzha, Kerala, has started the Coir spinning unit in the year 2024 under the PMEGP scheme and through Coir Board Regional Office, Kalavoor. Within two years of operation, the unit achieved steady production of coir yarn and rope supplied to local coir societies and manufacturers in Alappuzha. The enterprise generated direct employment for 8–10 local workers, predominantly women from nearby villages. The monthly turnover increased substantially, providing the entrepreneur with a stable income and creating regular wages for employees.

***

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister expresses grief over loss of lives in boat capsizing incident in Vaishali, Bihar
PM announces ex-gratia
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 11:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has expressed deep anguish over the loss of lives in a boat capsizing incident in Vaishali, Bihar.

The Prime Minister conveyed his thoughts to the bereaved families in this difficult time and prayed for the speedy recovery of all those injured. He also stated that the local administration is assisting those affected.

The Prime Minister announced that an ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund (PMNRF) would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000.

The Prime Minister’s Office said in a X post;

“The loss of lives in the boat capsizing incident in Vaishali, Bihar, is deeply painful. My thoughts are with the bereaved families in this difficult time. I pray for the speedy recovery of all those injured. The local administration is assisting those affected.

An ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000: PM @narendramodi”
