Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister welcomes Bloomberg’s plans to expand presence in India
Mike Bloomberg acknowledges India’s Economic Growth and rise to Global Leadership
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 10:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has welcomed Bloomberg’s plans to expand its presence in India and deepen its engagement with the country’s economy, markets and people.

In a post on X, Mike Bloomberg described Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi as “India’s longest serving elected Prime Minister for consecutive terms” and acknowledged India’s rapid economic growth and rise to global leadership. He also referred to the Prime Minister’s vision for India’s future and expressed pleasure at discussing Bloomberg’s 30th year in India and its plans to expand in the country.

Responding to Mike Bloomberg’s post on X, the Prime Minister, Shri Modi said it was a delight meeting him and congratulated Bloomberg on completing 30 years in India.

Shri Modi welcomed Bloomberg’s plans to expand its presence in India and deepen its engagement with the country’s economy, markets and people. He also highlighted the immense opportunities being created across sectors by India’s growth story.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

“It was a delight meeting you this morning. 

Congratulations to Bloomberg on completing 30 years in India. We welcome Bloomberg's plans to expand its presence in India and deepen its engagement with our economy, markets and people.

India’s growth story continues to create immense opportunities across sectors.”

 

It was a delight meeting you this morning. Congratulations to Bloomberg on completing 30 years in India. We welcome Bloomberg's plans to expand its presence in India and deepen its engagement with our economy, markets and people. India’s growth story continues to create immense opportunities across sectors.

item.title: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Inaugurates North East Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 in Mizoram, Calls for Greater Credit Flow to Region
item.category: Ministry of Development of North-East Region
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Development of North-East Region
item.description: Ministry of Development of North-East Region Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Inaugurates North East Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 in Mizoram, Calls for Greater Credit Flow to Region Northeast Among the Most Promising Markets for Bankers, Says Scindia Northeast Economy Growing at 9–11% Annually, ₹40,000 Crore in Investments Grounded Across Eight States Banking Touchpoints Cover 99.93% of Villages, 131 New Bank Branches and 126 ATMs Added Scindia Calls for State-Wise Credit-Deposit Ratio Targets and Northeast-Specific Credit Framework Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 10:04PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region
Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Inaugurates North East Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 in Mizoram, Calls for Greater Credit Flow to Region
Northeast Among the Most Promising Markets for Bankers, Says Scindia
Northeast Economy Growing at 9–11% Annually, ₹40,000 Crore in Investments Grounded Across Eight States
Banking Touchpoints Cover 99.93% of Villages, 131 New Bank Branches and 126 ATMs Added
Scindia Calls for State-Wise Credit-Deposit Ratio Targets and Northeast-Specific Credit Framework
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today inaugurated the North East Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 at Mizoram University in Aizawl. The conclave focused on expanding banking access, strengthening financial inclusion and accelerating economic growth across the Northeast.

Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma, State Minister Prof. Lalnilawma, MDoNER Secretary Srinivas Katikithala, Chief Secretary Khilli Ram Meena and NEC Secretary Satinder Kumar Bhalla attended the event. Representatives from the RBI, SBI, Punjab National Bank, Central Bank of India, UCO Bank, Bank of Baroda, Indian Overseas Bank, Indian Bank, India Post Payments Bank, Canara Bank, Punjab & Sind Bank and IDBI Bank participated. Development institutions, including NABARD, SIDBI, DFS, NEDFi, NERAMAC and NECBDC, were also represented.

Addressing the North East Bankers’ Conclave, Shri Scindia urged banks to focus on three priorities: expanding physical banking infrastructure, improving credit access through state-wise Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio targets, and supporting MSMEs and infrastructure development.

Describing the Northeast as one of the most promising banking markets in India and globally, Union minister Scindia highlighted the region’s annual economic growth of 9–11%. Expressing his personal connection with the Northeast, he urged bankers to explore its growing opportunities and ensure that the economic value generated in the region remains within the region.

Greater Credit Flow to Drive Economic Growth

Highlighting the need to convert financial inclusion into economic inclusion, Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said only ₹47 is extended as credit for every ₹100 deposited in banks across the Northeast.

He urged banks to expand credit access for entrepreneurs, farmers, women and MSMEs, emphasising that the Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio should reflect “Credit for Development” in the Northeast.

The Minister also stressed the need for a Northeast-specific credit-risk framework. He noted that community-based landownership in the region requires flexible collateral rules to improve access to loans.

Banking Network Expands Across Northeast

Reviewing progress since the first North East Bankers’ Conclave, shri Scindia said approximately 73% progress had been achieved over five years against the banking targets set at the inaugural conclave.

Key achievements include :-

  • 131 new bank branches and 126 ATMs added.
  • 247 new India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) centres established.
  • 6,674 bank branches and 5,823 ATMs operating across the region.
  • Banking touchpoints covering approximately 99.93% of villages.
  • 2,500 additional IPPB access points planned.

Of approximately 9,000 villages identified for improved banking and postal coverage, 6,905 have been covered. The minimum population requirement for opening a physical bank branch has also been reduced from 3,000 to 2,000.

Highlighting the Northeast’s growing adoption of digital banking, Shri Scindia noted that UPI accounts for 90.2% of all non-branch transactions across the region.

₹40,000 Crore Investments Grounded in Northeast

Union Minister Scindia said approximately ₹40,000 crore in investments have been grounded across the eight northeastern states following the Rising North East Investors Summit in May 2025.

He highlighted major infrastructure improvements, including the expansion of the region's airport network from 9 to 17 airports.

He also cited the Bairabi railway line in Mizoram, which has carried approximately 15 lakh passengers through 1,100 trips.

The Minister said that the Northeast receives more than one lakh crore annually through the allocation of 10% of Gross Budgetary Support, monitored by MDoNER. He also highlighted approximately ₹6 lakh crore in fiscal devolution to the eight states.

Northeast Offers Strong Demographic Advantage

Highlighting the region’s demographic and economic potential, Shri Scindia noted that the Northeast has a population of approximately 5 crore. He underscored the importance of harnessing the region’s young population through greater opportunities in education, skill development, entrepreneurship and employment. He said that the average literacy rate across the eight states stands at 93%, while Mizoram has achieved 100% literacy.

Emphasising the region’s natural wealth and economic potential, Scindia said, “The Northeast has a demographic and educational bulge, an array of natural resources and extraordinary natural beauty. When you land at Lengpui, it feels as though you have landed in a forest. Mother Nature has gifted this region something truly exclusive.”

Highlighting the region’s economic growth, he said, “You are not entering an unexplored economic area. The world is growing. Guess what the annual growth rate of the Northeast is ?

It is 9-11% every single year.” He urged banks to play a key role in sustaining this growth.

Reflecting on his engagement with the region, Shri Scindia said, “I have been the Minister of DoNER for about 32 months, and this is my 35th visit to the Northeast. From its caves and rivers to its living root bridges, and from its entrepreneurs to the capabilities of its governments at the village level, I have witnessed the immense potential of this region.”

State-Wise Banking Roadmap

Union minister Scindia outlined four priorities for the Department of Financial Services (DFS): preparing a plan for 70 bank branches, Business Correspondents and IPPB points; strengthening commercial-bank presence; developing a Northeast-specific credit-risk framework; and preparing an action plan for the region's financial system.

He said NEDFi, DFS, MDoNER and state governments have worked together to identify financial gaps and develop state-specific interventions.

Between April and June 2026, the Secretary, MDoNER, held individual consultations with states, which subsequently set their own targets.

The Minister urged bankers to ensure that the Northeast's growing financial access translates into economic opportunities and that value generated in the region remains within the region.

 

#RisingNortheast We must take banking and credit to the remotest corners of the North East - empower our entrepreneurs and turn financial inclusion into an economic opportunity! 📍At the Northeast Bankers’ Conclave 3.0 in Aizawl, alongside CM Pu @Lal_Duhoma ji @CMOMizoram https://t.co/u2Bgz8aIDn

— Jyotiraditya M. Scindia (@JM_Scindia) October 13, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Organises Workshop on Record Management under Special Campaign 6.
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, is observing the “Special Campaign 6” and organised a workshop on “Record Management” on 13th October, 2026, at the Conference Hall, Kartavya Bhawan 2, New Delhi, under the guidance of the Secretary, Legislative Department, Dr. Rajiv Mani.   

The workshop was led by Shri G. Panmei, JS&LC, Legislative Department, and attended by officers and staff members of the Department, including those from its attached offices, namely, the Official Languages Wing and Vidhi Sahitya Prakashan. 

Shri Ranjan Kumar, former Faculty Member, Institute of Secretariat Training and Management, New Delhi, was present at the workshop as the Resource Person and shared his valuable insights on record management. During the workshop, Shri Ranjan Kumar, highlighted the significance of effective record management in promoting administrative efficiency, transparency and accountability. He emphasised the need for systematic maintenance of official records, proper classification and indexing of files and documents, timely review of records, and their preservation or weeding out in accordance with the prescribed rules and guidelines. He further underscored the importance of adhering to record retention schedules and ensuring the proper disposal of records in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Shri G. Panmei, JS&LC, expressed his sincere gratitude to Shri Ranjan Kumar, for sharing his valuable insights and expertise on record management. He also encouraged the officers and employees to ensure the systematic maintenance and proper preservation of official records, their timely review, and adherence to the prescribed rules and guidelines regarding record retention and weeding out. He emphasised that effective record management is essential for the smooth functioning of the Department and for enhancing administrative efficiency and accountability.

item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav conduct joint review of stubble management “Stubble is not a problem, but a solution for enhancing farmers’ income and improving soil health”: High-level inter-ministerial meeting held at Krishi Bhawan Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan sends a clear message to states: “Take action on a war footing to prevent stubble burning; very little time remains” “We must protect the soil and ensure farmers’ prosperity”: Union Agriculture…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav conduct joint review of stubble management
“Stubble is not a problem, but a solution for enhancing farmers’ income and improving soil health”: High-level inter-ministerial meeting held at Krishi Bhawan
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan sends a clear message to states: “Take action on a war footing to prevent stubble burning; very little time remains”
“We must protect the soil and ensure farmers’ prosperity”: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
“Machines must operate in fields, not merely exist on paper: Repair old machines and ensure their availability to small farmers at subsidised rates”: Shri Shivraj Singh
“The Central Government is extending all possible financial assistance to states; Punjab must submit its Utilisation Certificate (UC) promptly to enable the next instalment to be released”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
“Collectors must take charge in the field and work through micro-planning: Prepare a roadmap to convert stubble into electricity, bio-CNG and manure instead of smoke”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level inter-ministerial review meeting was held today at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi, to implement crop residue (stubble) management in mission mode during the ongoing paddy harvesting season. The meeting was co-chaired by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, and Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, the agriculture ministers of key states, including Delhi-NCR, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, Union Secretary for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Narendra Bhushan, and other senior officials from the Central and state governments were present at the meeting.

During the meeting, both Union Ministers made it clear that very little time remained between the completion of crop harvesting and the sowing of rabi crops. Therefore, the administrative machinery must move beyond files and take action directly on the ground on a war footing. They issued firm directions for district-level collectors to convene meetings promptly, strengthen monitoring and ensure that practical solutions were implemented without delay. The emphasis was on swift coordination and effective action at the field level to prevent stubble burning during the critical period.

“Stubble is not a problem, but a means of improving farmers’ income and soil health”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Addressing the meeting, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that paddy harvesting was underway and farmers were eager to prepare their fields for the next crop. In such circumstances, merely telling farmers not to burn stubble would not be enough. They must be provided with alternatives that are easy to use, readily accessible and affordable. Stubble burning not only causes air pollution but also destroys beneficial soil organisms and burns away essential nutrients, turning them into ash. It is therefore necessary to protect Mother Earth and preserve soil health. When crop residue is incorporated into the soil, it can be converted into organic manure; when removed from the field, it can serve as a source of additional income for farmers through its use in bio-CNG, bio-ethanol, electricity generation and animal fodder.

He further stated that the objective was not merely to prevent stubble fires but to develop a robust system in which farmers would have no need to burn crop residue in the first place. The aim should be to create practical and economically viable arrangements for managing stubble while enabling farmers to benefit from opportunities such as carbon credits through environmentally sustainable agricultural practices. Such an approach would protect the environment while also strengthening farmers’ livelihoods and improving the long-term sustainability of agriculture.

Concern over rising incidents in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan; directions issued for action on a war footing

Commenting on the analysis of the data presented during the meeting, Shri Shivraj Chouhan said it was encouraging that, between September 15 and October 12, stubble-burning incidents had declined significantly compared with the corresponding period last year. Haryana recorded a reduction of 53.3 per cent, while Uttar Pradesh registered a decline of approximately 32 per cent. Punjab had also recorded some reduction. However, expressing concern over the increase in stubble-burning incidents in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, the Union Agriculture Minister directed both states to identify the affected districts and villages and immediately implement special action plans to address the situation. He emphasised that a substantial portion of harvesting was still pending. Therefore, even states that had achieved a reduction in incidents must not become complacent and should maintain complete vigilance throughout the remaining harvesting period.

Ensure 100 per cent utilisation of machines; prevent older machines from remaining out of operation

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan placed particular emphasis on ensuring that crop residue management machinery remained operational and was put to effective use. He stated that the Central Government had so far provided states with more than 3.54 lakh crop residue management machines, including 26,109 new machines during the current financial year, 2026–27. He directed the authorities to ensure that, alongside the distribution of new machines, older machines that had become non-functional were repaired immediately and brought back into operation. Failure to do so could create an unnecessary shortage of equipment despite the machinery already available. He also stressed the need to activate Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) and ensure that small and marginal farmers could access the required machinery at affordable, subsidised rates. The focus must be on making the equipment genuinely available to farmers when they need it, rather than allowing it to remain unused.

Substantial financial assistance from the Centre; Punjab urged to submit Utilisation Certificate promptly

Regarding the availability of funds, the meeting was informed that the Central Government had released a substantial amount of ₹4,266.47 crore to states under the Crop Residue Management (CRM) scheme between 2018–19 and 2025–26. This included ₹2,056.50 crore for Punjab, ₹1,171.71 crore for Haryana, ₹868.67 crore for Uttar Pradesh and ₹59 crore for Madhya Pradesh. For the current financial year, 2026–27, an allocation of ₹592.57 crore had also been earmarked, of which ₹430.87 crore had already been released. However, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan expressed concern over the slow utilisation of the allocated funds. He stressed that farmers must receive the necessary resources and equipment in time for them to manage crop residue effectively. In particular, the Punjab Government was urged to submit the Utilisation Certificate (UC) for the funds released earlier to the Centre without delay. This would enable the next instalment under the scheme to be released promptly and without any disruption, ensuring the continued availability of financial support for crop residue management measures.

Use stubble as fodder in drought-affected areas; establish direct links between farmers and industries

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan directed that, in areas facing drought-like conditions, stubble should be collected and stored safely for use as animal fodder and subsequently supplied to livestock. He also called for farmers to be connected directly with supply chains serving thermal power plants for the co-firing of stubble pellets, compressed biogas (CBG) facilities and second-generation (2G) bio-ethanol plants. Such linkages would help create additional avenues for the productive utilisation of crop residue and provide farmers with opportunities to earn additional income. He asked state governments to ensure that approved supply projects were implemented on the ground without delay. He also stressed the need to encourage improved, short-duration paddy varieties, such as Pusa 2090 and PR126, in place of longer-duration varieties such as Pusa-44. Shorter-duration varieties would allow farmers to harvest their crops earlier and provide sufficient time to clear their fields before the next sowing season.

Assurance of all possible assistance to states

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the primary responsibility for implementation at the grassroots level rested with state governments. However, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Central Government stood firmly alongside states and farmers, extending all possible technical, administrative and financial support at every stage. He called upon all participating ministries, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and district administrations to treat stubble management as a shared national commitment and work collectively towards its effective implementation. He emphasised that coordinated efforts by the Centre, state governments and local administrations were essential to ensure that practical solutions reached farmers in time. The ultimate objective was to keep agricultural fields free from pollution, protect soil health, improve farmers’ livelihoods and contribute to the prosperity of the farming community.

“Strict monitoring of the satellite observation gap after 3 PM directed”: Shri Bhupender Yadav

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav stressed the need to intensify ground-level monitoring and enforcement measures to prevent stubble-burning incidents. He called for special vigilance in key districts of Punjab, including Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Amritsar, Patiala and Gurdaspur, as well as in Haryana districts such as Kaithal, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Ambala and Fatehabad. The objective was to assess crop-harvesting patterns in these areas and anticipate the likelihood of stubble-burning incidents so that preventive measures could be undertaken in advance. He emphasised the importance of identifying vulnerable areas and strengthening local monitoring arrangements during the ongoing harvesting season.

Shri Yadav highlighted the need to integrate data relating to stubble burning with the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to improve the effectiveness of monitoring. He said it was important to forecast the likely timing of harvesting in the coming days and closely monitor meteorological conditions that could affect air pollution levels in the National Capital Region (NCR). Such information would help authorities assess the evolving situation and take the necessary action in a timely manner. He also called for effective evaluation of the impact of interventions and the identification of corrective measures to address emerging challenges. Continuous assessment of the measures being implemented would be essential to strengthen the response and improve the effectiveness of efforts to prevent crop residue burning.

Emphasising that monitoring must not depend solely on satellite data, Shri Yadav said district collectors should undertake ground-level assessments and strengthen enforcement measures to make efforts to prevent crop residue burning more effective. He underlined the need for strict surveillance through ground patrols and flying squads during the gap in satellite monitoring after 3 PM, when no satellite pass is available. This period requires particular attention to ensure that incidents of stubble burning do not go undetected. He stressed that a combination of satellite-based monitoring, field inspections and effective enforcement would help authorities respond more promptly and prevent the burning of crop residue during the critical harvesting period.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), National Culture Fund (NCF) and Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Sign MoA for Conservation and Development of Heritage Sites
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:21PM by PIB Delhi

HAL, NCF and ASI today signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) for undertaking heritage conservation and development works at three prominent heritage sites- Hampi in Karnataka, the Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, and Bekal Fort in Kerala.

The MoA was signed in the presence of Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture at Kartavya Bhawan-02, New Delhi. Shri Pradeep Kumar, Executive Director (HR), signed the MoA on behalf of HAL.

Senior officials from HAL - Shri M G Balasubrahmanya, Director(HR) , Ramesh K, DGM(HR)-CSR, Ms Varsha, CM(HR) ,Mr Sudhakar, Manager( HR) were also present at the event alongwith Senior officials of NCF and ASI.

HAL has accorded in-principle approval for financial support amounting to ₹23.60 crore for the projects over the financial years 2026-27 to 2028-29. The proposed initiatives aim to conserve, preserve and enhance visitor amenities at these important heritage sites, contributing to the protection of India’s rich cultural legacy and promoting sustainable heritage tourism.

The projects at Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, include interventions in the historic North and South Bazaar areas, with proposed development works extending approximately 270 metres and 250 metres, respectively. The initiatives at the Taj Mahal and Bekal Fort will focus on approved conservation and site-development works in consultation with ASI.

The National Culture Fund, established by the Ministry of Culture, facilitates partnerships between the Government and the corporate sector for the conservation and promotion of India’s tangible and intangible cultural heritage. Through this collaboration, NCF will facilitate the implementation of the projects in coordination with HAL and ASI.

The projects will be undertaken under the technical guidance and supervision of ASI, ensuring adherence to established conservation principles and prescribed norms.

The partnership reflects HAL’s commitment to corporate social responsibility and its contribution towards safeguarding India’s cultural heritage. It also underscores the importance of collaborative efforts between public institutions and corporate organisations in preserving the country’s invaluable heritage for future generations.

The signing of the MoA marks an important step towards strengthening public–private partnerships in the heritage sector and advancing the shared objective of protecting and promoting India’s cultural legacy.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship to Research Aspirations
The Journey of Ahmedabad’s Bhavesh A. Prabhakar
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi

Education can open pathways to advanced learning, research and professional growth, for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

When the Government support is made available, the financial constraints disappear that help the aspirants to continue higher education.

Bhavesh A. Prabhakar, a resident of Ahmedabad, Gujarat, faced this challenge while aspiring to pursue a Ph.D.

Coming from a family with limited financial resources, Bhavesh experienced significant economic barriers that threatened his ability to undertake doctoral studies.

Despite these difficulties, he remained committed to advancing his knowledge and developing strong research skills.

Support through the National Fellowship for SC Students

The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste (SC) Students (NFSC) Scheme became an important source of support in Bhavesh’s academic journey. His fellowship assistance began in December 2019, helping ease the financial difficulties that had made pursuing a Ph.D. uncertain.

Greater Focus on Education and Research

With financial pressure reduced, Bhavesh was able to focus more closely on his academic work. The assistance supported his efforts to pursue doctoral studies and work towards his goal of building research skills. His experience illustrates how financial assistance can help students continue advanced education when economic circumstances might otherwise limit their options.

Sustaining Academic and Professional Aspirations

Bhavesh is currently employed full-time. His journey highlights the role that targeted fellowship support can play in reducing economic barriers and helping students pursue their academic goals. By easing financial hardship, the NFSC Scheme has helped him continue working towards his Ph.D. and devote more time to learning and research.

Reflecting on the importance of the support, Bhavesh stated, “If I had not received the NFSC scholarship, I would not have been able to do my Ph.D.”

The fellowship helped address his financial concerns and enabled him to devote greater attention to education and research.

Bhavesh A. Prabhakar’s experience reflects the importance of making research opportunities more accessible to students from economically weaker backgrounds. Financial support can be a critical factor in enabling aspiring scholars to pursue advanced studies, strengthen their research capacity and work towards their long-term educational and professional aspirations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Limited Income to a More Secure Livelihood
Shri Tadikonda Rambabu’s Journey towards Financial Stability through Swachhta Udyami Yojana
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

Through targeted financial assistance and support for sanitation-related equipment, the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) under the NAMASTE framework is aimed to create opportunities for income generation and self-reliance. This way the sustainable livelihood opportunities can play an important role in improving the economic security and dignity of Safai Karamcharis.

Shri Tadikonda Rambabu, aged 40, is a Safai Karamchari belonging to the Scheduled Caste community. He has been working with the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation on an outsourcing basis since 2016.

Having completed his Secondary School Certificate (SSC), he was unable to pursue higher education due to financial constraints. His family depended primarily on his monthly income of approximately Rs 19,000, while meeting household expenses and supporting the education of his two sons remained a continuing challenge.

Shri Rambabu’s wife is a homemaker. His elder son is studying in Class 10 and his younger son is in Intermediate Second Year. With limited financial resources and experiences of social discrimination, he aspired to improve his family’s standard of living and provide his children with better educational opportunities.

On 21 August 2025, Shri Rambabu, along with four other members, received assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the NAMASTE framework. The group received an upfront capital subsidy for a project to procure a Gulfer 8 KL desludging vehicle, enabling them to undertake sanitation-related services and establish an additional source of income alongside their existing work.

The total project cost was Rs 50 lakh, supported by a loan of Rs 31.25 lakh and a capital subsidy of Rs 18.75 lakh. Through the project, Shri Rambabu now earns approximately Rs 10,000 in additional income per month. His total monthly income has increased from around Rs 19,000 to approximately Rs 29,000, helping him manage household expenses and his children’s educational needs more effectively.

The additional income has strengthened the family’s financial security and reduced the pressure of meeting day-to-day expenses. The project has also provided Shri Rambabu and his group members with an opportunity to build a more sustainable livelihood through sanitation-related entrepreneurial activity.

Shri Tadikonda Rambabu’s journey highlights the role of the Swachhta Udyami Yojana under the NAMASTE framework in supporting livelihood generation and socio-economic empowerment among Safai Karamcharis. By facilitating access to capital subsidy for sanitation equipment, the scheme has helped him increase his income, support his children’s education and work towards a more stable and dignified future for his family.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Mines
Ministry of Mines Organises Outreach Programme on Auction of Offshore Mineral Blocks
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, organised an Outreach Programme on Auction of Offshore Mineral Blocks on 13th October 2026 at New Delhi. The programme provided a platform for prospective bidders and stakeholders to understand the two offshore mineral blocks offered for auction, the applicable policy and regulatory framework, the bidding process and the support available for exploration.

The Ministry has issued the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) dated 1 October 2026 for the grant of operating rights for two offshore mineral blocks, Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01, located in the Andaman Sea. Both blocks contain polymetallic nodules and crusts and are being offered for the grant of a Composite Licence. Sewell Rise-01 covers an area of 632 square kilometres, while West Sewell Ridge-01 covers 1,000 square kilometres, taking the total area offered for auction to 1,632 square kilometres.

Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, highlighted the importance of strengthening India’s mineral supply chains to support economic growth, technological advancement, the energy transition and manufacturing competitiveness. He highlighted the potential of the Critical Mineral Processing Park coming up on the eastern coast of India to support offshore mineral processing.

Dr. Veena Kumari Dermal, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Mines, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to facilitate the transparent and responsible development of India’s offshore mineral resources. Taking stakeholder feedback into account, the Ministry has revised block configurations, including increasing the area of polymetallic nodule and crust blocks to provide greater operational flexibility for offshore exploration. She also noted that the Terms of Reference and Guidelines for Baseline Environmental Data Collection and Environmental Management Plans for offshore mineral exploration and exploitation in India’s Exclusive Economic Zone have been circulated to the concerned Central Ministries and Departments for comments and will be finalised shortly.

The Geological Survey of India (GSI) presented an overview of the offshore mineral blocks, including their geological characteristics and mineral potential. SBI Capital Markets Limited (SBICAPS), the Transaction Advisor, explained the policy framework, auction process, tender provisions and bidding requirements. MSTC, the auction platform provider, demonstrated the step-by-step procedure for purchasing tender documents and submitting bids through the e-auction portal.

The National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) presented the scheme for partial reimbursement of exploration expenses for Composite Licence holders of offshore mineral blocks. The presentation outlined the support available to facilitate exploration activities.

An open-house discussion enabled participants to interact with the Ministry and the organisations involved in the auction. Prospective bidders and other stakeholders sought clarifications and shared their views on the blocks, tender conditions, auction procedures and exploration-related support.

The auction is being conducted under the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, and the Offshore Areas Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2024, as amended. The auction framework seeks to ensure transparency in the allocation of offshore mineral resources and facilitate systematic exploration and responsible development of India’s offshore mineral potential.

Polymetallic nodules and crusts contain minerals such as nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese, which are important for various industrial applications and emerging technologies. The initiative forms part of the Government of India’s efforts to advance offshore mineral exploration and strengthen the country’s mineral resource base. Systematic exploration will be essential to establish the mineral potential of the blocks and assess their prospects for future development.

Auction Schedule

The sale of tender documents commenced on 1 October 2026. The pre-bid conference is scheduled for 4 November 2026, and the last date for submission of queries is 13 November 2026. Tender documents may be purchased up to 21 December 2026, while the last date for submission of bids is 28 December 2026.

The Notice Inviting Tender and related auction documents are available on the MSTC e-auction portal: https://www.mstcecommerce.com/auctionhome/mlcln/index.jsp

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Addiction to Self-Reliance: A Journey of Recovery and Renewed Hope
Gorakhpur UP’s Amit Kumar’s Journey towards Recovery and Financial Stability through the NAPDDR
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

Through the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment provides support to individuals affected by substance use through treatment, counselling, rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

Access to de-addiction treatment, rehabilitation and sustained psychological support can play an important role in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives.

Amit Kumar (name changed), aged 47, belongs to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community and resides in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. He was engaged in self-employment but faced significant personal, social and economic challenges due to substance addiction. Influenced by bad company and stress, he developed a habit of smoking and using addictive substances. Over time, his addiction adversely affected his physical and mental well-being, reduced his self-confidence and created difficulties in maintaining regular work and healthy social relationships. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, he experienced economic hardship and an unstable income due to irregular employment. Social stigma further contributed to his isolation, while strained family relationships added to his difficulties.

Despite these challenges, Amit Kumar aspired to overcome his addiction, regain his self-respect, lead a healthier life and support his family financially. He had previously undergone treatment in 2018 and experienced improvement, but subsequently relapsed. Determined to recover and rebuild his life, he sought treatment again and committed himself to the recovery process.

On 13 August 2021, Amit Kumar received support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) through Basudev Tiwari Sewa Sansthan’s Punarjanm Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. The centre provided free de-addiction treatment, medical care, prescribed medicines, psychological counselling and motivational support. Regular counselling sessions and follow-up care helped him address the challenges associated with addiction and remain committed to his recovery. Family counselling and emotional support also played an important role in rebuilding his confidence, improving family relationships and supporting his reintegration into society.

With sustained assistance from the centre and his own determination, Amit Kumar successfully quit smoking and substance use. Following his recovery, he resumed working and established a livelihood by driving his own auto-rickshaw. He now earns approximately ₹30,000 per month, a significant improvement from his earlier situation of irregular work and unstable income. His earnings have helped improve his family’s financial condition and enabled him to contribute more consistently towards household expenses. The combination of treatment, counselling, rehabilitation and follow-up support has helped him move towards a healthier, more responsible and financially stable life.

Amit Kumar’s journey highlights the role of the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction in supporting recovery, rehabilitation and socio-economic reintegration among individuals affected by substance dependence. The assistance provided through Punarjanm IRCA helped him regain his confidence, resume productive work and work towards financial self-reliance. His experience demonstrates how timely treatment, psychological support and family involvement can create opportunities for individuals to overcome addiction, rebuild relationships and lead a dignified life.

Amit Kumar’s transformation from addiction and economic uncertainty to recovery and livelihood security stands as an encouraging example of resilience and renewed hope. His journey reinforces the importance of accessible de-addiction services and sustained rehabilitation support in helping individuals reclaim their lives, strengthen their families and move towards a healthier and more secure future.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Food Processing Industries
NIFTEM-K Hosts India–Canada Roundtable on Pulse Protein Innovation, Value Addition and Strategic Partnerships
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi

National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management, Kundli (NIFTEM-K), an Institute of National Importance, under the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Government of India, organised a Roundtable Conference on “Pulse Protein Innovation, Value Addition and Strategic Partnerships” on 13 October 2026. The conference brought together senior government representatives, academic leaders, industry associations and research organisations from India and Canada to strengthen bilateral cooperation in pulse protein innovation, food processing, research and sustainable nutrition.

The conference was attended by Mr. Ken Cheveldayoff, Hon’ble Minister of Advanced Education, Government of Saskatchewan, Canada, along with David Anderson, Managing Director, Government of Saskatchewan, and Harish Vaidyanathan, Senior Trade Officer, Saskatchewan India Office. The University of Saskatchewan (USask) delegation included Dr. Baljit Singh, Vice-President (Research); Dr. Trever Crowe, Associate Dean (Research and Graduate Studies); Dr. Ajay Dalai, Professor; and Dr. Supratim Ghosh, Professor.

Industry and research organisations were represented by Greg Cherewyk, President, Pulse Canada; Julianne Curran, Vice-President (Market Innovation), Pulse Canada; Carl Potts, Executive Director, Saskatchewan Pulse Growers; Leanne Fischbuch, Executive Director, Alberta Pulse Growers; Bob Behari, CEO, Enviroway; and Prachi Kaul, Director, Shastri Indo-Canadian Institute. Representatives of Indian organisations and industry, including Nutrition International, Nutricircle, India Pulses and Grains Association, ICAR–Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur, the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT), Diet Foods, Good Food Institute India and IIT Delhi, also participated in the discussions.

In his address, Hon. Ken Cheveldayoff highlighted the importance of India–Saskatchewan relations and the value of personal connections in strengthening ties between India and Canada. He underlined the opportunities for closer cooperation in higher education, research, innovation and academic exchange, noting the potential for institutions and industry to work together on shared priorities.

Dr. Harinder Singh Oberoi, Director, NIFTEM-K, emphasised the importance of translating the points mentioned in the Memorandum of Understanding between NIFTEM-K and the University of Saskatchewan into tangible outcomes. He stated that the partnership should move beyond the agreement to a clear, time-bound programme of action that delivers meaningful benefits for both countries. He expressed his gratitude to all the stakeholders and expressed satisfaction about the significant progress made during the short period of about seven months after the MoU was signed. He highlighted the goal of working towards establishing the joint Centre of Excellence at NIFTEM-K within the next year, supported by a practical roadmap, defined milestones and institutional coordination.

The discussions also recognised key challenges in pulse processing and protein ingredient development. These include ensuring consistency in raw materials and ingredients, managing process energy requirements and energy use, optimising processing conditions, and preserving or improving the functional properties of pulse proteins. Participants also highlighted the importance of addressing texture-related challenges and developing fit-for-purpose pulse-based ingredients that can support value addition and the development of innovative food products.

Dr. Oberoi further stressed that the partners should identify priority research areas and agree on an actionable plan for the first two years. Potential areas of collaboration include pulse protein extraction and processing, value addition, development of innovative and nutritious food products, joint research projects and publications, joint PhD degree programme, student and faculty exchanges, training programmes, and collaborative research funding. He also highlighted the importance of industry participation to help translate research into scalable technologies, commercial products and wider market opportunities.

Dr. Baljit Singh while expressing satisfaction over the progress made by both the University of Saskatchewan (USask) and NIFTEM-K mentioned that USask has identified PhD students who will do part of their research work at NIFTEM-K. He also stated that a collaborative project entitled “ Sustainable health innovation in fortification (lentils) for SDG 2.2 (end all forms of malnutrition), has been submitted by USask in collaboration with NIFTEM-K and other international partners for funding by Government of Canada. The roundtable coordinated by Dr. Baljit Singh provided a platform for academic and industry stakeholders to discuss research collaboration, capacity building, technology development and commercialisation. Participants explored opportunities to develop value-added pulse-based foods, strengthen links between researchers and businesses, and address emerging needs in sustainable and plant-based nutrition. The discussions also focused on creating a coordinated framework through which research priorities, expertise and facilities in India and Canada can complement each other.

The conference forms part of the broader effort to advance the joint Centre of Excellence, with NIFTEM-K and the University of Saskatchewan serving as co-chairs of the initiative, as stated in the conference background. The proposed collaboration is intended to bring together academic expertise, government support and industry engagement to advance pulse protein innovation and strengthen research and educational links between the two countries.

The roundtable concluded with an emphasis on converting the discussions into defined priorities, responsibilities and timelines. The proposed roadmap and two-year research priorities are expected to provide a foundation for sustained institutional cooperation and measurable progress in pulse protein research, value addition and innovation, further strengthening India–Canada academic, scientific and industry partnerships.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NISD’s Five-Day Geriatric Caregivers Training Programme Successfully Concludes in Diu
56 Women Participants Trained To Strengthen Community-Based Elderly Care, Promote The Dignity, Safety And Well-Being Of Senior Citizens
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment , Government of India, in collaboration with the District Administration of Diu, in the Union Territory of Dadra And Nagar Haveli & Daman  and Diu, successfully conducted a Five-Day Geriatric Caregivers Training Programme for Primary Caregivers, Family Members and Frontline Workers, that concluded at Diu today.

The Programme was organized at Government Education Hub at Kevdi, Diu.

Organised by the Senior Citizen Division, NISD, the programme aimed to strengthen community-based elderly care by equipping family caregivers, Anganwadi Workers and frontline functionaries with essential knowledge, practical caregiving skills and sensitivity towards the needs of senior citizens.

On October 9, the programme was inaugurated by Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, who emphasised the importance of compassionate caregiving and community support for India's ageing population.

On the occasion, the Secretary administered Senior Citizen Pledge to sensitize the participants about upholding the dignity, safety, well-being and holistic care of senior citizens.

The inaugural ceremony was also attended by Joint Secretaries, MoSJ&E Shri Sajeesh Kumar N. and Dr Sandeep R. Rathod, Director, NISD Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, District Magistrate, Diu Shri Rahul Dev Boora and Ms. Ranjita Kotiyal, President, District Panchayat, Diu.

The training covered effective communication, age-related health conditions, monitoring of vital signs, infection prevention and control, fall prevention, basic first aid, balanced nutrition and use of comfort and assistive devices, complemented by practical demonstrations and hands-on sessions conducted by NISD's training team.

During the training programme, the key areas included the ageing process and changing needs of senior citizens; rights, dignity and well-being of older persons; roles of families, communities and frontline caregivers; principles of basic geriatric care; assistance with routine activities and ADLs; personal hygiene; nutrition and hydration; medication-related support; mobility assistance; safe transfer techniques; fall prevention and home safety.

The programme also covered basic first aid and response to common emergencies, communication skills, psychosocial support, loneliness and social isolation, emotional well-being, and dementia awareness and basic caregiving approaches.

During the programme special emphasis was placed on the prevention, identification and reporting of neglect, abuse and exploitation of senior citizens, while reinforcing the principles of privacy, dignity, respect and compassionate care.

The participants were also oriented to Government schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and support services available for senior citizens, enabling them to facilitate timely access to relevant benefits and services.

The programme combined technical sessions, interactive lectures, demonstrations, practical exercises, case studies and field-oriented examples. Group activities, experience-sharing and question-and-answer sessions will provide participants an opportunity to relate the training inputs to their field experience and develop practical responses to the diverse needs of older persons.

Practical exposure to basic caregiving techniques formed an important component of the programme, with emphasis on translating knowledge into effective community-level support.

The programme concluded with the distribution of Certificates to 56 trainees in the presence of Shri D. R. Damania, Chief Officer, Diu Municipal Council; Shri Rahul Dev Boora, District Magistrate, Diu and Smt. Hemlata G. Baria, Advocate, Diu.

The collaboration between the NISD, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, and the Union Territory Administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, through the Office of the Collector, Diu, reflected a coordinated approach towards strengthening geriatric care and community-based support mechanisms at the grassroots level.

The initiative reaffirmed NISD's commitment to developing a skilled and sensitised caregiving workforce and promoting dignified, compassionate and community-based care for senior citizens.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO to lead thematic session on ‘Semiconductors & Next-Gen Chips’ at ESTIC-2026
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) will spearhead a thematic session on ‘Semiconductors and Next-Gen Chips’ during Emerging Science, Technology & Innovation Conclave (ESTIC-2026) scheduled to be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi from October 27 to 29, 2026. The conclave is being jointly organised by 12 ministries/departments under the guidance of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. It is a significant national initiative aimed at advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 and strengthening Aatmanirbharta through science, technology and innovation.

The DRDO session will bring together eminent leaders from the industry, academia, indigenous chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics. It will feature a keynote address by VP & MD, Micron India followed by talks by CEO, Bharat Semi, CEO, Netrasemi and Director, IIT Madras. The talks will explore key developments in semiconductor technologies, purpose-built AI system-on-chips, intelligence at the silicon edge and the evolving microprocessor landscape.

The speakers with diverse expertise will enable a substantive dialogue on semiconductor fabrication, chip design, AI computing, indigenous semiconductor platforms, research and development, and strategic and defence applications. The session is expected to foster stronger collaboration among industry, academia and strategic stakeholders, identify emerging technological opportunities and contribute to the development of a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, with emphasis on indigenous capabilities for critical and next-generation applications.

The Outreach Stall at ESTIC 2026 will provide a platform to showcase the Ministry’s key initiatives, achievements, research programmes, and contributions to science, technology, and innovation. The stall will feature a diverse range of indigenous technologies developed by DRDO laboratories, including advanced communication systems, quantum technology prototypes, extreme-cold-weather clothing, the PRABALA female full-body protector, passive and powered exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, high-power pulse laser diodes, and scramjet engine technology.

The exhibits will highlight ongoing efforts to strengthen indigenous R&D, promote technology development and self-reliance, and address critical requirements in defence and other strategic sectors. The stall will also foster collaboration among academia, industry, start-ups, and research institutions while enhancing public awareness of the Ministry’s role in advancing India’s scientific and technological capabilities.

Presiding over the curtain-raiser event organised by DRDO in Bengaluru, Karnataka on October 13, 2026, Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Electronics and Communication Systems) Dr BK Das underscored the importance of semiconductors and next-gen chips for economic competitiveness, digital sovereignty and national security. He stressed that building an end-to-end, resilient microelectronics ecosystem is essential to powering telecommunications, automotive systems, industrial automation, AI hardware and strategic defence platforms as India advances towards Viksit Bharat.

Dr Das added that strengthening domestic capabilities is critical to protecting the national economy from global supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical volatility and international technology export controls. He underlined India's aim to emerge as a global semiconductor powerhouse, advancing strategic autonomy and high-value exports across the microelectronics value chain.

Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Technology Management) Dr Anupam Sharma highlighted the critical role of semiconductors in modern warfare, stating that these technologies are integral to virtually every aspect of military operations. He added that business in the semiconductor-related segment is expected to rise to 200 billion dollars by 2035.

Director, Directorate of Extramural Research & Intellectual Property Rights, Director, Solid State Physics Laboratory, Director, Electronics and Radar Development Establishment and Center Head, Combat Aircraft Systems Development & Integration Centre were among those present on the occasion.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
21st Meeting of Maritime State Development Council Concludes Successfully at Mumbai
Council reinforces Centre–State coordination for integrated maritime growth under statutory mandate and development of National Ports Perspective Plan
Shipbuilding Project Credit Risk Insurance Policy (SbPCP), and Business Credit Shield Policy–Shipbuilders (BCSPS), credit risk insurance products are launched to support India’s shipbuilding industry
One Nation One Port Process (ONOP) reforms to be implemented across all the ports by March 2027
Council Mandates Electronic publication of port tariffs for transparency
States, in coordination with the Central Government, to develop port-linked Industrial Regions with plug-and-play infrastructure and fast-tracked approvals
MSDC is the cooperative federalism at play in maritime governance, delivering for our ports & for port-led industrialisation: Sarbananda Sonowal
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The 21st Maritime State Development Council (MSDC) concluded today in Mumbai with landmark outcomes for India’s maritime sector. This was the first meeting of the MSDC after its recognition as a statutory consultative body under the Indian Ports Act, 2025, notified on 15th May 2026. The Council, originally constituted in 1997, now functions with an enhanced mandate to promote integrated maritime growth, coordinated policy formulation, and planned development of maritime infrastructure.

Chaired by Union Minister for Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Shri Sarbananda Sonowal, the MSDC meeting brought together Ministers of Coastal States, Administrators of Union Territories, senior officials of State Maritime Boards, Chairpersons of Major Ports, allied maritime institutions, and representatives of Central Ministries. Among the dignitaries present were Shri Kanubhai Desai, Finance Minister of Gujarat; Shri Digambar V. Kamat, Minister (Ports), Government of Goa; Shri Nitesh Rane, Minister of Fisheries & Ports Development, Government of Maharashtra; and Shri Malladi Krishna Rao, Minister from Puducherry. Senior Secretaries and CEOs of Maritime Boards from Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala also participated, along with Chairpersons of Major Ports including Deendayal, JNPA, MbPA, Cochin, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, SMPA, Kamarajar, and Mormugao. Heads of allied organisations such as the Inland Waterways Authority of India, Shipping Corporation of India, Dredging Corporation of India, Indian Port Rail & Ropeway Corporation, Cochin Shipyard, Indian Maritime University, DPIIT, NITI Aayog, Indian Navy and Coast Guard were also in attendance.

The meeting was preceded by educational port visits to the Mumbai Port Authority Cruise Terminal and Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), showcasing India’s cruise and container port capabilities.

During the deliberations, the Council adopted the Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets, which together identify over 500 initiatives across ports, shipping, inland waterways, shipbuilding, green shipping and global collaboration. States and State Maritime Boards were urged to prepare Port Master Plans for Other Than Major Ports aligned with these national targets, with MoPSW sharing the standardized template used by Major Ports.

The Council endorsed the priorities of the National Perspective Plan and urged States to fast-track multimodal connectivity projects through road, rail, inland waterways, pipelines and conveyors. It resolved that States, in coordination with MoPSW, to develop port-linked industrial clusters with land availability, plug-and-play infrastructure and fast-tracked approvals, integrated with port capacity expansion and connectivity projects.

On statutory compliance, the Council approved draft MSDC Regulations and Guidelines on port data and tariff transparency, and instructed all States and Union Territories to notify subordinate rules under Section 77 of the Act within three months.

"The Indian Ports Act gave the MSD council its legal foundation. Today the Centre and the coastal states turned that foundation into a shared work plan, with deadlines every one of us has agreed to meet," Sarbananda Sonowal said. "This is cooperative federalism in maritime governance, delivering for our ports and for port-led industrialisation."

In a major step towards ease of doing business, the Council resolved that the One Nation One Port Process (ONOP) reforms, including One Nation One Documentation, Port Process Re-engineering and Inter-ministerial Process Reforms, to be implemented across all ports by March 2027. It further resolved that all ports shall integrate with the Maritime Single Window (MSW – Sagar Setu) by March 2027, ensuring unified digital processes nationwide. Transparency of port tariffs through electronic publication was also mandated. To support uniform implementation, Minister Shri Sarbananda Sonowal launched the Ready Reckoner for Implementing ONOP, a comprehensive guide for Major and Other Than Major Ports. The document includes references to central circulars issued by CBIC, MHA and MoHFW for implementing inter-ministerial process reforms, and sets out clear expectations from State and Union Territory Governments to expedite ONOP implementation.

The Council gave particular emphasis to port connectivity, shipbuilding and cruise shipping. It resolved to prioritise connectivity projects under Sagarmala, implement the National Coastal and Inland Shipping Strategic Plan, promote modal shift of cargo to coastal shipping, facilitate development of shipbuilding, ship-repair and recycling clusters, and leverage the Maritime Development Fund, Shipbuilding Development Scheme and Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Programme for financing. Cruise shipping infrastructure development at Major and Non-Major Ports was also endorsed.

A significant announcement was made by Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal, introducing two specialized credit risk insurance products to support India’s shipbuilding industry under the National Shipbuilding Mission. Developed under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS), these first-of-their-kind insurance policies aim to reduce financial stress in large-scale ship manufacturing. The Shipbuilding Project Credit Risk Insurance Policy (SbPCP), developed by ECGC Ltd., will cover export projects, while the Business Credit Shield Policy–Shipbuilders (BCSPS), developed by The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. (NIACL), will protect domestic projects. The Government of India will subsidise insurance premiums and provide direct support to insurers in case shipyards file claims. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Sonowal said, “Building a ship is a massive, multi-year journey, a single missed milestone payment could stall an entire shipyard’s operations. With these new insurance policies, we are stepping in to give them a real safety net. We want our shipyards to focus on what they do best, building world-class vessels, without the fear of delayed payments or sudden global market shifts holding them back.”

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal emphasized the significance of the meeting, stating, “The MSDC has now entered a new statutory phase, strengthening cooperative federalism in maritime governance. With the adoption of MIV 2030 and MAKV 2047 targets, India’s ports and shipping sector will be future-ready, competitive and aligned with global standards. The Council’s resolutions today mark a decisive step towards integrated maritime growth and port-led industrialisation.”

The 21st MSDC has set a jointly owned course of action for integrated development of Major and Non-Major Ports, reinforcing India’s maritime vision under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal called the meeting "a meeting of Team India" and tied the council's work to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call of "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas," or together with all, development for all, trust of all, effort of all.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Union Women and Child Development Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi Visits NCPCR, Reviews Office Functioning and Directs Timely Disposal of Pending Files by December 31, 2026
7,000 files Weeded out by NCPCR during 2025-26, target of Weeding out of 10,000 files for 2026-27
Expedite development of an AI based tool to proactively detect Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material (CSEAM) – Smt. Annpurna Devi
Union Women and Child Development Minister directs that complaints to be handled sensitively, responsibly and expeditiously
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annapurna Devi, visited the office of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) on 13th October, 2026 to inspect the premises under the “Swachhta Abhiyan”, implementation phase of which has started from 2 October to 31 October, 2026. She inspected the NCPCR office located in the Chandra Lok Building, Janpath.

During the inspection, while reviewing the record management, the Minister pointed out that all physical files should be digitized and only those files which require preservation should be retained in hard copy. She stated that the process of weeding out should be expedited, as it would not only beautify the office but also create space that can be utilized for better purposes.

Smt. Annpurna Devi was informed that during 2025-26, NCPCR weeded out more than 7,000 files by scanning more than 5.3 lakh pages. For 2026-27, NCPCR has targeted scanning of more than 8 lakh pages and weeding out of over 10,000 files.

The Minister emphasised the need for the timely disposal of pending files by December 31, 2026, to ensure efficient and expeditious administrative processes. She also stressed the importance of maintaining cleanliness and hygiene in the workplace.

The Minister interacted with the staff of NCPCR to understand their domain work and their contributions. She expressed satisfaction on the general upkeep and cleanliness of the office.

After the inspection, Smt. Annpurna Devi interacted with the Chairperson, Shri V. Prem Chand, and the Member Secretary, Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, to review the progress of the initiatives undertaken by NCPCR. The Chairperson apprised the Minister of the efforts of NCPCR in developing Social Media Guidelines for Technology Companies.

The Minister was also apprised that NCPCR, in collaboration with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is working on the development of an AI-based tool to proactively detect Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material (CSEAM) circulating on the internet. The Minister expressed that both initiatives should be implemented expeditiously, as both areas are very important and deserve immediate attention.

Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi directed that complaints received should be handled sensitively, responsibly and expeditiously. Recalling the Hon'ble Prime Minister's statement that “an effective grievance redressal system is the true strength of a democracy”, she stated that no stone should be left unturned to extend all support to the complainants.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
Ministry of Panchayati Raj to undertake cleanliness drive and disposal of pending matters on 14 October 2026 under Special Campaign 6.0
Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Local Bodies across States and Union Territories to Participate in a Dedicated One-Day Drive for Cleanliness, Improved Public Spaces and Expedited Disposal of Pending Matters
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Special Campaign 6.0 for Institutionalising Swachhata and Minimising Pendency (SCDPM 6.0), the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) will organise a dedicated one-day cleanliness and pendency disposal drive on 14 October 2026. The drive is part of the Implementation Phase of the Campaign, being observed from 2 October to 31 October 2026. It aims to promote workplace cleanliness, improve the use of office space and expedite the disposal of pending matters, including references and other identified pendencies. Activities planned for the day include cleanliness shramdaan and Swachhata drives at workplaces and workstations, minor repairs and removal of clutter, staff orientation on bio-waste management, proper collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, scrap disposal, public grievance redressal, interaction with Safai Mitras and review of progress under the Campaign. All Divisions and Sections of the Ministry are actively participating in the Campaign and taking steps to ensure the timely completion of planned activities.

To encourage grassroots-level participation, 14 October 2026 has also been designated for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)/Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) across the country to undertake dedicated campaign activities. The Ministry had earlier issued an advisory on 12 October 2026 to the Additional Chief Secretaries, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries of the Panchayati Raj Departments of all States and Union Territories, calling for the active participation of PRIs/RLBs. The activities will include cleanliness drives in Panchayat offices and nearby public places, removal of unused materials, beautification of public spaces using locally available resources and tree plantation with community participation. PRIs will also review pending complaints, grievances and applications for timely disposal. Personnel engaged in cleanliness and sanitation activities will be felicitated.

As part of its efforts to improve workplace efficiency, the Ministry also organised an e-Office training session for its officials and staff at Jeevan Prakash Building, New Delhi. The session covered the latest e-Office features, file workflow processes and digital record management, with a focus on smoother file movement and timely disposal of official work. These initiatives seek to promote Swachhata, minimise pendency and strengthen efficient, accountable and responsive governance in line with the objectives of Special Campaign 6.0.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) & Autonomous Bodies(ABs) observes Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Autonomous Bodies (ABs) are actively participating in the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 commenced from 2nd October 2026.

MHI & its CPSEs/ABs have conducted various events including Shramdaan, cleaning drives, health check-up camps, tree plantation drives, waste to wealth initiatives etc., at various locations. E-Waste, including old computers and printers, obsolete electronic equipment, electrical items, batteries and scrap machinery parts were identified, segregated and collected in accordance with applicable environmental and e-waste guidelines.

During the Implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, all CPSEs and ABs have systematically planned their activities related to record management, cleanliness drives, scrap disposal, space and E-Waste Management. These efforts are being closely monitored by the Ministry to ensure active participation in the campaign’s implementation phase during 2nd October to 31st October 2026.

MHI observed a dedicated one-day event on 6th October 2026, during which Shri Vijay Mittal, Joint Secretary, MHI, felicitated Safai Mitras by presenting them with protective gear kits containing T-shirts, gloves and masks.

 
 Shri Vijay Mittal, Joint Secretary, MHI felicitated Safai Mitras

In addition, MHI conducted a cleanliness drive at the public park adjacent to the GPOA-3 Building, Netaji Nagar. A large number of MHI’s officials participated and contributed Shramdaan to support the campaign. Almirahs were provided to various Sections within the Ministry to facilitate proper document management and optimize space utilization.

Cleanliness drive was conducted at the public park adjacent to the GPOA-3 Building, Netaji Nagar

Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) carried out Shramdaan, plantation and cleaning activities at BTPS Manuguru, Satpura Site, Sarni; Talcher Site; TP Jhansi; HPEP Hyderabad’s Wednesday Market; HEP Bhopal’s Gandhi Park, HERP Varanasi; and FSIP Jagdishpur. BHEL’s Koradi site organised a medical camp to promote health and well-being. At FGD Korba Site, cleaning and housekeeping staff were felicitated and presented with awards for their role in maintaining clean surroundings.

HERP Varanasi                                              HPEP Hyderabad                                           FSIP Jagdishpur

Andrew Yule & Co Ltd. (AYCL) organized Health Check-up Camp at the Tea Gardens in Assam and West Bengal for Tea Garden Workers and Safai Mitras. The Safai Mitra engaged at the registered office were felicitated for their contribution to maintain workplace cleanliness.

Health Check-up Camp by AYCL at the Tea Gardens in Assam and West Bengal

Cement Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL) undertook cleanliness and workspace improvement activities at Rajban Unit, including the removal of unused materials, office equipment and minor repairs. Tree plantation drives were also conducted at Bokajan Unit to promote green cover and environmental sustainability.

E-waste: Obsolete electronic equipment, electrical items, batteries and scrap machinery parts were identified, segregated and collected at CCIL

Engineering Projects (India) Ltd. (EPIL) organised a tree plantation and cleanliness drive at Government School, Nilakantha Nagar, Nayapalli, Odisha, with student participation. The drive included plantation activities and cleaning of over 1,200 sq. ft. of the school playground, promoting environmental sustainability and cleanliness.

EPIL organised a tree plantation and cleanliness drive at Government School, Nilakantha Nagar, Nayapalli, Odisha

Instrumentation Limited (IL), Palakkad, undertook a special Swachhata drive covering office and common areas, including painting and rearrangement of workspaces to enhance the working environment and optimise space utilisation. A health check-up camp was also organised for employees to promote preventive healthcare and overall well-being under Special Campaign 6.

A damaged and unused room was renovated and repurposed into a functional office space at Instrumentation Limited (IL), Palakkad

The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) carried-out cleanliness drives across offices, laboratories, workshops and other premises. A tree plantation drive was also organised, with 20 native medicinal saplings planted. Further, a health check-up camp was organised for Safai Mitras and supporting staff. Under the Waste to Wealth initiative, a miniature artillery gun system was created using discarded and scrap materials, promoting resource recovery, recycling and environmental sustainability.

   Artistic Sculpture Created from recycled materials by ARAI    Bellow Man made from valve, bellows and flanges by FCRI

Fluid Control Research Institute (FCRI) undertook various activities including segregation of unused items and clearing of space at the High Pressure Air Flow Test Facility, along with tree plantation near the Oil Flow Test Facility. A decorative item was also created from scrap materials such as valve bodies, bellows and flanges and displayed near the staff canteen, promoting creativity and the principles of waste-to-wealth.

E-waste: Computers, printers and laboratory equipment were identified and segregated FCRI

Further, many other cleanliness campaigns, plantation drives, health camps, E-waste

management activities, waste to wealth initiative etc.  events have been conducted by other CPSEs/ABs under MHI.

MHI and its CPSEs/ABs are committed to conduct various other events in the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6.
