item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
10th National Convention of Agrivision–2026 held in New Delhi
Indian Agriculture Must Move Beyond a Production-Centric Approach Towards Agri-Food Value Chains: Dr. M. L. Jat
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

The 10th National Convention of Agrivision–2026 is being held on October 13th –14th at the ICAR–NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi, under the aegis of Agrivision, the ICAR Agricultural Education Division. As the 10th national convention of Agrivision, the event marks a significant milestone and has brought together a broad cross-section of the agricultural community. Around 450 students from agriculture and allied sciences, representing 25 states, are participating alongside eminent speakers, scientists, senior officials of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), agricultural entrepreneurs and farmers.

The inaugural session was attended by Chief Guest Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and Director General, ICAR. Other dignitaries included Dr Y. S. Malik, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Education), Dr Anupam Mishra, Vice-Chancellor, Central Agricultural University, Imphal; Dr A. K. Singh, Vice-Chancellor, Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University.

Addressing the gathering, Dr M. L. Jat emphasised that Indian agriculture must move beyond a narrowly production-centric approach and adopt a broader agri-food system and value-chain perspective. He highlighted the importance of market research and market intelligence, aligning production with market demand, and improving farmer profitability. His address underscored the need to connect agricultural production with marketing and value addition.

Dr Anupam Mishra and Dr A. K. Singh appreciated Agrivision’s activities and encouraged students to pursue entrepreneurship, innovation and employment generation in agriculture. They also highlighted the importance of opportunities in teaching, research and extension.

The convention aims to create a meaningful interface between students, eminent scientists, senior officials, entrepreneurs and farmers, enabling the exchange of ideas and experiences across the agricultural value chain. Deliberations focus on agricultural education, technological transformation, research, market-oriented agriculture, entrepreneurship and farmer-centric development.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
FACULTY AND COURSE MEMBERS OF 66TH NATIONAL DEFENCE COLLEGE COURSE CALL ON THE PRESIDENT
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi

The faculty and course members of the 66th National Defence College Course called on the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (October 13, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the security and technological landscapes are changing rapidly, bringing new and complex challenges. These developments call for greater preparedness, strategic foresight and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances. Fast decision-making mechanism is also becoming more important because the techniques of modern warfare have expanded into cyber security, space technology, and biotechnology apart from the traditional domains.

The President said that today, national security extends beyond military capabilities. It requires close cooperation between scientific institutions and the armed forces to translate innovation into practical solutions. Recent conflicts have highlighted the importance of cost-effective technologies that complement advanced defence systems and make the best use of available resources. She underlined the importance of government initiatives such as the Research, Development and Innovation Scheme, for strengthening the link between innovation and national security.

The President said that the use of Artificial Intelligence in various domains of science, national security and economic activities is increasing. She said that decision making cannot be outsourced exclusively to this technology and emphasised the need for a balanced approach.

The President underlined that economic resilience is an integral part of national security framework. She said that Indian economy has demonstrated its capabilities to absorb disruptions created by external factors. India has accomplished this without compromising the strategic freedom of action.

Please click here to see the President’s speech

Ministry of Defence
RRM to Attend Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference 2026 of NCC in Guwahati
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Special Joint State Representatives and Additional Director General’s Conference of National Cadet Corps led by Director General NCC, Lt. General Virendra Vats, will be held in Guwahati on October 15, 2026 to deliberate on issues concerning the NCC in the North Eastern Region (NER), West Bengal and Sikkim. The conference will be chaired by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth and will bring together senior representatives from the Ministry of Defence, NCC and the State Governments of the participating States.

The conference will focus on key issues relating to the expansion of NCC, cadet welfare, training, institutional strengthening and administrative challenges. It will also provide a platform for enhanced coordination between the NCC and State Governments to explore collaborative initiatives for increasing the reach, effectiveness and impact of the organisation.

The NCC plays a significant role in youth development, nation-building and community engagement through its Social Service and Community Development (SSCD) activities. With a presence in more than 99% of districts across India, it continues to contribute to the development of disciplined, responsible and motivated citizens. It functions under the shared responsibilities of the Central and State Governments.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
MCL strengthens E-Waste Management Across Its Establishments under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) has joined the nation in observing Special campaign 6 and is undertaking significant initiatives to promote responsible e-waste management across its Headquarters and operational areas. Special campaign 6 will be observed till 31st October 2026 focusing on systematic waste collection, environmental awareness and promotion of cleanliness across all MCL establishments.

As part of the drive, e-waste collection kiosks are set up across MCL areas to facilitate the collection and responsible disposal of discarded electronic items through authorised recycling channels. Employees at the Headquarters and operational areas are enthusiastically participating in the campaign, contributing to cleanliness initiatives and promoting environmentally responsible practices.

Awareness activities are also being conducted to sensitise employees and nearby communities about the harmful effects of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and associated risks to human health and the environment.

In the first week of implementation phase of the campaign, MCL cleaned 73 sites out of the 240 identified sites, cleaning an area of 3,06,663 sqft against the target area of 10,00,000 sqft. The campaign also targets the disposal of 600 metric tonnes of scrap, while 350 HEMM batteries have been disposed of generating revenue through scrap disposal.

Through Special Campaign 6, MCL is reinforcing its commitment to workplace cleanliness, environmental protection and responsible e-waste management supporting the national objective of a cleaner, more sustainable and resource-efficient future.

L. Jat ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, Organises Soybean Harvest Day; Scientific Analysis of Yield Data to Assess Potential for Productivity Enhancement Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi The ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Improved Soybean Varieties NRC 268 and NRC 270 Show Promising Signs of Yielding 20 Quintals per Hectare Despite Adverse Weather Conditions
Compilation of yield data to help assess future productivity gains: Dr. M. L. Jat
ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, Organises Soybean Harvest Day; Scientific Analysis of Yield Data to Assess Potential for Productivity Enhancement
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi

The ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), organised a Soybean Harvest Day on 9 October 2026. On this occasion, the yield potential of the improved soybean Varieties NRC 268 and NRC 270, developed by the Institute, was assessed. Preliminary data obtained after harvesting one acre each under the two varieties indicate encouraging yields of approximately 20 quintals per hectare. This assessment is important for understanding the performance of improved varieties under adverse weather conditions and evaluating the potential for enhancing soybean productivity in the country. At present, the average soybean productivity in India is approximately 10–11 quintals per hectare.

Research and trials conducted across the country by ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute and under the All India Coordinated Research Project on Soybean indicate that yields of 15–20 quintals per hectare can be achieved by adopting improved varieties and appropriate production technologies. Under favourable conditions, yields may potentially reach approximately 22–25 quintals per hectare.

Appreciating these preliminary findings, Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), said that improved varieties and scientific production technologies play a significant role in enhancing soybean productivity in the country. He stated that the indications of yields of approximately 20 quintals per hectare from NRC 200 68 and NRC 200 70, despite adverse weather conditions this year, were highly encouraging. He further emphasised that the scientific analysis of these data would help guide future research strategies aimed at increasing soybean productivity.

The Director of ICAR–National Soybean Research Institute, Indore, stated that the significance of the data collected during Soybean Harvest Day extends beyond assessing the yield of a single year. Systematic collection and analysis of data over several years will help understand changes in productivity across different regions, varieties and production conditions. This will provide a scientific basis for assessing annual improvements in productivity and estimating the potential for future yield enhancement. Long-term data will also be useful in evaluating the effectiveness of research and technology dissemination efforts.

The Institute regularly organises such events to assess the actual yield potential of different soybean varieties, understand the impact of improved technologies, and disseminate information on high-yielding varieties and scientific production practices to farmers. This initiative will help strengthen coordination among soybean research, agricultural extension services and the dissemination of scientific knowledge to farmers.

The primary objective of the Soybean Harvest Day was to assess the yield potential of improved varieties and establish a scientific basis for enhancing productivity through the systematic collection of yield data. The data obtained from the harvest will be analysed further to develop a better understanding of varietal performance and the influence of different production conditions.

item.title: New technology provides environment friendly route for treating dye-contaminated wastewater
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology New technology provides environment friendly route for treating dye-contaminated wastewater Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi A sustainable, multifunctional machine learning enabled filter for wastewater treatment, developed by integrating green-synthesized zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles with biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) nanofibers, assisted by machine learning can provide an environment friendly route for treating dye-contaminated wastewater. The discharge of persistent organic dyes from industrial activities,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
New technology provides environment friendly route for treating dye-contaminated wastewater
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi

A sustainable, multifunctional machine learning enabled filter for wastewater treatment, developed by integrating green-synthesized zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles with biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) nanofibers, assisted by machine learning can provide an environment friendly route for treating dye-contaminated wastewater.

The discharge of persistent organic dyes from industrial activities, particularly the textile industry, represents an important environmental challenge because these compounds can be stable, toxic, and resistant to natural degradation. The research addresses the need for sustainable wastewater-treatment technologies.

Existing wastewater-treatment approaches such as adsorption, sedimentation and flocculation can separate pollutants but do not necessarily destroy them. Biological treatment can also be slow for highly stable dyes. Photocatalysis offers an attractive alternative because it can degrade pollutants under relatively mild conditions while using renewable energy.

However, conventional photocatalytic systems face several challenges: recovery of nanoparticle catalysts; separation of catalysts from treated water; electron-hole recombination; dependence on light availability; and the requirement for efficient catalyst-pollutant contact.

To tackle this challenge, a new technology developed by the Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST) Mohali, autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) immobilised ZnO (zinc oxide prepared from natural sources) within porous PLA nanofibers and introduced mechanical excitation along with light. The mechanical vibrations generated piezoelectric polarization, which suppressed photogenerated electron–hole recombination and enhanced reactive-species formation. The work was published in the journal Advanced Functional Materials (Wiley).

Fig 1: Schematic illustration of green-synthesized, highly crystalline ZnO nanoparticles using turmeric powder.

Dr. Aviru Kumar Basu’s lab synthesised ZnO nanoparticles using turmeric extract, where naturally occurring bioactive compounds like curcumin, flavonoids and phenolic compounds acted as reducing and stabilizing agents, avoiding conventional synthesis routes involving harmful reagents.

The fabrication of PLA-ZnO nanofibers through electrospinning, produced a porous, high-surface-area and mechanically stable catalytic membrane rather than using ZnO as a freely dispersed powder. The integration of photocatalysis and piezocatalysis enabled pollutant degradation using both light and mechanical vibrations.

The PLA-ZnO nanofibers achieved 98.6% MB and 96.7% CR decolorization within 120 min under combined light and ultrasonic excitation. This new material also demonstrated antibacterial activity, achieving approximately 75% inactivation of E. coli and 71% of S. aureus after 6 h. Machine learning (ML) was integrated with the experimental study to predict dye-decolorization behaviour from parameters such as wavelength, time, catalyst amount, ultrasonic frequency, light intensity and dye concentration.

Fig 2: Schematic of PLA-ZnO nanofiber preparation using the e-spin method.

The developed PLA-ZnO nanofibers can be used for the treatment of wastewater containing persistent organic dyes and microbial contaminants, particularly those associated with textile and industrial effluents for cleaner and safer water. They can also be used for Photocatalytic and piezocatalytic environmental remediation as well as for antibacterial water-treatment membranes.

Publication link: https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.77852

These provisions offer a one-time opportunity for regularisation of exemption status of Provident Fund (PF) Trusts that are recognized under the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Retrospective regularization of exempt status of Provident Fund (PF) Trusts through Amnesty Scheme, 2026
EPFO steps up nationwide drive and reminds eligible establishments as deadline of 28 December approaches
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 2:37PM by PIB Delhi

Provisions for Amnesty were introduced as a transitional measure in the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme 2026, notified on 29.06.2026. These provisions offer a one-time opportunity for regularisation of exemption status of Provident Fund (PF) Trusts that are recognized under the Income Tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961), but lack a formal exemption order granted under section 17 of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions (EPF&MP) Act, 1952 or section 143 of the Code on Social Security (CoSS), 2020.

The operational guidelines for Amnesty, including the manner of application and procedural requirements, were detailed in the circular issued on 11.07.2026. The Amnesty window remains open for a period of six (6) months from the date of notification, expiring on 28.12.2026. With less than three months remaining before the deadline, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is urging eligible establishments pan-India to expedite their submissions. Besides retrospective regularisation of exempt status, key benefits under the scheme include waivers of statutory requirements under the CoSS, 2020—such as minimum employee headcount, corpus size, and the 3-year compliance rule—along with complete operational flexibility postregularisation to comply either as an exempt or an unexempt establishment.

To ensure maximum awareness, EPFO has rolled out extensive multi-channel initiatives across the country. Strategic meetings and seminars have been conducted in collaboration with apex industry and market bodies, including the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). Chartered Accountants and statutory auditors have been specifically engaged to identify and assist qualifying PF Trusts. In parallel, EPFO Zonal and Regional Offices pan-India have organized nationwide seminars and workshops to engage directly with local establishments, employers, and trust members, supported by multi-media campaigns, social media outreach, and explanatory infographics simplifying procedural compliance guidelines.

To support applicants effectively, the Exemption Division (Head Office) has conducted dedicated hybrid training programs for EPFO field officials posted across the country. In addition, dual-track institutional and employer training has been carried out both through online modules and physically at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS) for departmental officers and employers alike.

Furthermore, EPFO has actively coordinated with the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue / Income Tax Department) to institutionalize data sharing of exempted establishment records. This data integration focuses on identifying, cross-verifying, and bringing unnotified or non-compliant PF trusts under the statutory umbrella, while ensuring that tax-recognized trusts without formal EPFO exemption orders regularize their status promptly. EPFO Regional Offices nationwide continue active follow-ups to facilitate the submission of regularisation applications within the stipulated timeframe.

Eligible PF Trusts across India are advised to avail of this one-time opportunity to enable continuance of income tax benefits available to trusts recognized by the Income tax department.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Ministry of Education, constitutes Three Member Committee to examine student death at IIIT, Ranchi
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Education has taken cognizance of the unfortunate death of a student at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Ranchi campus. In order to examine the circumstances and related issues in detail, a three-member committee headed and chaired by Prof. Rajni Abbi, Director, South Campus, University of Delhi, along with a senior psychiatrist and a senior officer from the Ministry of Education, as Members has been constituted. Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Ranchi is a Public Private Partnership Institute established under the (PPP Mode).

The Committee has been mandated to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and assess the implementation of the Guidelines, with particular reference to the availability and functioning of basic facilities, institutional support systems, counselling and mentoring arrangements, and student grievance redressal mechanisms. It will identify any systemic gaps and recommend appropriate measures to strengthen student well-being and help prevent the recurrence of such incidents. The Committee shall interact with stakeholders and examine relevant records and documents as required.

The Ministry is undertaking suitable interim administrative arrangements to ensure the smooth and effective functioning of the Institute, keeping in view the interests and well-being of the students.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister and CM (NCT Delhi) review Air Pollution Mitigation measures at Anand Vihar Hotspot and visit DPCC’s AI-enabled ICCC facility at Shastri Park
Dignitaries inaugurate EV Charging Stations; Flag off 150 Electric Buses; and Inaugurate 13 new CAAQMS in Delhi
Shri Bhupender Yadav congratulates Delhi Government for boosting E-mobility, containing Air Pollution at Anand Vihar Hotspot, augmenting CAAQMS grid and connecting to ICCC for improved Air Quality Monitoring
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:53PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with Chief Minister (NCT Delhi), Smt. Rekha Gupta, today undertook a detailed on-ground review of the air pollution mitigation measures being undertaken by Government of NCT Delhi at the major hotspot of Anand Vihar. The dignitaries also visited the AI-enabled Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) of the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) at Shastri Park.

During the review, the dignitaries virtually inaugurated public EV charging stations at ISBT Anand Vihar, Nand Nagri depot, Rohini Sector-37 depot, Nangloi depot and Keshopur depot in Delhi, along with flagging-off 150 new electric buses at Swami Vivekanand ISBT, Anand Vihar. The Ministers also inaugurated 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) installed by DPCC across Delhi. Other dignitaries present on the occasion included Sardar Manjinder Singh Sirsa, Minister for Environment, Forest & Wildlife (GNCTD), Dr. Pankaj Kumar Singh, Minister for Transport (GNCTD), Shri Harsh Malhotra, Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), East Delhi and Union MoS (Road Transport and Highways), besides senior officials from the Union and NCT Delhi Governments.

Under the Sewa Sankalp Abhiyaan, flagged off 150 electric buses today at Anand Vihar, Delhi, along with Chief Minister Smt. @gupta_rekha ji and Delhi Environment Minister Shri @mssirsa ji. Also virtually inaugurated public EV charging stations at five locations, strengthening Delhi’s clean mobility infrastructure. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, India is advancing towards a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future. These initiatives reflect our collective commitment to reducing emissions, promoting electric mobility and building a Viksit Bharat that grows in harmony with nature.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) October 13, 2026

During the visit to Anand Vihar ISBT, the Ministers were informed that Anand Vihar had become a major air pollution hotspot area due to traffic congestion, traffic of commuting buses at bus terminal, road dust along roadsides, road dust emanating from rom unpaved roads and roadsides, potholes, unpaved parking and incomplete paving of the terminal, construction and demolition activities, garbage and plastic dumping, along with open burning of waste.

Detailing the air pollution mitigation measures undertaken at the hotspot, Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav informed the media that short term and long term actions were assigned to 11 agencies. Internal roads have been paved, encroachment has been removed, construction activities followed green netting and dust control measures, illegal C&D waste dumping has been removed and traffic congestion has been removed. Long term measures such as greening activities are being taken up at the location. He highlighted that with the concerted efforts from various departments of Delhi, the persistent issue of air pollution at this hotspot has now been contained.

The dignitaries then visited the AI-enabled Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) of the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) at Shastri Park. The ICCC is designed to serve as a unified digital platform integrating data on air quality, dust-control sites, ambient noise levels, industrial emissions, stubble-burning incidents, citizen grievances, and enforcement vehicles, thereby enabling real-time monitoring, data-driven decision-making, and coordinated enforcement actions across agencies. The ICCC is designed to integrate 15 external data systems, of which 9 have been integrated and the remaining 6 are being connected in phases.

Visited the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) at Shastri Park and reviewed its operations along with Delhi Chief Minister Smt @gupta_rekha ji and Environment Minister Shri @mssirsa ji. We also inaugurated 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) to enable accurate monitoring of PM2.5 and PM10 levels. The Delhi Government has established the new Integrated Command and Control Centre to ensure close monitoring of every pollution hotspot and swift action on every issue. Equipped with AI-powered cameras, real-time data and GPS technology, the centre monitors pollution control measures round the clock. Under the leadership of PM Shri @narendramodi ji, we are working on mission mode to tackle every major source of pollution.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) October 13, 2026

During the visit, the Union Environment Minister and CM (NCT Delhi) virtually inaugurated 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) installed by DPCC across Delhi. These are located at SKV Ghummanhera, GBSSS Chhawla, GBSSS Karala, GGSSS Hastsal, GBSSS Jharoda Kalan, DJB Ghoga, DJB Burari, DTL Tikri Kalan, NIH Narela, AIIMS-CAPFIMS Maidan Garhi, Maharaja Surajmal Stadium Nangloi, Maharaja Agrasen College Vasundhara Enclave and ljiNTPC Eco Park Badarpur. These stations will provide continuous, time-resolved air quality and meteorological data to support scientific assessment, regulatory enforcement and public dissemination of AQI.

Briefing the media on the occasion, Shri Yadav informed that in addition to the existing population-based norms, air quality monitoring stations have now been installed at one station per 25 sq km (5 km × 5 km grid) in Delhi, and this grid would be expanded further in other NCR cities. It was added that coverage in peri-urban and suburban areas is critical for assessing the inflow and outflow of pollution. It was highlighted that Delhi had 47 existing CAAQMS operated by various agencies namely, DPCC, CPCB, IMD, IITM and MoHUA. The Minister informed that with the addition of 13 new CAAQMS, the network has now been expanded to 60 stations providing realtime air quality data through CPCB server as well as SAMEER mobile app.

Shri Yadav congratulated the Chief Minister, GNCTD and officials of Delhi Government for augmenting the public transport through E-mobility, eliminating the Anand Vihar Air Pollution Hotspot area through coordinated efforts and inaugurating the new CAAQMS and connecting to ICCC for improved air quality monitoring.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance NLMC’s first end-to-end e-auction of RINL land parcels generates ₹366.33 Crore in successful bids on Day 1, 150 plots sold Highest auction price crosses ₹1.80 lakh per square yard, reflecting strong market demand Second Phase of RINL e-auction on October 30th Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, successfully conducted Day 1 of the e-auction of premium land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
NLMC’s first end-to-end e-auction of RINL land parcels generates ₹366.33 Crore in successful bids on Day 1, 150 plots sold
Highest auction price crosses ₹1.80 lakh per square yard, reflecting strong market demand
Second Phase of RINL e-auction on October 30th
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, successfully conducted Day 1 of the e-auction of premium land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity operating Visakhapatnam Steel Plant. The first phase marks a significant milestone for NLMC, as it is the Corporation’s first end-to-end e-auction, demonstrating a structured, transparent and technology-driven approach towards monetising surplus public assets.

Of the land parcels offered in the first phase, 150 plots were successfully sold, generating a total successful bid value of ₹366.33 crore against an aggregate reserve price of ₹312.48 crore. The successful bids recorded an average premium of 17.23% over the reserve price, reflecting encouraging market participation and interest in the properties on offer.

The auction also recorded significant price realisation, with the highest auction price crossing ₹1.80 lakh per square yard. This strong price discovery reflects robust market demand for well-located land parcels in Visakhapatnam. It underscores the role of a transparent and competitive e-auction process in unlocking the economic potential of public assets.

The auction is being facilitated by NLMC in coordination with RINL, with Quikr India Private Limited (QIPL) serving as the Transaction Consultant. The online bidding process is being conducted through RailTel’s E-Nivida platform.

The e-auction forms part of the broader effort to facilitate the productive utilisation of surplus land assets held by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other government entities. Through a structured and market-driven process, NLMC works with asset-owning organisations to bring identified properties to the market, encourage participation from prospective buyers and support transparent value discovery.

Ahead of the auction, NLMC and RINL undertook investor outreach activities in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Hyderabad during September 2026. These meetings provided prospective bidders with an opportunity to understand the properties on offer, seek clarifications and familiarise themselves with the participation process.

The outreach programme also helped address queries relating to registration, documentation, Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) requirements and online bidding. These efforts were aimed at widening awareness, facilitating bidder participation and ensuring that interested buyers had access to relevant information before participating in the e-auction.

The successful outcome of Day 1 of the RINL land e-auction marks an important step in NLMC’s efforts to facilitate transparent and competitive monetisation of public assets. The response to the auction demonstrates the potential of well-structured market processes to attract investor interest and support value realisation from surplus government assets.

Final Opportunity to Own Land in Visakhapatnam: Second Phase of RINL E-Auction on October 30 -

Following the encouraging response to the first phase, the second and final phase of the e-auction offers prospective buyers another opportunity to acquire land parcels in key locations of Visakhapatnam. The second phase will cover the remaining 216 land parcels and has been rescheduled to October 30, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM. As this is the final phase of the current auction, interested buyers are encouraged to review the available plots and complete their registration within the prescribed timeline. The first-phase results provide prospective bidders with an indication of market participation and price discovery, making this an important opportunity for those looking to explore land ownership in Visakhapatnam.

Interested bidders must complete their registration by October 27, 2026. Details of the available land parcels, reserve prices, eligibility conditions and participation requirements can be accessed on the official e-auction portal: https://eauction.enivida.com/.

Prospective buyers are encouraged to review the available information, undertake due diligence and complete the necessary formalities before the deadline to participate in the final phase of the auction.

About NLMC

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a Government of India company under the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. It facilitates the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other government agencies. NLMC works in coordination with asset-owning organisations to support the structured identification, preparation and monetisation of such assets through transparent and market-oriented processes.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri holds bilateral talks with 1st Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Industry & Trade of Czech Republic
Both sides agree to expand defence industrial collaboration
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh held a bilateral meeting with 1st Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Industry and Trade of Czech Republic Mr Karel Havlíček in New Delhi on October 13, 2026. During the interaction, both leaders reviewed the entire spectrum of defence industrial cooperation between the two countries. While the two sides welcomed the ongoing collaboration and successful establishment of various joint ventures, they agreed to further expand this cooperation, including under the aegis of India-Czech Joint Defence Committee to promote ‘Make-in-India' and ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’.

The two leaders also discussed the ongoing issues of peace & security and acknowledged the need for greater cooperation to maintain regional stability. They reiterated that the partnership between India and the Czech Republic is based on historical & cultural ties, and shared values of mutual trust & respect.

Mr Karel Havlíček is on a four-day visit to India and is interacting with various Ministries, Trades and Businesses. He is scheduled to visit various industries in Bengaluru and Mumbai during his stay.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Celebrating Uttarakhand’s Spiritual Heritage at the 8th edition of PM Mementos e-Auction
27 mementos reflect the state’s sacred landmarks, folk traditions and regional identity
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

Uttarakhand’s identity as Devbhoomi, the land of the gods, finds expression in a collection of 27 mementos featured in the eighth edition of the PM Mementos e-auction. These gifts presented to the Prime Minister include framed artworks, photo prints, temple models and other keepsakes. They reflect the close connection between faith, art and cultural landscape. Proceeds from the auction support the Namami Gange Programme.

Four temple models represent some of Uttarakhand’s revered places of worship. These include two models of Shri Kedarnath Dham, a model of Omkareshwar Temple at Ukhimath and a wooden model of Ganga Ji Mandir at Mukhba. Together, they reflect the importance of pilgrimage and devotion in the state’s cultural life.

 

 

A photo print brings together the four Char Dham shrines: Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. A framed image of Mansa Devi in Haridwar, a view of Adi Kailash, a representation of Mahasu Devta Temple and an LED-lit glass memento featuring Kartik Swami Temple add to this sacred landscape. A print featuring Narayan Ashram and the Kumaon Himalayas captures the mountain surroundings that shape the region’s spiritual character.

Faith also finds expression through the region’s folk art. Aipan art appears on a wall clock and in an artwork depicting Maa Durga. These pieces reflect the place of religious imagery in local artistic traditions. Seven Uttarakhandi/Pahari caps add a familiar expression of the state’s regional identity.

 

 

The collection also includes a badminton racket signed by Uttarakhand’s Lakshya Sen. It represents sporting achievement within an ensemble shaped largely by the state’s religious and cultural heritage.

The model of Ganga Ji Mandir at Mukhba connects this heritage with the purpose of the PM Mementos initiative. It reflects the Ganga’s place in Uttarakhand’s spiritual life, while proceeds from the auction support the river’s rejuvenation and conservation through the Namami Gange.

The 8th edition of PM Mementos is currently live and has been extended until 31. Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in

Freight loading during the first six months of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Registers 6.14% Growth in Freight Loading in September 2026 over September 2025
Food Grain Loading Grows by 25%, Clinker by 20% and Domestic Container by 10%
Cumulative Freight Loading during April-September 2026 Rises 4.1% over the Corresponding Period Last Year
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 1:00PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways recorded continued growth in freight and passenger segments during September 2026, with higher freight loading, and growth across several key commodity categories. Freight loading during the first six months of the financial year also registered sustained growth, reflecting continued demand for rail transportation across major sectors of the economy.

Freight Loading Registers 6.14% Growth

Indian Railways loaded 135.35 million tonnes of freight in September 2026, compared to 127.52 million tonnes in September 2025, registering a 6.14 per cent growth over the corresponding month last year.

Several major commodity segments recorded strong growth during the month. Food Grain loading grew by 25 per cent, Clinker by 20 per cent, Domestic Container by 10 per cent, Coal by 9 per cent, Balance Other Goods by 8.2 per cent, Mineral Oil by 6 per cent, Finished Steel by 5.5 per cent and Iron Ore by 5.2 per cent.

Coal Supply to Power Houses Strengthened

Indian Railways stepped up domestic coal supply to power houses during September 2026. The average number of coal rakes supplied per day increased to 443 rakes, compared to 397 rakes per day in September 2025, registering a 11.6 per cent growth.

Freight revenue during September 2026 increased by ₹1,266 crore over September 2025, registering a 9.3 per cent growth.

Cumulative Freight Loading Crosses 833 Million Tonnes

On a cumulative basis, Indian Railways loaded 833.7 million tonnes of freight during April-September 2026, registering 4.1 per cent growth over the corresponding period last year. Freight revenue during the same period recorded 3.7 per cent growth.

***

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Manik Sharma

item.title: Industrial Pollution Abatement: Sustainability through Regulations under Namami Gange
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Jal Shakti
item.description: Ministry of Jal Shakti Industrial Pollution Abatement: Sustainability through Regulations under Namami Gange Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:44PM by PIB Delhi Industrial pollution abatement is emerging as a key pillar river rejuvenation, with regulation increasingly evolving from conventional enforcement to continuous compliances, scientific monitoring, cleaner production, resource efficiency and technological improvement. Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Industrial Pollution Abatement: Sustainability through Regulations under Namami Gange
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:44PM by PIB Delhi

Industrial pollution abatement is emerging as a key pillar river rejuvenation, with regulation increasingly evolving from conventional enforcement to continuous compliances, scientific monitoring, cleaner production, resource efficiency and technological improvement.

Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs), independent technical assessments, implementing sector-specific Charters, monitoring of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), targeted action plans and sustained regulatory follow-up. Together, these interventions are creating a more accountable and sustainable pathway for industries to reduce pollution while improving water and resource efficiency.

From periodic inspection to continuous compliance

A major intervention has been the establishment of an Annual Inspection mechanism for GPIs, which commenced in 2017 with support of CPCB, the National Regulatory Authority. The programme focusses on 100% inspection of GPIs in the Ganga basin, through third party agencies e.g., technical institutes of national importance and online submission of inspection reports through mobile applications/web portals to enhance efficacy and transparency. For the 2026 inspection cycle, 40 technical institutes have been nominated to participate in the inspection process.

The scale of this monitoring framework has expanded considerably since 2017. In the 2025 inspection cycle, 3,703 GPIs were assessed (1,296 GPIs in the Ganga basin and 2,407 GPIs in the Yamuna basin). The exercise covered 113 districts across six States and one Union Territory, with the GPIs having potential to discharge into 46 tributaries and sub-tributaries of the Ganga and Yamuna.

The inspections go beyond visual assessment. The prescribed methodology includes studying the compliance of the industries against ‘Consent to Operate’ issued by State regulators (State Pollution Control Board) to the individual Industries, sampling from ETP inlets, outlets and aeration tanks, assessment of flow, pH, BOD, COD, TSS and TDS, verification of OCEMS connectivity, examination of recipient drains and water bodies, groundwater assessment, checks for any bypasses and ZLD profiling wherever applicable. Cases involving bypasses, multiple discharge points or defunct/non-existent/non-operational ETPs/ GPIs are reported with geo-tagged photographic or videographic evidence in the portal itself.

Regulation delivering measurable results

The progressive assessment of GPIs demonstrates the impact of sustained regulatory intervention. Across the assessed GPIs, compliance increased from 39% in 2017 to 70% in 2025, while the number of operational GPIs stood at 3,154 in 2025 increasing from 888 in 2017. During the same period, BOD load declined from 26 TPD (2017) to 12.02 TPD (2025), reflecting a substantial reduction in pollution load.

 

 

The Ganga basin has exhibited a progressive trend from 2017 to 2025, with compliance rising from 39% in 2017 to 86% in 2025. BOD load declined from 26 TPD to 7.16 TPD, representing a 72.46% reduction, while effluent discharge declined from 349 MLD to 274.88 MLD, a reduction of 21.24%.

 

 

The GPI Inspection further recorded that, among 3,145 operational GPIs, 2,715 were compliant, while non-compliant operational GPIs stood at 448, accounting for approximately 14% of operational GPIs. The regulatory process for non-compliant GPIs includes issuance of Show Cause Notices and closure action by State regulators (SPCBs), as applicable.

Thus, regulation is functioning not merely as an enforcement mechanism, but as a continuous self-improvement mechanism—inspection, identification, corrective action and follow-up.

Independent Technical Institutions: adding scientific rigour

A distinctive feature is the involvement of independent technical institutions in industrial inspections. The 2025 exercise engaged 25 technical institutes, while 40 institutes have been nominated for the 2026 cycle. The prescribed inspection team includes at least two experts from a technical institute, a SPCB officer alongwith the participation from State Mission for Clean Ganga/District Ganga Committees.

This model brings guidance from scientific and sector-specific expertise into regulatory oversight for technological or processes improvement in GPIs for pollution and resources reduction with overall improvement in efficiency and compliance to the norms. It also enables inspection findings to be supported by laboratory analysis, OCEMS verification, field observations and geo-tagged evidence, thereby strengthening the credibility and effectiveness of compliance assessment.

Sector-specific Charters: from pollution control to pollution prevention

The regulatory framework has also expanded upstream - from treating pollution after it is generated to preventing pollution at source. Sector-specific Charters have been developed for Pulp & Paper, Sugar, Distillery, Textile and Tannery sectors. These five sectors collectively represented around 70% of GPIs in the Ganga basin and 88% of the total pollution load in the earlier assessment.

The Charter for Water Recycling and Pollution Prevention Industries specifically seeks to optimise water and chemical use, reduce freshwater consumption and wastewater generation, improve effluent treatment and promote reuse and recycling, with the ultimate objective of preventing discharge of untreated effluent into recipient river streams.

The Charter establishes measurable targets, including reduction in water consumption, ETP/RO upgradation and, in the longer term, recycling of water against total input. It also explicitly envisages third-party involvement in planning, assessment, design and monitoring of process technologies and ETP upgradation, bringing regulators, technical institutions, research organisations and industry stakeholders together.

Targeted action for high pollution-load industries

Targeted interventions have also been undertaken for industries contributing significantly to pollution load. In 2022, 246 GPIs were identified as top contributors requiring priority action. To address their pollution load, 17 sector-specific workshops were conducted, with 222 GPIs participating and submitting action plans. The remaining 24 GPIs were either closed or had shifted to dry operations.

The progress of these industries was assessed against short-, medium- and long-term goals. 173 GPIs achieved short-term goals, 141 achieved medium-term goals and 126 achieved long-term goals. An estimated 65% reduction in pollution load was recorded during 2022–23 compared with 2021–22, with the pollution load declining from 18.68 TPD to 6.381 TPD. Subsequently, 156 industries came out of the priority list, while 66 remained for priority action

CETPs: strengthening pollution control at industrial clusters

Industrial clusters often require a collective approach to effluent treatment. Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) provide a shared treatment facility for industries located within such clusters, enabling their wastewater to be treated collectively. CETPs therefore form an important component of industrial pollution abatement, particularly in industrial clusters.

In 2025, 41 CETPs were assessed across the Ganga and Yamuna main-stem States, of which 40 were operational. Their combined operational capacity stood at 514.53 MLD, with utilisation of 286.31 MLD, while 27 CETPs were complying with the prescribed requirements. The assessment also identified specific operational and technological gaps and enabled measures such as improvement in operation and maintenance, upgradation of treatment systems, introduction of biological treatment where required, improved functioning of Primary Effluent Treatment Plants and regular monitoring of outlet quality.

 

 

The assessment of CETPs has enabled specific interventions rather than one-size-fits-all approach. Measures include improvement in operation and maintenance, upgradation of treatment systems, introduction of biological treatment where required, improved operation of Primary Effluent Treatment Plants, regular outlet monitoring and cleaner chemical practices.

For textile clusters, recommended measures include adoption of a Chemical Management System, eco-friendly non-toxic chemicals and low-salt dyes. For tannery clusters, cleaner production measures, improved PETP treatment and mechanical desalting have been recommended.

Water conservation: turning treated wastewater into a resource

One of the important shifts has been the recognition of treated wastewater as a resource rather than merely a waste stream.

The Charter-based interventions have helped industries reduce specific freshwater consumption and wastewater generation through reuse and recycling. The latest assessment records substantial reductions across major sectors, alongside increased adoption of treatment and recycling technologies.

The Sugar sector, for instance, has witnessed a major improvement in resource efficiency. Between 2017 and 2025, freshwater consumption declined from 155 L/T cane to 58 L/T cane, wastewater discharge declined from 190 L/T cane to 136 L/T cane, and BOD discharge declined from 0.0065 kg/T cane to 0.0029 kg/T cane. The improvement has been supported by high-pressure boilers, Condensate Polishing Units, tertiary ETP upgradation, reuse of treated wastewater and other process improvements.

The Pulp & Paper sector has also recorded significant resource-efficiency gains. The latest assessment reports 60 recycled-fibre-based Pulp & Paper mills operating on Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD), along with estimated savings of 928.89 MLD of groundwater and corresponding energy conservation of 1,649.80 MW annually.

Present CETPs in industrial clusters of Ganga basin are designed with an approach of reuse of treated water by the member industrial units.

A new paradigm of sustainable industrial regulation

The impact of industrial pollution-control measures is reflected not only in compliance statistics but also in broader environmental outcomes.

The assessment records no black liquor discharge from Pulp & Paper mills, no effluent discharge from distilleries, no incidence of coloured water discharge and fish mortality, approximately 719 million litres of groundwater saved per day, and improved water quality in tributaries including Ramganga, Kosi, Dhela and Bahela.

The interventions have also contributed to around 1,277.6 MW/year of energy savings and an estimated 1,162.6 tonnes CO₂e reduction in carbon footprint.

Sustaining pollution abatement through regulation

The industrial pollution abatement journey under Namami Gange reflects an important evolution in environmental governance leading to the efficient compliance achievement.

The approach combines regulation with science, enforcement with facilitation, monitoring with technology and compliance with resource efficiency. Annual GPI inspections provide the regulatory backbone; independent technical institutions add scientific rigour; sector-specific Charters encourage cleaner production and water recycling; targeted action plans address high pollution-load industries; and CETP assessments strengthen pollution control at industrial clusters.

The numbers tell the story. In the 2025 assessment, 3,703 GPIs were covered, including 1,296 in the Ganga basin and 2,407 in the Yamuna basin. The Ganga basin has seen compliance rise from 39% in 2017 to 86% in 2025, alongside a 72.46% reduction in BOD load.

The objective is therefore no longer limited to ensuring that industries comply with prescribed norms. It is about creating an enduring culture of responsible production, water conservation, pollution prevention, reuse and recycling.

From regulation to responsibility, from monitoring to measurable outcomes, and from pollution control to sustainable production, industrial pollution abatement is becoming a sustained and integral part of the journey towards cleaner and healthier rivers.

***

ND/HM

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DARPG releases the 53rd Monthly Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for Central Ministries/ Departments performance for the month of September, 2026
A total of 2,38,579 grievances redressed by Central Ministries/ Departments in September, 2026.
For the 51st month in a row, the monthly disposal crossed 1 lakh cases in the Central Secretariat
Department of Posts, Department of Financial Services (Insurance Division) & Department of Telecommunications top the Group A category in the GRAI rankings released for the month of September, 2026
Ministry of Textiles, Ministry of Heavy Industries & Ministry of Tourism top in Group B category in the GRAI rankings released for the month of September, 2026
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) monthly report for September, 2026, which provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal. This is the 53rd report on Central Ministries/Departments published by DARPG.

The progress for September, 2026 indicates 2,38,579 Grievances redressed by Central Ministries/Departments. The Average Grievance Disposal Time in the Central Ministries/Departments for 2026 is 13 days. These reports are part of the 10-step CPGRAMS reform process which was adopted by DARPG to improve the quality of disposal and reduce the timelines.

The report provides the data for new users registered through the CPGRAMS Portal in the month of September, 2026. A total of 92,822 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in September, 2026, through various channels, out of which, the highest registrations are from Uttar Pradesh (17%). The Feedback collected from Call Centre and Online is 1,87,362 feedbacks in the month of September, 2026, where 1,11,794 feedbacks were collected for Central Ministries/Departments.

The report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in September, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 12,996 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of September, 2026.

The report also presents an overview of the Review Meeting Module, which has been operationalised on 14th September 2025 across Central Ministries and Departments. This module facilitates Secretary-level reviews of public grievances, thereby enhancing the efficiency of redressal mechanisms and improving citizen satisfaction. As of 30th September, 2026, a total of 454 review meetings have been conducted, out of which 27 meetings were held in September, 2026.

The following are the Key Highlights of the DARPG’s monthly CPGRAMS report for September, 2026 for Central Ministries/ Departments:

PG Cases:

  • In September 2026, 2,27,837 PG cases were received on the CPGRAMS portal, 2,38,579 PG cases were redressed and there exists a pendency of 85,687 PG cases.
  • Grievances registered via Common Service Centers stands at 12,996 grievances for September, 2026.
  • 35% of the accounted grievances for September, 2026 were directed towards key departments such as the Ministry of Labour and Employment [37,492 grievances]; Department of Financial Services (Banking Division) [31,968 grievances] and Ministry of Railways (Railway Board) [9,914 grievances]

PG Appeals:

  • In September 2026, 48,653 appeals were received and 42,116 appeals were disposed.
  • 23,230 appeal pendency recorded in September for the year 2026.

Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) – September, 2026

  • Department of Posts, Department of Financial Services (Insurance Division) and Department of Telecommunications are amongst the top performers in the Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index within the Group A (more than equal to 500 grievances) for September, 2026.
  • Ministry of Textiles, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Ministry of Tourism are amongst the top performers in Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index within the Group B (less than 500 grievances) for September, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum
The vision I have come with is power to empower; Beyond the power to control, power to enable; Beyond the power to compete, power to collaborate; Beyond the power to succeed, power to help others succeed: PM
Our constant endeavour is to ensure that India's capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well: PM
India's progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities: PM
We do not grow at anyone's cost; We grow with the world and for the world: PM
In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability: PM
For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction: PM
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today addressed the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. Acknowledging Mr. Michael Bloomberg’s earlier remarks, the Prime Minister celebrated the forum's unprecedented debut in India. He praised the platform's ability to unite the world’s brightest minds to deliberate on key global themes, including the economy, technology, energy, and international affairs. "I congratulate Mr. Bloomberg and his entire team; you have chosen the right place at the right time,” remarked Shri Modi.

Addressing the summit's core focus on emerging global powers, the Prime Minister highlighted a monumental paradigm shift in the 21st century's third decade, where technology, data, knowledge, and innovation have become the ultimate metrics of power. He challenged the audience to reconsider the fundamental purpose of this power, questioning whether it should elevate a select few or actively democratize opportunities for millions, emphasizing a shift from controlling to enabling and from competing to collaborating. '“Moving beyond the power to succeed to the power to help others succeed, the vision with which I have come here today is Power to Empower,” asserted Shri Modi.

Grounding this philosophy in ancient cultural wisdom, the Prime Minister quoted traditional Sanskrit texts emphasizing that the true value of knowledge, wealth, and power is determined entirely by how ethically they are utilized. He stressed that understanding this profound purpose of power is absolutely essential for navigating today’s complex global dynamics. "Meaning, the true value of Power lies in its Purpose,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Translating these ancient ideals into modern administration, the Prime Minister stated that the concept of 'Power to Empower' is not a mere global sermon but a deeply ingrained cultural tradition actively applied to the nation’s governance and work culture. He announced his intention to illustrate this transformative philosophy using concrete examples of the nation's progress. "Therefore, I will take my point forward using examples from India itself,” noted Shri Modi.

Showcasing the vibrant dynamism of the 'Mother of Democracy', the Prime Minister proudly listed the nation's massive linguistic diversity, its 80,000 publications, and over a thousand television channels. He emphasized that in the modern social media era, the nation's half-a-billion YouTube and Instagram users engage in robust, open debates, proving that digital power is actively fueling democratic discourse. "In present times, what has played a major role in this is digital power,” observed Shri Modi.

Recounting the aggressive battle against digital exclusion, the Prime Minister noted that just over a decade ago, mere access to mobile phones and the internet was considered an elite privilege. He explained that since 2014, the government deliberately slashed data prices down to ensure that everyone from small-town students to village shopkeepers could instantly access knowledge and markets. "Meaning, Connectivity in India has not just connected people; it has also connected opportunities,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the extraordinary scale of financial inclusion, the Prime Minister invited international guests to witness a seamless digital payments ecosystem where a humble street vendor and a massive car showroom utilize the exact same technological platform. He framed this radical financial democratization as the ultimate proof of inclusive technology at work. "This is the strength of Inclusive Technology,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing the nation's commitment to international technological solidarity, the Prime Minister declared that domestic digital capabilities are continuously shared with the Global South and other partner countries to help them build their own Digital Public Infrastructure. He cited the open-source CoWIN platform, deployed during the pandemic, as a prime example of domestic innovation actively unlocking global possibilities. "Meaning, our capability should empower humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.

Championing the massive democratization of innovation, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's explosive startup growth, which skyrocketed from a few hundred in 2014 to over 2.5 lakh today. He proudly pointed out that nearly half of these startups originate from smaller cities and that over 45 percent feature female leadership, proving that the power to solve problems is reaching all segments of society. "Meaning, opportunities for Innovation are reaching more people,” noted Shri Modi.

Pivoting to the core philosophy of public administration, the Prime Minister stated that governmental authority must never aim to create systemic dependency, but must instead focus on rendering citizens entirely capable and empowered. He credited this exact empowerment-driven governance model for successfully lifting 25 crore people out of poverty over the last decade. "And India is walking on this very path,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing the systemic eradication of corruption, the Prime Minister highlighted the deployment of the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer systems to deliver government assistance directly into citizens' bank accounts. "This has reduced corruption, increased the convenience of the country's citizens, and established a direct relationship between Government and Citizen,” observed Shri Modi.

Illustrating this empowerment philosophy on the global stage, the Prime Minister recalled the critical vaccine shortages during the COVID-19 pandemic and questioned whether life-saving manufacturing power should have been hoarded by a few nations. He expressed immense pride that the nation chose a humanitarian path by supplying vaccines to over 100 countries. "Our Manufacturing Capability became a medium of assistance for other countries as well,” asserted Shri Modi.

Presenting a unique example of inclusive foresight, the Prime Minister mentioned a recent domestic AI Impact summit that expanded the dialogue beyond human applications to actively discuss how artificial intelligence could benefit animal welfare. He used this anecdote to prove that an increasingly capable nation will continually generate broader benefits for the entire world. "The more capable India becomes, the more beneficial it will be for humanity, for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Calling for a balanced global order, the Prime Minister argued that while competition, innovation, and national strength are vital, they must be fundamentally paired with compassion and a commitment to solving global challenges like climate change, water governance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies. He insisted that the world desperately needs powers that actively create new, shared opportunities. "Power is not just the ability to move ahead; it is also the ability to empower others to move ahead,” asserted Shri Modi.

Demonstrating the nation's fierce commitment to climate action, the Prime Minister recalled the bold 2015 Paris Agreement pledge to achieve 40 percent installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030. He proudly announced that the nation surpassed this target in November 2021, nine years ahead of schedule, becoming the very first G20 country to do so. "This was not just about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a sign of India's changing Energy Journey,” noted Shri Modi.

Quantifying this massive green energy pivot, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's renewable energy capacity has skyrocketed from a mere 75 gigawatts in 2014 to approximately 300 gigawatts today. He highlighted this four-fold expansion as a monumental achievement in the country's sustainable development.

Explaining the grassroots economic benefits of this energy transition, the Prime Minister detailed how the PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM schemes are actively empowering households and farmers to generate their own solar power and slash input costs. He noted that these initiatives have added over 30 gigawatts of capacity, reducing carbon emissions by over 30 million tonnes annually while simultaneously protecting nature and enriching citizens. "And it is also empowering people,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Contrasting the nation's cooperative ethos with global power struggles, the Prime Minister stated that amidst international races for dominance, the country is intentionally forging a distinct, stabilizing path. He noted that the current decade serves as an undeniable witness to this unique national temperament. "In this race for Power in the world, India is moving ahead with a different temperament,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the cascading shocks defining the 21st century's third decade, the Prime Minister listed the rapid succession of global pandemics, regional wars, and severe supply chain disruptions affecting critical minerals, energy, and trade. He painted a stark picture of a world where one crisis barely recedes before another emerges. "The world searches for a way out of one crisis; by then, a new crisis emerges,” observed Shri Modi.

Condemning the weaponization of global interconnectedness, the Prime Minister lamented that essential elements like supply chains, energy, minerals, technology, and payment systems are being actively exploited as instruments of pressure and dominance. He warned that the integration achieved by decades of globalization is rapidly fracturing into dangerous geopolitical chokepoints. "The roots that globalization created in past decades, when and where they turned into chokepoints, we all are seeing this,” noted Shri Modi.

Addressing the resulting global crisis of confidence amidst rapid technological disruption and demographic challenges, the Prime Minister stated that the world is desperately searching for reliable partners who will maintain supply lines and honor commitments during crises. He positioned the nation as the ultimate dependable ally offering a radically different, cooperative approach to global relations. "And it is right here, India stands before you with a different temperament, a different thought,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Defining the nation's global operating model, the Prime Minister declared that the country's 21st-century progress is fundamentally defined by collaborative, inclusive advancement. He cited the nation's role as the provider of one-fifth of the world's generic medicines, a pioneer of digital identity models, and a trusted talent hub hosting over 2,000 Global Capability Centres servicing the globe. "India's progress is the story of moving forward by collaborating with everyone, by taking everyone along,” asserted Shri Modi.

Reiterating the nation's role as a stabilizing global force, the Prime Minister emphasized that whenever the world requires a steady pillar, the country responsibly extends its hand to support the international community. He outlined a fundamental philosophy of equitable advancement on the global stage. “We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world, and for the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Drawing upon profound historical legacy, the Prime Minister pointed out that the nation historically gifted the concept of 'Zero' to humanity without ever demanding royalties, and continues to operate with that exact same selfless spirit today. He contrasted this with historical global organizations that operated strictly on self-interest. "And even today India is working with this same spirit,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the nation's track record of building inclusive global platforms, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Big Cat Alliance, the Global Biofuel Alliance, IMEC, and Mission LiFE. He stressed that these platforms were intentionally designed to generate universal benefits for all forms of life rather than serving narrow geopolitical interests. "Meaning those which benefit everyone, which benefit every life, India has taken such initiatives,” asserted Shri Modi.

Summarizing the overarching philosophical framework driving the nation's foreign policy, the Prime Minister invoked the visions of 'One Sun, One World, One Grid', 'One Earth, One Family, One Future', and 'One Earth, One Health'. He emphasized that the country exclusively utilizes its power to connect, unite, and elevate others. "And even in this, the use of Power is only to Empower others,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Showcasing the nation's macroeconomic resilience amidst global uncertainty, the Prime Minister proudly cited a 7.8 percent growth rate for the April-June quarter, a current account deficit slashed to a mere 0.61 percent, and foreign exchange reserves exceeding 700 billion dollars. He declared that the domestic banking system is currently enjoying its strongest position in decades. "In a world full of uncertainties, India offers reliability and stability,” asserted Shri Modi.

Attributing recent sovereign rating upgrades to this immense structural strength, the Prime Minister highlighted the relentless execution of systemic reforms, including the implementation of GST to create a unified national market, the drafting of Insolvency Laws, the consolidation of 29 labor codes into four, and the decriminalization of hundreds of minor business offenses. He assured global investors that this unstoppable momentum is a deliberate, proactive choice driving the nation forward. “For us, reforms are not a compulsion. They are a conviction,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address by invoking the ancient Vedic mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the global community to walk, speak, and understand one another together to multiply collective strength and solve major global challenges. He expressed profound confidence that the Bloomberg New Economy Forum would serve as a massive platform to propagate this exact spirit of creating shared global opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DARPG releases the 50th Report on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) for States/UTs for September, 2026
A total of 99,134 PG cases received for the States/UTs & 1,15,168 PG cases redressed in September, 2026,
Under the Sevottam Scheme, 1,312 training courses completed, in which ~43,738 officers have been trained in the last five Financial Years
Posted On: 13 OCT 2026 12:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) released the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) 50th monthly report for States/UTs for September, 2026. The said report provides a detailed analysis of types and categories of public grievances and the nature of disposal by the States/UTs.

In September, 2026, 99,134 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 1,15,168 PG cases were redressed. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in September, 2026 with 45,970 PG cases, followed by Andhra Pradesh with 8,340 PG cases. As of 30th September, 2026, the total pendency of PG cases on the CPGRAMS portal stands at 2,37,128 across all States and UTs. Moreover, 23 States/UTs have more than 1,000 pending PG cases each.

The report provides the data for new users registered on CPGRAMS through CPGRAMS Portal during September, 2026. A total of 92,822 new users have registered on CPGRAMS in September, 2026, through various channels, out of which, the highest registrations are from Uttar Pradesh (15,742). The Feedback collected through Call Centre and Online are a total of 1,87,362 feedbacks in September, 2026, where, 75,568 feedbacks were collected from States/UTs.

The report also provides the state-wise analysis on the grievances registered through Common Service Centres in September, 2026. CPGRAMS has been integrated with the Common Service Centre (CSC) portal and is available at more than 5 lakh CSCs, associating with 2.5 lakh Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). A total of 12,996 grievances have been registered through the Common Service Centres in the month of September, 2026.

The report also provides the total number of training programmes conducted and officers trained over the last five financial years under the Sevottam Scheme. Between FY 2022–23 and FY 2026–27, a total of 1,312 training courses were conducted, training ~43,738 officers.

Key Highlights for the month of September, 2026, are as follows:

General Highlights

  • A Review Meeting was conducted with States/UTs on 24th September, 2026 to review the grievance redressal performance against service delivery benchmarks and identify measures to strengthen grievance redressal.
  • West Bengal completed its full integration with CPGRAMS Portal on 22nd September, 2026.
  • Under the Sevottam Scheme, in the last five Financial Years (FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27), 1,312 training courses have been completed, in which ~43,738 officers have been trained.
  • In September 2026, Karnataka received the highest number of grievances through CSCs, constituting 54% of the total 12,996 grievances received via CSCs.

Status of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • In September, 2026, 99,134 PG cases were received for the States/UTs and 1,15,168 PG cases were redressed, representing the highest disposal of the year.
  • Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of disposals in September, 2026 with 45,970 PG cases, followed by Andhra Pradesh and Haryana with 8,340 and 6,437 PG cases respectively.

Status of Pendency of Public Grievances on CPGRAMS

  • 23 States/UTs have more than 1000 pending grievances as on 30th September, 2026.
  • For States/UTs, as on 30th September, 2026, there exists a pendency of 2,37,128 PG cases which represents an approximate 6.3% decrease over the pendency recorded in August 2026.
