That is the message of Tarang Shakti”- Shri Rajnath Singh “Future military power will be defined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding and acting”- RM “The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms” said RM Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi Raksha Mantri…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Addresses Participants of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur, Emphasises Self-Reliance in Defence and International Cooperation
“Different nations, different aircraft, different experiences, but one sky. That is the message of Tarang Shakti”- Shri Rajnath Singh
“Future military power will be defined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding and acting”- RM
“The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms” said RM
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh addressed the participants of the second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur on October 10, 2026. Hosted by the Indian Air Force (IAF) from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multinational air exercise brought together air forces from seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) including Australia, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America along with 32 observer nations.

Congratulating the IAF and all organisations and personnel involved in the successful conduct of the exercise, the Raksha Mantri welcomed the participating nations and appreciated their contribution to strengthening professional understanding and operational cooperation. He noted that the presence of participating air forces had added significant value to the exercise and expressed hope that the contingents would return with valuable professional insights and a deeper understanding of India's capabilities and perspectives. He highlighted the importance of self-reliance in the defence sector, technological innovation and international partnerships in addressing the evolving challenges of modern warfare.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh observed that modern warfare was undergoing a profound transformation, extending beyond the traditional domains of land, sea and air to encompass space, cyber, the electromagnetic spectrum and the information domain. He highlighted the growing influence of unmanned systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electronic warfare and long-range precision weapons in shaping contemporary military operations.

“Future military power will be defined less by the number of platforms we possess. It will be determined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding, and acting,” he said, underlining that speed, precision, information and integration had emerged as defining attributes of military capability. He also emphasised the need for continuous vigilance in view of the rapidly changing geopolitical environment and the uncertainties associated with technological advancements in the defence sector.

The Raksha Mantri said that India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, had recognised the importance of strengthening national resilience against emerging security challenges and had adopted Atmanirbharta in defence as a national policy. He stressed that a nation must possess the capability to produce its own weapons and critical technologies to sustain itself during prolonged conflicts and periods of uncertainty.

Highlighting the transformation of the Indian Defence Forces, RM said that the Indian Air Force had evolved from a force operating with limited resources at the time of Independence into a modern aerospace power equipped with advanced aircraft, precision weapons, sophisticated sensors, integrated networks and increasingly advanced indigenous technologies. He emphasised that Atmanirbhar Bharat did not mean isolation from the world, but the development of domestic capabilities to design, develop, manufacture, maintain and upgrade critical defence technologies.

Referring to India's growing aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Raksha Mantri highlighted indigenous programmes and systems, including the Tejas fighter aircraft, helicopters such as Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand and the Light Utility Helicopter (LUH), the Akash air defence system, AESA radars, electronic systems, and emerging unmanned and aerospace technologies. RM also referred to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme as an important step towards mastering fifth-generation stealth fighter technology and underscored the importance of advanced aero-engine development and co-production. He said that India was keen to explore cooperation with like-minded countries in research, co-development, co-production, maintenance, training and innovation. Emphasising the growing importance of trusted partnerships and resilient supply chains, he stated, “The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms.”

The Raksha Mantri observed that building strong indigenous capabilities must go hand in hand with meaningful cooperation with trusted partners. India must be capable of acting independently when required while also operating effectively with other nations when their interests and responsibilities converge, he emphasised.

In this context, RM highlighted the significance of Exercise Tarang Shakti in translating the principles of capability, technology, interoperability and trust into operational experience. The exercise provided participating air forces an opportunity to operate alongside one another, exchange operational knowledge, assess procedures and understand different platforms, doctrines and approaches to mission planning. He noted that multinational exercises enabled aircrews and commanders to learn from one another, examine existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve their systems and processes.

Describing the spirit of the exercise, Shri Rajnath Singh said, “Different nations. Different aircraft. Different experiences. But one sky. That is the message of Tarang Shakti.” He emphasised that the value of the exercise extended beyond the sorties flown and scenarios practised, encompassing the ability to communicate, coordinate and operate effectively with partner forces. The RM called upon the Indian Air Force to incorporate the lessons of the exercise into its training, tactics, technology, doctrine and future capability development. He expressed confidence that the participating nations would carry forward the professional relationships and mutual understanding developed during the exercise to explore new avenues of aerospace and defence cooperation.

The second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti builds on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024 and reinforces India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and international cooperation. The exercise brought together diverse combat, transport, surveillance and air-to-air refuelling capabilities, providing opportunities for joint mission planning, operational learning and enhanced interoperability. The participation of indigenous platforms, including the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, also highlighted India's progress in indigenous aerospace design, engineering and manufacturing.

The contemporary relevance of the exercise is underscored by the decisive role of air power in Operation Sindoor, which demonstrated the Indian Air Force’s ability to execute precise, calibrated and effective operations in furtherance of national security objectives. The operation highlighted the importance of operational preparedness, integrated planning, credible deterrence and the effective application of air power in a complex security environment. The experience gained from operational employment reinforces the value of multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti in advancing professional understanding and preparing for the evolving challenges of modern warfare.

Beyond flying operations, the exercise featured professional engagements, industrial visits and cultural interactions, including yoga sessions, heritage visits and an International Night celebrating the traditions of participating nations. Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani, Chief of the Air Staff , Air Chief Marshal A P Singh,  Chief of the Naval Staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, other dignitaries,  officials of the Ministry of Defence and participating countries attended the event.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Second Convocation of AIIMS Deoghar
“Let Your Knowledge Heal, Your Research Innovate and Your Service Inspire”: Vice-President to Young Graduates
Vice-President Urges Young Medical Professionals to Make Competence, Compassion and Character Their Guiding Principles
“Access to Quality Healthcare and Higher Education for Tribal and Rural Communities Is Central to the Vision of Viksit Bharat”: Vice-President
“AIIMS Deoghar Reflects the Vision of Balanced and Inclusive Development”: Vice-President
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 2:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the Second Convocation of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Deoghar, Jharkhand, and congratulated the graduating doctors, nurses and healthcare professionals. Describing the convocation as a celebration of the aspirations of the Santhal Pargana region, he said that AIIMS Deoghar symbolises the growing opportunities in medical education and healthcare for tribal and rural communities.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Second Convocation of AIIMS Deoghar in Jharkhand today. Highlighting AIIMS Deoghar as a symbol of balanced and inclusive development, the Vice-President emphasised that access to quality healthcare and medical education must reach every corner of the country.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 10, 2026

Highlighting the legacy of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Sidho-Kanhu and Tilka Manjhi, the Vice-President urged the graduates to carry their knowledge beyond institutional boundaries and serve villages, tribal communities and the most remote parts of the country. He said that the highest meaning of medical knowledge lies in service to society, and called upon the young professionals to uphold competence, integrity, empathy and ethical conduct. He emphasised that a medical degree is not merely an achievement but an obligation to serve the underserved and vulnerable with compassion and dedication.

The Vice-President appreciated AIIMS Deoghar’s contribution to strengthening regional healthcare. He commended its community outreach initiatives covering malaria elimination, lymphatic filariasis surveillance, anaemia, hearing health and school health, noting that the responsibility of a medical institution extends well beyond its campus.

Referring to the expansion of medical education and healthcare infrastructure under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that the number of medical colleges in the country has increased from 387 before 2014 to 846. He said that institutions such as AIIMS Deoghar reflect the commitment to balanced and inclusive development. Access to quality healthcare and higher education in every State, district and village, he emphasised, is essential to realising the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

The Vice-President noted with satisfaction that women constituted 132 of the 173 graduating students. He said this reflected the country’s progress from women’s empowerment towards women-led development and underscored the transformative role of education in enabling women to realise their potential.

Addressing the graduates, the Vice-President urged them to remain connected to the communities the Institute was established to serve, embrace emerging technologies responsibly, and ensure that advances in artificial intelligence, telemedicine and digital diagnostics benefit people in remote areas as well as cities. He also called upon them to champion a “No to Drugs” message among young people and commended nursing professionals for their essential role in providing compassionate patient care.

The Vice-President expressed confidence that the Institute would continue to grow as a centre of clinical excellence, scientific research and compassionate service to Jharkhand and the wider eastern region. He concluded by urging the graduates to make competence, compassion and character the guiding principles of their professional lives and contribute meaningfully to the making of a Viksit Bharat.

The convocation was attended by the Governor of Jharkhand, Shri Santosh Kumar Gangwar; Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav; Jharkhand Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare, Dr. Irfan Ansari; Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Dr. Nishikant Dubey; Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), Shri Pradip Kumar Varma; Deoghar MLA, Shri Suresh Paswan; President of AIIMS Deoghar, Professor M. V. Padma Srivastava; and Executive Director and CEO of AIIMS Deoghar, Professor Nitin M. Gangane, among other dignitaries, faculty members, graduating students and their families.

item.title: The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fifth and final day of the Assembly, 9 October 2026.
item.dc:creator: Rajya Sabha Secretariat
item.description: Rajya Sabha Secretariat The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fifth and final day of the Assembly, 9 October 2026. Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 1:10PM by PIB Delhi Shri Harivansh and Members of the Delegation attended the meeting of the Governing Council of the IPU, which took up the remaining agenda items, including the election of the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and reports of specialised…
item.content:encoded:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fifth and final day of the Assembly, 9 October 2026.
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 1:10PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Harivansh and Members of the Delegation attended the meeting of the Governing Council of the IPU, which took up the remaining agenda items, including the election of the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and reports of specialised meetings.

Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha; Shri Anurag Singh Thakur, MP, Lok Sabha; and Smt. Kamaljeet Sehrawat, MP, Lok Sabha, cast the three votes allocated to India in the election of the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union.

Following the election by secret ballot, the incumbent IPU President declared Mr. Milton Dick, Speaker of the House of Representatives of Australia, elected as the next President of the IPU. Immediately after the announcement of the result, Shri Harivansh and other Members of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation congratulated Mr. Dick in person and wished him a successful tenure as President of the IPU.

Subsequently, Dr. Sasmit Patra, MP, Rajya Sabha, presented to Mr. Milton Dick a congratulatory letter from the Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha.

After the conclusion of the Governing Council meeting, the Assembly held its sittings to adopt the Arusha Communiqué; the resolution submitted by the Standing Committee on Democracy and Human Rights on “Inclusive social development for all: Parliamentary strategies to promote the rights and empowerment of persons with disabilities”; and the resolution on the emergency item, “Urgent parliamentary action to address climate-related disasters and strengthen resilience in the Himalayan region and other vulnerable regions”.

Thereafter, H.E. Mussa Azzan Zungu, Speaker of the National Assembly of Tanzania and President of the Assembly, declared the Assembly closed.

The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, participated in the 153rd IPU Assembly held in Arusha, Tanzania, from 5 to 9 October 2026. The Delegation’s participation was eventful and effective, and it contributed to the resolutions and outcomes of the IPU Assembly.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to Lead 94th Fit India Sunday on Cycle in Varanasi
Varanasi Pedals for Fitness with Asian Games Medallists at 94th Fit India Sunday on Cycle
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 1:08PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi/Varanasi, 10 October 2026: Reinforcing the message of fitness, youth empowerment and a drug-free India, the 94th edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle will be organised in Varanasi on 11 October 2026, along the route from Namo Ghat to Diksha Mandap, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 6:00 AM onwards. Centred on the theme “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat,” the initiative will bring together young people, fitness enthusiasts, citizens and sporting icons to promote an active lifestyle and encourage youth to stay away from substance abuse.

The event will bring together citizens, young people, fitness enthusiasts and members of the sporting community to promote cycling as a simple, accessible and sustainable way to embrace an active lifestyle. Through collective participation, the initiative aims to strengthen the message that fitness is a daily commitment and that sports and physical activity can play a vital role in building a healthier, stronger and drug-free India.

 

 

Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports and Labour and Employment, will grace the occasion as the Chief Guest. The event will also feature sportspersons whose performances at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games brought laurels to the nation. Prachi Chaudhary won bronze in the women’s 400m, while Parul Chaudhary secured two bronze medals in the women’s 3000m steeplechase and 5000m events. Jay Kumar won silver in the mixed 4x400m relay and bronze in the men’s 4x400m relay and Raj Kumar Pal won a gold medal as part of the hockey team.

Their participation will bring a special sporting dimension to the event, offering young participants an opportunity to engage with athletes who have represented India at the highest levels of competition. Their journeys reflect the importance of discipline, perseverance, regular training and a commitment to excellence—values that resonate with the message of Sundays on Cycle.

Pedal towards fitness and a drug-free future with Sundays on cycle ! Join us for the 94th edition of Fit India movement as we unite for "Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat" for a healthier, drug-free Viksit Bharat. 📍Namo Ghat, Varanasi 🗓️ 11th October 2026 | 6:00 AM https://t.co/PZ6RYah1SP

— Fit India Movement (@FitIndiaOff) October 9, 2026

Along with the participation of the athletes, the event will feature a range of fun and fitness activities at Namo Ghat, including yoga sessions, energetic Zumba, fun games and exciting interactive activities, offering participants an engaging platform to embrace fitness and wellness.

The campaign aligns with the broader vision of building a Fit India and a drug-free society, encouraging citizens to make cycling, walking and other forms of physical activity part of their daily routines. It also reinforces the message that the fight against substance abuse requires collective action, with families, communities, educational institutions and sporting icons playing an important role in guiding young people towards positive choices.

With Varanasi joining the 94th edition of Sundays on Cycle, the event will carry forward the spirit of collective fitness, youth participation and sporting excellence-bringing people together around one shared purpose: a healthier, fitter and drug-free India.

Fit India Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India (CFI), Raahgiri Foundation and MY Bharat. The cycling drive is conducted simultaneously across all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs), SAI Training Centres (STCs), Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) and Khelo India Centres (KICs). Over 6,000 NAMO Fit India Clubs also organise the cycling initiative nationwide every week.

PM to Lay Foundation Stone and Inaugurate National Highway Projects Worth Around ₹3,700 Crore in Tamil Nadu
PM to Inaugurate and Lay Foundation Stones for Port Projects at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V.O. Chidambaranar Port
PM to inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal
PM to dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras
PM to Participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School
PM to Perform Darshan and Pooja at Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 12:46PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on 11 October. At around 11:30 AM, he will undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. At around 12:15 PM, he will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai. Thereafter, he will undertake a walkthrough of the Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

At around 1:30 PM, the Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of, inaugurate and dedicate various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. At around 3 PM, he will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai and address the gathering.

Prime Minister will inaugurate the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore. The corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure. It also features advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations. It is expected to reduce daily travel time for commuters and improve connectivity between Chennai’s rapidly growing western suburbs and the city centre.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of and inaugurate key National Highway projects worth around ₹3,700 crore. These projects will strengthen road connectivity, reduce travel time, ease traffic congestion and support economic growth in the State.

Prime Minister will inaugurate the 36-km, four-laned Vadugapatti-Therkuvenganallur section of NH-744. The project will improve connectivity to important pilgrimage, industrial and commercial centres in the region, facilitating smoother movement of people and goods. He will also inaugurate the 30-km, four-laned Madurai Ring Road section of NH-744A. The project will improve traffic movement around Madurai and help ease congestion within the city.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the four-lane Thiruvarur Bypass on the Nagapattinam-Thanjavur section of NH-83. The project will strengthen road connectivity in Thiruvarur and facilitate smoother traffic movement by providing an alternative route around the town.

Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over ₹750 crore. He will dedicate the Karaikal-Peralam railway line, further strengthening rail connectivity in the region. He will also dedicate three rail flyovers in Coimbatore and surrounding areas. These will ease congestion at busy level crossings, reduce waiting time and improve road safety for commuters. Prime Minister will also inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal, which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of several port-related projects in Tamil Nadu to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency.

Prime Minister will inaugurate four infrastructure projects at Chennai Port: a Paved Storage Yard, four EXIM Godowns, an upgraded Cruise Terminal and a Seafarers Club. These projects will improve cargo storage and handling, expand warehouse capacity, modernise passenger facilities to enable the simultaneous embarkation and disembarkation of more cruise passengers, and provide modern welfare, recreational and support facilities for visiting seafarers and maritime personnel.  Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for eight major development projects at V.O. Chidambaranar Port. The projects will expand cargo and container capacity, building infrastructure for the transition to cleaner maritime energy, and improving the efficiency of cargo evacuation and logistics within the Port ecosystem. Prime Minister will also inaugurate the Coal Berth-3 project and lay the foundation stone for capital dredging works for Container Terminal Phase-I, Stage-II at Kamarajar Port.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) in Chennai. With a total cost of around ₹1,620 crore and a capacity of 270 thousand metric tonnes per annum (TMTPA), the project aims to produce Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks for the manufacture of world-class, premium-quality lubricants in India.

Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras. He will also launch its pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan - from the foetal stage to old age. Prime Minister will also release C-STROKE, a one-of-its-kind human ischaemic stroke atlas. Featuring over 1,000 annotated microscopic sections from a stroke-affected brain, the atlas will help researchers worldwide identify novel therapeutic targets.

Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai. The Golden Jubilee marks five decades of the institution’s contribution to education and its role in nurturing  generations of students through academic excellence, discipline, cultural values and holistic education. Guided by its motto, “Sa Vidya Ya Vimuktaye” (Knowledge that liberates), the school seeks to nurture individuals who make meaningful contributions to society. Over the years, the institution has evolved in response to changing educational needs while continuing to place strong emphasis on character-building, knowledge and responsible citizenship.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Tribal Affairs Second Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Kolkata Eight States reviewed progress on pending claims, record incorporation, Community Forest Resource Rights and PVTG Habitat Rights; district-wise, time-bound action plans called for Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, convened the Second Regional Review Conference on implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Second Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Kolkata
Eight States reviewed progress on pending claims, record incorporation, Community Forest Resource Rights and PVTG Habitat Rights; district-wise, time-bound action plans called for
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, convened the Second Regional Review Conference on implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (FRA) at Kolkata, West Bengal on 9th October 2026. The Conference brought together senior functionaries of the Tribal Welfare, Revenue and Forest Departments and Tribal Research Institutes of eight States, namely West Bengal, Assam, Tripura, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Additionally senior officials of Andhra Pradesh were invited to share the best practices the State has undertaken on digitization, integration of FRA titles into government records and taking up proactive measures on convergence of livelihood schemes with FRA titleholders and providing credit facilities to the right holders. Further, District officials- Collectors, Sub Collectors and ITDP/ITDA Project Officers, where districts having a large pendency of FRA claims, also attended, to review the status of implementation and deliberate on a coordinated way forward. The Conference follows the First Regional Review Conference held in Bengaluru on 10 September 2026 for the Southern States.

Proceedings began with a Welcome Address by the Principal Secretary, Tribal Development Department, Government of West Bengal, who apprised the gathering of the objectives of the Conference and extended a formal welcome to the dignitaries and delegates which was followed by the Keynote Address of the Joint Secretary, MoTA, and the Special Address of the Secretary, MoTA.

In his Keynote Address, the Joint Secretary said that as on 31st August 2026, over 54 lakh claims had been received nationally, and about 25 lakh titles had been distributed. About 11 lakh claims still remain pending at different stages, while over 18 lakh claims have been rejected. He noted that Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Assam account for substantial pendency concentrated in particular districts. He highlighted that the Regional Conference focuses on the following key priorities such as timely disposal of pending claims and review of rejected claims in accordance with the Act and Rules, reconciliation of FRA data, digitization of FRA case records, incorporation of recognised rights into revenue and forest records, accelerate recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights and Habitat Rights recognition for PVTGs. 

In her Special Address, the Secretary, MoTA, said that the FRA places the rights, dignity and aspirations of forest-dwelling communities at the heart of inclusive and sustainable development. She appreciated the experience of Andhra Pradesh in digitization and creating of record of rights of FRA title holders to avail the post claim support, Odisha and Chhattisgarh in pioneering the recognition of PVTG habitat rights and recognition of highest number of IFR claims. She stressed that recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights (CFRR) must be matched by the capacity to exercise them. Gram Sabhas need support to prepare and implement Community Forest Resource Management Plans, and States should operationalise the joint advisory of MoTA and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. This advisory enables integration of these plans with the working and management plans of Forest Departments, while keeping the authority of the Gram Sabha central. She added that assistance is available under DA-JGUA for capacity building of Gram Sabha for preparation of such CFR management plans and their execution. She also called for PVTG-wise roadmaps for Habitat Rights which need to be prepared with sensitivity and the active participation of traditional institutions and the Gram Sabhas of all concerned villages. She further emphasised that recognised rights must be incorporated into Revenue and Forest records with accurate maps, and that convergence with programmes for productive land use, housing and livelihoods must become a regular part of implementation.

The Director, FRA, MoTA, presented the national scenario, including pendency in high-pendency States and priority districts. Her presentation also covered the importance of incorporating the Record of Forest Rights into revenue and forest records in line with the Ministry’s advisory of 24 June 2026 and Habitat Rights under the Ministry’s guidelines of 5 January 2026. She also outlined the financial support available from MoTA to take forward such interventions by the States. Further, states were also asked to reconcile data discrepancies and delays in Monthly Progress Reports. Also, States have been directed to prepare an action plan for strengthening Gram Sabhas to create awareness of FRA rights, post Claims support, and for preparation of the CFR management plan on priority. The Deputy Secretary, TRI & IT, MoTA, spoke on digitisation of FRA records and demonstrated the National-level FRA Portal and the FRA mobile app which can be useful to advance digitization, geospatial integration and decision-support systems for FRA governance. Also, urged the States to integrate their existing FRA records through Application Programming Interface (API).

State-wise Presentations

Officers of the eight States presented the status of FRA implementation in their respective States, covering claim pendency, incorporation of records, Community Forest Resource Rights and Habitat rights of PVTGs and digitisation of FRA records. The States also presented the action plan for timely disposal of pending claims, review of rejected claims, recognition of CFRR and habitat rights in a time bound manner and strengthening convergence so that eligible right-holders receive livelihood and development support.

The Conference concluded with a Valedictory Address by the Joint Secretary, MoTA, and a Vote of Thanks by the Director, FRA, MoTA.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to Declare Open BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Demonstration Games 2026 in Ahmedabad
BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Demonstration Games 2026 to Be Held in Ahmedabad on 12 October
BRICS Nations to Showcase Traditional and Indigenous Sports and Cultural Heritage at Ahmedabad Games
Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Gujarat, will organise the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex, Ahmedabad, on 12 October 2026, under India's BRICS Chairship.

Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Hon'ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, will inaugurate the event. The inauguration will be graced by the presence of Shri Harsh Sanghavi, Hon'ble Deputy Chief Minister, Gujarat, Smt. Raksha Nikhil Khadse, Hon'ble Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, and Dr. Jayram Gamit, Hon'ble Minister of State for Sports, Gujarat.


The Games will bring together delegations from BRICS Member and partner countries to showcase traditional and indigenous sporting practices and promote cultural exchange, heritage preservation and people-to-people cooperation through sport.

Designed as a non-competitive platform, the Games will focus on the demonstration, documentation, and exchange of traditional sporting practices, with emphasis placed on cultural significance, practitioner interaction and knowledge-sharing.


Participating countries are expected to showcase a diverse range of traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices:

- Belarus:Gorodki

- Bolivia: Lucha de Cholitas, Tinku, Rayuela, Trompo, Cachinas and Carrera de Sacos

- Brazil: Zarabatana (Indigenous Blowpipe), Corrida de Toras (Log Race), Brazilian Para-Jiu-jitsu and Capoeira

- China: Wushu, Lion Dance and Health Qigong

- Ethiopia: Ethiopian Wrestling (Tegel), Ethiopian Gena (Field Hockey) and Selus Gebeta/18-12/Bube/Shahe

- India: Mallakhamb, Yogasana, Kalaripayattu

- Iran: Zoorkhaneh, Haft Sang and Ghanieh

- Kazakhstan: Asyk Atu, Togyzkumalak and Qazaq Kuresi

- Russia: Gorodki and Sambo

- South Africa: Kgati and Iintonga

- United Arab Emirates: Al Tabbah

Bilateral meetings with visiting delegations are planned on the sidelines to explore opportunities to strengthen cooperation in sports and promote traditional and indigenous games within the BRICS framework.

The Games are expected to serve as a unique platform for celebrating the rich sporting heritage of participating countries while fostering mutual understanding, cultural exchange, and stronger people-to-people ties among BRICS nations.

 

*****

 

Ayushman Kumar

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs valedictory session of National Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development
Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, PM calls for making Anganwadis as Centres of community participation
PM suggests Universities could adopt nearby Anganwadi Centres and undertake social-impact studies
On women’s safety, PM emphasises on preventive actions through convergence of efforts across various departments
PM calls for greater focus on the health, nutrition and overall development of adolescent girls
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 9:41PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development, at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan earlier today.

The Summit, part of the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister, brought together Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories for focused deliberations on nutrition and early childhood care, child protection, women’s safety and empowerment, and strengthening delivery of services through greater convergence.

Prime Minister appreciated the intensive deliberations and emphasised the importance of collaborative decision-making between the Centre and States. He suggested that States could take this model further by organising similar Chintan Shivirs at the district level and at Nagar Palika and Mahanagar Palika levels. He also suggested dedicated Chintan Shivirs for Anganwadi Workers to enable them to exchange experiences, innovations and practical solutions from the field.

Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Prime Minister stressed that an Anganwadi Centre should not function as an isolated institution but become a centre of community participation. He said families living around Anganwadi Centres could also be encouraged to contribute on special occasions by sharing nutritious food, toys and locally relevant items for children.

Prime Minister called for deeper engagement of universities and educational institutions with Anganwadi Centres. Universities could adopt nearby Anganwadi Centres and undertake social-impact studies, creating opportunities for students to contribute while also generating useful insights for improving service delivery. Medical students and NSS and NCC volunteers could similarly be associated with Anganwadi Centres and community initiatives, he said. He also called for greater focus on the health, nutrition and overall development of adolescent girls.

Prime Minister discussed issues concerning women’s safety, he suggested developing age-appropriate modules for children on women’s safety, dignity and empowerment. He also laid emphasis on preventive actions through convergence of efforts across various departments.

Highlighting the close relationship between cleanliness, health and nutrition, Prime Minister called upon Women and Child Development Departments across the country to take active ownership of the Swachhata Abhiyan. He stressed that good health and nutrition begin with cleanliness and that Anganwadi Centres and surrounding communities could become important platforms for promoting this behavioural change.

Prime Minister observed that national movements such as Vocal for Local and One District One Product (ODOP) should be promoted for Women Empowerment. He added that women’s collectives and community institutions could become important partners in strengthening local products, livelihoods and economic empowerment.

Prime Minister emphasised that the Ministry of Women and Child Development and its counterparts in the States are entrusted with responsibilities touching one of the largest and most important segments of society. The children being nurtured in Anganwadi Centres today will become the youth and citizens who build Viksit Bharat.

***

item.title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Holds Daylong Western Zone Regional Review Meeting In Diu
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Holds Daylong Western Zone Regional Review Meeting In Diu Meeting Attended By Ministry Officials, Senior Representatives of Governments of Goa, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra And Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu Secretary MoSJE Shri Sudhansh Pant Reviews Implementation of Key Welfare, Social Empowerment And Social Defence Schemes With Focus On Last-Mile Delivery, Beneficiary Saturation And Outcome-Oriented Implementation Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 9:35PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Holds Daylong Western Zone Regional Review Meeting In Diu
Meeting Attended By Ministry Officials, Senior Representatives of Governments of Goa, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra And Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu
Secretary MoSJE Shri Sudhansh Pant Reviews Implementation of Key Welfare, Social Empowerment And Social Defence Schemes With Focus On Last-Mile Delivery, Beneficiary Saturation And Outcome-Oriented Implementation
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 9:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, convened a day long Regional Review Meeting (RRM) in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH&DD), to undertake a comprehensive review of the implementation of major welfare, social empowerment and social defence schemes in the Western Zone of the country, here today.

The Meeting brought together senior representatives from the States of Rajasthan, Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra, along with senior officers of the Union Territory Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, chaired the meeting and outlined the key implementation priorities and objectives of the Regional Review Meeting.

Under the guidance of Hon'ble Administrator of UT of DNH&DD Shri Praful Patel, several senior officers participated in the Regional Review Meeting.

Secretary, Social Welfare Department, Shri Ashish Mohan, Collector, Diu Shri Rahul Dev Boora and Director-cum-Deputy Secretary, Social Welfare Department Shri Puneet Kulshreshtha, were among other senior officers of the UT who attended the Review Meeting.

Senior representatives from the participating States including Shri Lalit Kumar, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Rajasthan; Shri Dipak Desai, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Goa; Ms Deepa Mudhol Mundhe, Commissioner, Department of Social Welfare, Government of Maharashtra and Ms Sonali Mule, Director under Government of Maharashtra, participated in the deliberations.

 

Dr. Jagdish Vadhvana, Joint Director, OBC Division; Dr. Prarthana Sherashiya, Dy Director, Social Defence; Shri Hiren L Chaudhari, Dy Director, Scheduled Caste Welfare; Shri Deepak Chavda, Social Welfare Officer, OBC Division from the Government of Gujarat, also attended the daylong meeting.

Senior officers from the Ministry including the Additional Secretary Smt. Debolina Thakur, along with Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, Shri Parveen Kumar Thind, Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Deputy Director General, Smt. Pratima Gupta and Director, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, attended the Meeting.

Chairing the Meeting, Shri Sudhansh Pant said the Regional Review Meeting is aimed at strengthening institutional coordination between the Ministry, the participating States and the Union Territory Administration and ensuring effective, transparent, accountable and outcome-oriented implementation of social justice and empowerment programmes, with particular emphasis on last-mile delivery, beneficiary coverage and saturation, efficient utilization of resources and measurable outcomes.

He said the Meeting provides an institutional platform for a scheme-wise assessment of progress, identification of implementation gaps and challenges, sharing of best practices and formulation of time-bound corrective and follow-up measures to improve the delivery of benefits to eligible beneficiaries.

Shri Pant exuded confidence that the mechanism of Regional Review Meeting is expected to further strengthen the institutional framework for effective implementation of social justice, social empowerment and social defence programmes in the Western Region.

The Secretary said that the Meeting reinforces the Government's commitment to inclusive development, social protection, dignity, equal opportunity and empowerment of vulnerable and disadvantaged sections of society, with a continued focus on ensuring that the benefits of government schemes reach the last mile.

Scheme-wise Review of Major Programmes

The Regional Review Meeting undertook a detailed scheme-wise review of major programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, including the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), measures for strengthening the enforcement machinery under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).

The review assessed physical and financial progress, beneficiary coverage and saturation, utilization of funds, institutional mechanisms, implementation of statutory safeguards, awareness and outreach measures, rehabilitation and social reintegration initiatives, as well as convergence with the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA).

A detailed discussion and open-house session provided an opportunity to examine implementation challenges and identify practical solutions relating to beneficiary identification and saturation, inter-departmental convergence, monitoring and data management, fund utilization, grievance redressal and dissemination of best practices and replicable models. The session also focussed on evolving time-bound corrective measures wherever required.

 

Review of Scholarships, Senior Citizen Welfare and NAMASTE

The day-long deliberations covered key welfare and social empowerment initiatives, including Scholarship Schemes, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) and the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE).

The review of Scholarship Schemes focussed on beneficiary coverage, application and verification processes, timely disbursement of assistance, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-related issues and measures to strengthen outreach among eligible students, particularly those who remain outside the existing coverage.

Under AVYAY, the review assessed initiatives relating to the welfare, protection and empowerment of senior citizens, including institutional care, active ageing, social security, accessibility, support services and convergence with programmes and interventions of the Union Territory Administration.

The review of NAMASTE focussed on the identification and profiling of sanitation workers and waste pickers, occupational safety and dignity, ensuring zero fatalities during sanitation work, access to social security and health benefits, mechanization of sanitation operations, capacity building, livelihood support and convergence with other welfare and social protection schemes.

Focus on Last-Mile Delivery and Measurable Outcomes

A dedicated Outcome Review Session assessed the extent of coverage and saturation of eligible beneficiaries, quality and timeliness of service delivery, implementation bottlenecks, awareness and outreach mechanisms, technology-enabled monitoring, grievance redressal and feedback systems, and convergence between Central Government schemes and programmes implemented by the States and Union Territory Administration.

Particular emphasis was placed on last-mile delivery and measurable outcomes, with the objective of ensuring that government interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of intended beneficiaries.

The meeting identified priority interventions and specific action points and takeaways for the participating States and the Union Territory, with emphasis on strengthening implementation mechanisms, improving outreach, addressing gaps in beneficiary identification and ensuring timely and transparent delivery of benefits.

Way Forward

The concluding session focused on consolidating the key observations, priorities and recommendations emerging from the deliberations. The Way Forward included finalization of action points and responsibilities, strengthening coordination between the Ministry, States and Union Territory Administration, time-bound resolution of implementation issues, improved monitoring of physical and financial progress and submission of follow-up Action Taken Reports (ATRs) by the concerned authorities.

Commitment To NMBA, Senior Citizens’ Respect & Welfare

Secretary Sudhansh Pant administered Senior Citizen Pledge and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Pledge, to the participants during the Meeting, reiterating adopting and strengthening the Whole of the Government and Whole of the Society approach for the Nasha Mukt Viksit Bharat and upholding and consolidation of the social values to uphold honour, dignity, welfare and healthcare of the Senior Citizenry, across the country.

Organised…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Bharat 6G Alliance Strengthens Global Partnerships at 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026
Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani addresses valedictory session; DoT highlights ESTIC 2026 and its focus on intelligent networks and quantum communication
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 concluded at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, with a valedictory address by Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. Organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) alongside India Mobile Congress 2026, the three-day event brought together global telecom leaders, policymakers, standards organisations, industry, academia and researchers to discuss the roadmap towards IMT-2030 and beyond.

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development is his address congratulated the Bharat 6G Alliance for organizing the two-day 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 and for inviting over 75 speakers, which included more than 30 international experts.

The Union Minister of State said that India is moving from being one of the world’s largest telecom markets to becoming an important telecom technology nation and our indigenous technology journey has taught us something important: Self-reliance and global collaboration are not opposites. The stronger our capabilities, the stronger the partner we can be to the world. The Union Minister of State highlighted that 6G must not create a new digital divide while we are still closing the old one. Affordability, accessibility and coverage must therefore be design requirements — not afterthoughts and in 6G, connectivity need not end where the tower ends. The integration of terrestrial and satellite networks can take connectivity further — to remote villages, islands, oceans and places that traditional networks struggle to reach. India is ready to test these technologies at scale — and share what we learn with the world. Our national goal is Viksit Bharat — a developed India by 2047, the hundredth year of our independence.

The experts contributed to sessions on 5G-Advanced foundations for 6G, global standards, spectrum and WRC-27, international trials and testbeds, AI-native and sustainable networks, startups and academia, global alliances, and industrial use cases. The Symposium emphasized that global interoperability and inclusive 6G development will depend on collaboration across countries, industry, research institutions and standards bodies.

The Symposium reaffirmed India’s commitment to contributing to global 6G research and standards while building indigenous capabilities and strengthening international partnerships. Its discussions called for coordinated standards development, collaborative research, spectrum harmonization and large-scale testing, with affordability, accessibility, security and sustainability embedded in the design of future networks.

A key outcome was the exchange of five new MoUs with GSMA, one6G, GTI Alliance, 6G Innovation Forum (6G IF) Taiwan and VOICE, strengthening opportunities for international cooperation, joint research, trials and knowledge exchange. B6GA also released ten white papers and reports, including a Progress Report on 6G Joint Principles, reflecting continued work towards a 6G ecosystem that is secure, open, resilient, inclusive and sustainable by design.

During the valedictory session in the presence of the Minister of State for Communications, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) presented a curtain raiser for the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026. The second edition of this national science and technology platform is scheduled from 27–29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and organised by CSIR in collaboration with 12 participating departments/Ministries. Its theme is “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies”.

The three-day Conclave features plenary talks, 9 thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, presentations by science and technology leaders and deep-tech Startups, exhibitions and B2B/B2G connect meetings.

In the 2nd edition of ESTIC 2026 , DoT is identified to led the  thematic session “Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication”, scheduled for 28 October 2026. The session will explore technologies shaping future digital infrastructure and secure communications. It will feature a keynote by Mr. N. G. Subramaniam, Vice President, TCS; presentations by deep-tech entrepreneurs and technology leaders; and a panel discussion with experts from IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi, HFCL, Reliance Jio and Bharat 6G Alliance, moderated by Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT.

For more details , please visit: www.estic2026.in

About Bharat 6G Alliance

Established in July 2023, Bharat 6G Alliance is an industry-led collaborative platform bringing together telecom service providers, industry, startups, academia and research institutions to advance India’s 6G ambitions. It promotes indigenous research and innovation, intellectual property creation, international standards engagement and partnerships for an affordable, secure, sustainable and globally interoperable 6G ecosystem.

For more details www.bharat6galliance.com

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Presents SIDM Champion Awards 2026 and Calls for Greater Private Sector Participation, R&D Investment and Enhanced Defence Production Capacity
“National security increasingly depends on the country's ability to design, develop, manufacture and control the technologies and equipment required by our Defence Forces”- Shri Rajnath Singh
“Marking a historic milestone, India's defence exports have reached a record ₹38,424 crore in the FY 2025-26, registering growth of over 60% compared with the previous financial year”- RM
“Defence manufacturers must treat expenditure on R&D as an investment that strengthens operational preparedness, improves competitiveness and contributes to national security” said RM
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh presented the SIDM Champion Awards 2026 at the 8th Annual Session of the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) in New Delhi on  October 09, 2026. A total of 15 Champion Awards were presented at the event, recognising organisations for their achievements in indigenous technology development, product innovation, design, import substitution, manufacturing excellence and exports. RM congratulated the awardees for their contributions to indigenous defence manufacturing, technological innovation, design capabilities, import substitution, manufacturing excellence and exports.

Underlining the importance of the session's theme, “Sovereign Capabilities, Contested Frontiers: Accelerating India's Strategic Autonomy in an Era of Disruption,” the RM said that national security increasingly depends on the country's ability to design, develop, manufacture and control the technologies and equipment required by its Defence Forces. He expressed confidence that India's talent pool, young workforce, industrial capabilities and policy support would enable the country to emerge among the world's leading defence manufacturing nations.

The Raksha Mantri acknowledged SIDM's role in strengthening the domestic defence industrial ecosystem and facilitating policy-industry dialogue. He called upon the Indian defence industry to increase private sector participation in defence production, strengthen research and development (R&D), enhance surge and production capacity, and accelerate technological innovation to advance India's strategic autonomy and self-reliance in defence.

Shri Rajnath Singh said that the transformation of India's defence industry from a major importer of defence equipment to a credible and reliable exporter of sophisticated military hardware is a significant achievement. He noted that India's defence exports reached a record ₹38,424 crore in the financial year 2025-26, registering growth of over 60 per cent compared with the previous financial year. He reiterated the target of achieving ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029.

Emphasising the importance of private sector participation, Shri Rajnath Singh recalled his earlier call for increasing the private sector's share in India's total defence production from approximately 24 percent to 50 percent. He said that the private sector's contribution had grown significantly over the past 12 years and urged industry leaders to set progressive milestones to achieve this shared national objective. He assured the industry that the Government would continue to support its growth while maintaining the necessary standards of regulation, safety, quality and accountability.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, the Raksha Mantri observed that modern conflicts increasingly depend on technological capabilities, including drones, missiles, air defence systems and rapidly evolving software and communications technologies. “Defence manufacturers must treat expenditure on R&D as an investment that strengthens operational preparedness, improves competitiveness and contributes to national security” said RM.

Referring to Operation Sindoor, RM highlighted the importance of ensuring that domestic manufacturing facilities can rapidly scale up production when required. He urged the industry to develop innovative solutions to expand manufacturing capacity and respond swiftly to changing operational demands.

Established in 2017, SIDM has emerged as a unified platform representing large enterprises, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), startups, academia and foreign original equipment manufacturers. He said that policy reforms introduced by the Government, including the Defence Acquisition Procedure, Defence Procurement Manual, Positive Indigenisation Lists, SRIJAN portal and Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX), were aimed at expanding the capabilities of India's private defence industry.

The event was attended by Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Director General (Acquisition) Shri A. Anbarasu, SIDM Founder President Shri Baba Kalyani, SIDM President Shri Arun Ramchandani, senior government officials, representatives of the Defence Forces, and leaders of Indian and international defence companies.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry to Observe World Mental Health Day 2026, Reaffirming Commitment to Accessible, Inclusive and People-Centred Mental Healthcare
​​​​​​​Tele-MANAS renders yeoman service in bringing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health support within easy reach of people across India through toll-free helpline 14416
Over 47.75 lakh calls received since launch on 10 October 2022; 53 Tele-MANAS Cells operational across all 36 States and Union Territories
Women account for nearly 44% of recorded caller profiles, reflecting growing access to mental health support through telephone-based counselling
MANN Jaagriti initiative to strengthen community awareness, encourage early help-seeking and address mental health stigma
Mental health services integrated into over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; District Mental Health Programme sanctioned for 767 districts
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will observe World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026, reaffirming the Government of India's commitment to making mental healthcare accessible, affordable, inclusive and people-centred. This year's global theme, “Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change,” underscores the importance of listening to individuals with lived experiences of mental health conditions and ensuring their voices contribute to shaping responsive mental health policies and services.

At the heart of India's efforts to improve access to mental healthcare is Tele MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States), which has emerged as an important pillar of the country's mental healthcare delivery system. Through its national toll-free helpline 14416, Tele-MANAS is providing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health counselling and support, enabling people to seek professional assistance easily, irrespective of their geographical location or socioeconomic background.

Tele-MANAS: Making Mental Health Support Just a Phone Call Away

Launched on 10 October 2022, Tele-MANAS has rendered yeoman service in bridging gaps in access to mental healthcare by bringing timely counselling, emotional support and professional guidance directly to people through a simple telephone call.

Since its launch, Tele MANAS has received 47,75,644 calls, with 53 operational cells across all 36 States and Union Territories, as of October 2026. This extensive reach reflects the growing importance of accessible, technology-enabled mental health services in addressing diverse mental health needs across the country.

Through 14416, individuals experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, stress, sleep-related concerns or other mental health challenges can connect with trained counsellors without having to travel to a healthcare facility for initial support. Available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and supported by multilingual services, the helpline makes it easier for people to seek help at a time and place convenient to them.

The service is particularly significant for people residing in rural, remote and underserved areas, where access to specialised mental healthcare facilities may be limited. By offering a confidential and supportive platform, Tele-MANAS is also helping address hesitation associated with seeking mental health assistance and encouraging individuals to reach out early.

Beyond initial counselling, the programme facilitates access to specialised mental health professionals and appropriate referral services wherever required, helping ensure continuity of care through linkages with the wider public healthcare system.

Growing Public Engagement Reflects the Importance of Accessible Mental Healthcare

The increasing utilisation of Tele-MANAS highlights the importance of having a readily accessible platform where individuals can seek support without fear of stigma or discrimination.

An analysis of 13,35,275 recorded caller profiles indicates that women account for 43.78% (5,84,587) of callers, while men constitute 54.18% (7,23,427). The substantial participation of women highlights the role of telephone-based counselling in providing a convenient and supportive avenue for seeking mental healthcare.

The service has also witnessed significant engagement among young and working-age populations, with individuals aged 18–45 years accounting for 73.2% of recorded caller profiles.

The range of concerns reported by callers, including emotional distress, stress related to examinations, workplaces and relationships, anxiety and sleep disturbances, demonstrates the importance of accessible mental health support in everyday life.

By providing a platform where individuals can speak openly, receive guidance and be connected to appropriate services, Tele-MANAS is contributing to a broader shift towards recognising mental health as an integral part of overall health and well-being.

MANN Jaagriti: Taking Mental Health Awareness to Communities

As part of World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry is also taking forward MANN Jaagriti, a structured community awareness and engagement initiative aimed at strengthening mental health literacy, reducing stigma and encouraging timely help-seeking.

The initiative seeks to move beyond one-time awareness activities by promoting sustained community engagement through schools, colleges, workplaces, health facilities and other community platforms.

Through locally relevant activities, States and Union Territories will encourage open conversations around mental health, promote early identification of mental health concerns and create greater awareness about available services, including Tele-MANAS.

The initiative will also encourage the involvement of healthcare professionals, educators, community workers, youth, families, caregivers, civil society organisations and persons with lived experience of mental health conditions.

By bringing mental health conversations into everyday community settings, MANN Jaagriti aims to foster supportive environments where seeking mental health assistance is recognised as a positive and important step towards well-being.

Strengthening Mental Healthcare from the Community to the District Level

Complementing the reach of Tele-MANAS, the Government of India continues to strengthen mental healthcare services through the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) and the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP).

The DMHP has been sanctioned for implementation in 767 districts, with support extended to States and Union Territories under the National Health Mission. The programme facilitates outpatient care, counselling, psychosocial interventions, medicines, follow-up care, outreach activities and referral services, alongside provisions for inpatient mental healthcare at the district level.

Mental health services have also been integrated into the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package offered through over 1.83 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs across the country.

Through these facilities, primary healthcare teams undertake screening and early identification of mental health concerns, provide psychosocial support and follow-up care, and facilitate referrals to higher healthcare facilities wherever necessary.

Together, these initiatives are strengthening a continuum of mental healthcare that connects community awareness, primary healthcare, district-level services and digital counselling platforms.

Towards a More Inclusive and Supportive Mental Healthcare Ecosystem

On World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reiterates that mental healthcare should be within everyone's reach and seeking help should never be a source of hesitation or stigma.

The growing reach of Tele-MANAS, alongside the expansion of community-based and primary mental healthcare services, reflects the Government's continued efforts to build a responsive healthcare system that places the needs, dignity and well-being of individuals at its centre.

Through Tele-MANAS, the Ministry is reinforcing a simple but important message: mental health support need not be distant, difficult or inaccessible. Help is available, and reaching out can begin with a phone call.

The Ministry encourages individuals experiencing mental health concerns, as well as families and caregivers seeking guidance, to make use of the free and confidential services offered through Tele MANAS at 14416, available 24×7 across the country.

Every conversation matters. Every voice deserves to be heard. And mental health support must be accessible to all.

***

SR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Files to Freedom: DEPwD Drives Swachhata, Pendency Reduction and Efficient Governance
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is intensifying its efforts under Special Campaign 6 (2–31 October 2026) to reduce pendency, improve record management, free office space and ensure responsible e-waste disposal.

Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and promote efficient governance. DEPwD has nominated a Nodal Officer and advised its Attached and Subordinate Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies to nominate Nodal Officers and identify pending matters.

Building on Special Campaign 5.0, DEPwD and its organisations digitised and weeded out 11,972 physical files/documents, freed approximately 15,588 square feet of office space, generated ₹14.47 lakh in revenue and conducted 64 cleanliness campaigns during October 2025.

Swachhata and pendency-reduction activities have continued beyond the annual campaign, with progress regularly recorded on the Special Campaign 6 Portal (SCDPM) in accordance with DARPG guidelines.

The current progress recorded on the portal reflects the Department’s ongoing efforts towards effective record management and disposal of pending matters. Against 52 cleanliness campaigns identified for the current phase, 13 have already been conducted. Of the 928 physical files due for review, 172 have been reviewed, while 32 e-files have been put up for review.

The Department is also addressing various categories of references and public grievances as part of its pendency-reduction efforts. The portal records that 154 out of 202 targeted public grievances and 20 out of 43 public grievance appeals have been addressed. Further, 10 out of 55 references from Members of Parliament, 3 out of 8 Parliamentary Assurances, 2 out of 2 JMC References relating to Cabinet Proposals, and 4 out of 6 PMO References have been addressed.

As part of the ongoing Swachhata Special Campaign 6, a cleanliness activity was conducted on 8th October 2026 at the Guest House of Swami Vivekanand National Institute of Rehabilitation Training and Research (SVNIRTAR) and its adjoining areas. The activity focused on maintaining cleanliness, hygiene and sanitation and promoting responsible waste-management practices, contributing to a clean, healthy campus environment.

Special Campaign 6.0 reinforces the twin objectives of Swachhata and good governance by reducing avoidable pendency, improving record management, freeing usable space and ensuring responsible disposal of obsolete material, particularly e-waste. It seeks to transform redundant records and material into opportunities for greater efficiency, accountability and optimal utilisation of public resources.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment “Accessibility Cannot Be an Afterthought”: DEPwD Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach to Sugamya Bharat Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi “Accessibility cannot be an afterthought, nor can it be left to a single department or agency. It requires a concerted effort across all ministries, departments and levels of government, in partnership with civil society.” This was the central message of Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, IAS, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), as she called…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
“Accessibility Cannot Be an Afterthought”: DEPwD Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach to Sugamya Bharat
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

 “Accessibility cannot be an afterthought, nor can it be left to a single department or agency. It requires a concerted effort across all ministries, departments and levels of government, in partnership with civil society.” This was the central message of Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, IAS, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), as she called for a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to advancing accessibility across India at the consultation “Sugamyata Ka Sankalp” held at the India International Centre, New Delhi.

Emphasising that accessibility cuts across education, healthcare, employment, transport, financial services and public infrastructure, Ms. Nanda stressed that progress in one sector depends on coordinated action across others. She underscored the need for States to accord accessibility the priority it deserves and for all stakeholders to work together to translate the vision of an inclusive and accessible India into reality. Her message reinforced that accessibility must be embedded at the design stage itself, rather than being added on or corrected later.

Organised by DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, in partnership with The Association of People with Disability (APD), India, and in collaboration with Ipsos, the consultation brought together representatives from government, the disability sector, academia, research and civil society to assess the progress of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, identify persistent accessibility gaps and deliberate on priorities for its next phase.

Shri Girish C. Hosur, Joint Secretary, DEPwD, presented the journey and achievements of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, highlighting the Department’s role in leading the initiative and advancing accessibility across public infrastructure, transport and digital services. His presentation provided the context for discussions on consolidating progress and strengthening implementation in the years ahead.

Shri S. Govindaraj, Commissioner, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, emphasised that accessibility is the need of the hour. He highlighted the importance of the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan in advancing accessibility across the country and stressed the need to build on the progress achieved so far to address the barriers that continue to affect persons with disabilities.

Welcoming the participants, Mr. Subir Hari Singh,  President, APD, highlighted the importance of bringing together diverse stakeholders to advance accessibility. He emphasised that meaningful progress depends on sustained partnership among government, practitioners, experts and persons with disabilities. He also outlined APD’s mission and its work in the disability sector.

The consultation featured two moderated roundtable discussions led by Ms. Tripti Sharma, Director, Ipsos. The first examined sectoral challenges in the implementation and use of accessibility data, while the second explored approaches to measuring accessibility across sectors and the essential features of a credible and practical measurement framework. The discussions underscored the importance of reliable data and evidence to guide planning, monitor implementation and assess progress.

Participants included representatives from the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Prasar Bharati and the Airports Authority of India. State Commissioners for Persons with Disabilities, representatives of the State Governments of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and disability-sector leaders from across India participated both in person and online.

Launched in 2015, the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan marked a significant national initiative to advance accessibility in the built environment, transport systems and information and communication technologies. The consultation, held against the backdrop of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, provided an opportunity to reflect on achievements, identify continuing barriers and explore ways to strengthen accessibility standards, implementation and measurement.

In his closing remarks, Mr. Sukanto Aich, Chief Executive Officer, APD, observed that the gathering itself—bringing stakeholders together to learn from one another and commit to collaboration—was a sign of hope for making the vision of Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan a reality.

The consultation reinforced the shared responsibility of governments, institutions, civil society and the disability sector in building an accessible and inclusive India. Its central message was clear: accessibility must move beyond isolated initiatives to become an integral, measurable and coordinated priority across every sector.
