item.content:encoded:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
PRESS RELEASE ON the 382nd  REPORT OF The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sports on "Reforms and Strengthening of the National Testing Agency (NTA)"
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sports headed by Shri Mukul Wasnik, M.P., Rajya Sabha presented the 382nd Report on "Reforms and Strengthening of the National
Testing Agency (NTA)" pertaining to the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education to the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha on 9th October, 2026.

2.         The Committee during the course of preparation of the 382nd Report, heard the views of Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education; Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Chairperson, National Testing Agency; Director General, National Testing Agency; Dr. K. Radhakrishnan, Former Secretary, Department of Space & Chairman, High-Level Committee of Experts and other representatives of the Department, and examined the subject in detail.

3.         The Report was considered and adopted by the Committee at its meeting held on 25th August, 2026. The Observations/Recommendations made by the Committee in the Report are enclosed herewith.

4.         The Report is also available on the following link:- https://sansad.in/rs/committees/16?departmentally-related-standing-committees

382nd Report

OBSERVATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

10.1 The Committee notes that under the National Education Policy 2020, the National Testing Agency has been vested with very important responsibilities. It conducts all of India’s most significant public examinations such as JEE-Mains, NEET-UG, UGC-NET, and CUET, among others and therefore acts as the gateway for the higher education system. In total, the NTA conducts examinations for which about 1.2 crore students sit annually. Moreover, the successful conduct of an all India exam like NEET requires a whole-of-government mobilization across departments at the Union, State, and local government level. Thus, the NTA has extremely significant responsibilities and also faces the task of coordination with multiple stakeholders.

The NTA is in a continually evolving state and its organizing structure may be finalized such that the resources and accountability structures of the NTA are in correspondence with the responsibilities which it has been vested with. In doing so, the Department may introduce appropriate Parliamentary framework that ensures NTA’s accountability to Parliament.

10.2 The Committee notes that investment in question banks is the most viable defense against paper leaks in the long-run. The repeated use of the same question sets or the practice of having examiners set new question papers every year can be a risk to the integrity of the examination process. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that NTA should invest in building a large, diverse, and continuously updated question bank which can be drawn on to set papers without the advance knowledge of the question-setters. The Committee notes that in the CBT format, question papers no longer have to be printed and transported to examination centers. Therefore, there is no compulsion to set question papers long in advance. Accordingly, the final question papers should be set very close to the examination, with questions drawn from the question bank using digital tools and only vetted by experts. Finally, the Committee emphasizes strict quarantine and sequestering of the final paper-vetters until the conclusion of the examination.

The Committee further recommends that the NTA must rely on bona fide experts from our most renowned educational institutions – including IITs, AIIMSs, IIMs, etc. - to develop its question banks and for translation. The NTA must also develop a system to check the track record of said experts to establish their integrity and to rule out any conflict of interest (e.g., owners or faculty of private coaching centers, family members giving the exam, etc.) before recruiting them.

10.3 The institutional culture matters as much as the procedures. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that National Testing Agency needs to cultivate a culture where every official from the Director General to the centre invigilator sees themselves as a guardian of examination integrity, not just as a jobholder in an administrative system.

The Committee notes that recent challenges have affected the public trust in the National Testing Agency, and that rebuilding this trust will require consistent, transparent, and two-way communication with stakeholders. The Committee notes that the NTA's present engagement with candidates is largely confined to one-way communication through portals and notifications. It notes that the NTA’s channels for feedback from students and educational institutions need greater public awareness. The Committee recommends that such channels be built into the ordinary functioning of the NTA and be widely dispersed across students, parents, and instructors, so as to enable the agency to be more responsive to stakeholder concerns.

10.4 The Committee notes the measures taken by National Testing Agency since 2024. The institutional framework including SLCCs, DLCCs, Biometric authentication, mobile jammers, AI-based CCTV analysis is welcome. However, the cancellation of NEET (UG) 2026 despite all these measures shows the need for greater procedural and institutional reforms.

10.5 The Committee notes that of the 39 sanctioned positions in the NTA, only 23 officers are currently in position and on deputation to the NTA – a vacancy of 41%. The Committee notes that the hiring of manpower to strengthen the NTA was among the key recommendations of the High-Level Expert Committee chaired by Dr. K Radhakrishnan. The Committee notes the shortage of manpower in the NTA and urges the agency to expedite the recruitment to all sanctioned positions.

The Committee notes that all the 39 permanent posts that exist in the NTA are currently filled through a deputation mode. Officers on deputation generally serve for a limited tenure of two to three years before returning to their parent cadres. However, the conduct of national-level entrance examinations requires considerably expertise which is generally built over several years of experience. Accordingly, a dedicated cadre of professional staff is required for this purpose. The Committee recommends that the NTA should therefore hire its own officers on a permanent basis, with a particular emphasis on specialists in psychometrics, examination security, digital infrastructure, data analytics, and examination logistics. The 16 posts under the Central Staffing Scheme should be treated as a supplementary layer of senior leadership, not as a substitute for domain expertise.

10.6 The Committee observes that for CBT examinations conducted by NTA a concrete implementation plan for secure government CBT centers, including budgetary provisioning and a current mapping of existing government-owned facilities, needs to be finalized expeditiously. The Committee is of the view that adequate government-owned infrastructure must be in place so that reliance on private centers is avoided.

10.7 The Committee notes the recommendations made by the High-Level Committee of Experts (HLCE) for a phased transition to CBT mode, and broadly concurs with this approach. The Committee notes that most entrance examinations conducted by the NTA are already run on Computer-Based-Testing, including the JEE-Mains, UGC-NET, and CUET. The Committee notes that digital literacy constitutes a critically important academic and professional skill that is increasingly prevalent among the student population. The Committee notes that the NEET-UG is an outlier in its reliance on pen-and-paper testing. The Committee therefore recommends that NEET should also be moved to a CBT approach. 

The Committee however continues to have concerns about the accessibility of CBT to students from remote regions and from marginalized backgrounds. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the transition to CBT be accompanied by a concerted national testing strategy to maximize digital accessibility. Some features of the strategy may be as follows:

  1. For NEET (UG), any transition to CBT must be preceded by significant investment in government-owned CBT infrastructure across the country, particularly in Tier-2, Tier-3 cities and rural areas. The HLCE's recommendation of 1,000 secure government CBT centers must be implemented with a clear and phased timeline to facilitate the examinations. The Committee suggests that the NTA itself to financially support the establishment of mid-sized IT labs (100-200 nodes) in schools and colleges across the country. As long as the school/college administration provide the space for the IT lab, the NTA can invest in the hardware equipment needed on the condition that the facilities be given up to the NTA for the conduct of any examination required.
  2. The Committee emphasizes that there must be at least 1 test center in each district to offer all exams to minimize the stress and financial burden of transport and accommodation on students.
  3. The Committee notes that private institutions engaged as examination centres on a sub-contracted basis have often proved to be a weak link in examination security. Therefore, all centers must be owned and operated by the Union and/or State Governments.
  4. Students must also be offered opportunities to give CBT mock exams to enable them to familiarize themselves with the format and with a digital interface.
  5. The Ministry of Education may consider including CBT-based exams at the school level as well, to build familiarity with digital testing among students.
  6. Before rolling out the CBT mode, in places where infrastructure for CBT is inadequate due to the absence of computers and/or connectivity, the National Testing Agency should consider a hybrid model where the encrypted questions may be delivered to the exam centre directly and then printed there itself, which the Committee has been informed is feasible, until full CBT readiness is achieved.
  7. The multi-session nature of CBT-based NEET (UG) examination would require a robust, transparent, and independently audited normalisation methodology. This normalisation methodology should be developed and explained to the public before any transition to CBT.
  8. Switching over the NEET (UG) to CBT mode should involve consultations with the stakeholders viz. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, medical education regulators, students and their families.

10.8 The Committee takes note of two procedural concerns raised before it:

  1. Invigilators completing signing and checking formalities during the course of the examination disturbs the focus of students who are already racing against time; the Committee, therefore, is of the view that a separate 15 minutes window, before or after the test, be kept exclusively for such formalities and not in between the exam duration.
  2. Candidates arriving a few minutes late at the exam centers are mostly denied entry altogether resulting in wasting their year-long hard work over a minor delay. The Committee observes that there are some genuine reasons due to which a candidate may arrive late at the examination centre. The Committee is of the view that some mechanism be evolved such that students be allowed entry into the exam hall after signing an undertaking recording their late arrival and be allowed to attempt the exam only for the remaining time, with no extra time granted under any circumstances.

10.9 The Committee notes that public rallies, processions, or large gatherings on the day of examination can delay candidates and cause them to miss their reporting time. The Committee recommends that the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 be amended to direct District Administration to withhold permission for any rally, procession, or any other public gathering on examination days, and to ensure that smooth traffic and law-and-order arrangements are in place well in advance, so that no candidate is affected by an avoidable, external disturbance.

10.10 The Committee notes that presently NEET (UG) qualifies far more candidates than the seats available across MBBS, BDS, AYUSH, and nursing courses put together. A reasonably wide qualifying pool gives students a fair chance through counseling rounds and private or deemed seats, but an excessively wide gap creates needless stress for lakhs of students. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that NTA and the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare should undertake a data-based, year-wise review of the qualifying percentile and cut-off methodology, keeping the number of qualified candidates reasonably aligned to actual seat availability, without compromising merit.

10.11 The Committee notes that, contrary to the Civil Services Examination that follows a multi-stage format for filtration of candidates, NEET (UG) examination remains a single-stage test that covers MBBS, BDS, nursing, and AYUSH admissions together handling more than 22 lakh students. The Committee is of the view that NTA should examine the feasibility of a two-stage format for its large examinations, such as having a common prelims examination for all medical streams while conducting specialized mains stage for specific courses, so that a candidate seeking nursing or AYUSH is tested and ranked apart from one seeking admission to MBBS, reducing avoidable competition.

10.12 The Committee notes that firms involved in examination-related services such as paper setting, logistics, printing, administration etc. that have been blacklisted by one or more State government(s) or organisation(s) have continued to secure contracts with other States and organisations. There is currently no preventive mechanism to counter this malpractice.

The Committee recommends that NTA should create and maintain a National Registry of Blacklisted Examination Vendors. This registry should include the names of firms, their associated individuals and entities, the nature of the disqualification, and the authority that imposed it. It should be publicly accessible online. Contracting with any entity on this list by NTA, any State Government(s), or any other public examination authority should be considered under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The Committee notes that it has previously made the same recommendation in its 371st report on the Autonomous Bodies of the Higher Education Department.

10.13 The Committee notes that the coaching industry has effectively created a parallel curriculum that often matters more than the official school curriculum. It is a direct consequence of examination design choices. When examination papers tests beyond the NCERT or state board syllabus, or test rapid recall and pattern-recognition developed through repetitive practice rather than genuine conceptual understanding, they inevitably reward coaching over learning. This design has fostered a large, largely unregulated private coaching industry that displaced school-level learning as the primary site of preparation for these examinations. Moreover, it creates a barrier to socio-economic mobility by privileging students who can afford coaching have a structural advantage over equally talented students who cannot.

The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Education should ensure that there should be specific, measurable standards for ensuring that NEET (UG), JEE (Main), and CUET papers test conceptual understanding based on the official school curriculum, rather than rewarding techniques specific to coaching. Further, there should be a regulatory framework for the coaching industry, with attention to fee transparency, safety standards, and the mental health of students in coaching centers.

10.14 The Committee was informed, during the course of its meetings, that the NTA only has data on the number of candidates registered from different States for various examinations and no data on whether those students succeeded or not. Participation data and success data are very different things. A State may have high registration numbers but poor pass rates, pointing to a quality or access problem.

The Committee recommends that NTA should conduct an annual Equity Audit examining, for each major examination, the participation rates, pass rates, and cutoff achievement rates of candidates disaggregated by State, gender, school board type (government, aided, private), medium of instruction, and social category (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, general). The audit findings should be published in NTA's Annual Report and submitted to the Ministry of Education for policy consideration. The Ministry of Education may utilise the data for policy consideration.

10.15 The Committee notes that the intense pressure of a single high-stakes examination affects the mental health of lakhs of young candidates, before, during, and after the declaration of results. The Committee is of the view that NTA partners with mental health prof1essionals to offer free, accessible counseling helplines, circulate simple stress-management material well ahead of each examination, and ensure that examination centers maintain a calm, supportive environment, particularly during the sensitive period surrounding results.

10.16 During the course of its meetings, the Committee was apprised that presently NEET (UG) has no limit on how many times a candidate can attempt it, and no real upper age limit either. This has resulted in anomalies such as the participation of candidates above the age of 70 years in the NEET examinations. The Committee recommends that the Ministry explore, alongside the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and all other relevant stakeholders, possibilities of reasonable age limits and reasonable attempt limits to all major examinations including the NEET-UG. The Committee notes that an exception to this rule may be made only for the UGC-NET.

10.17 The Committee notes that the cooperation and expertise of the State Governments is critical to the success of the examinations. Therefore, it recommends that a revamped NTA must include adequate representation from State Governments on its Governing Body.

    1.  The Committee recommends that the NTA must be reimagined not just as a body to administer exams but as a think-tank for all matters and policies relating to examinations. The NTA must have a research wing staffed by academics with credentials in education research other than bureaucrats and officers. The absence of a research wing currently precludes the NTA from conducting critical tasks like longitudinal studies that gauge if the NEET, CUET, UGC-NET exams etc. actually fulfill their intended purpose.  Similarly, a NTA with deep academic expertise can also be a resource for other educational institutions like the CBSE which are implementing interventions like the introduction of an OnScreen Marking system in Board Examinations. The Committee thus recommends greater academic and research expertise in the NTA to help it better conduct its own examinations as well as eventually to facilitate non-NTA examinations.
    1.  The Committee notes that once the NTA's digital infrastructure has matured, examinations should be conducted on CBT basis with a Computer Adaptive Testing (CAT) model which is universally regarded as the gold standard for assessment. This will require the use of AI tools that can pull questions from a large question bank, modify them to the aptitude of the student, evaluate questions correctly, and normalize scores based on objective considerations such as the difficulty of the questions. Such a system will minimize the scope for malpractices. There will be no standard question paper that can be leaked. Further, no two candidates at the same center will receive an identical set of questions, reducing the scope for cheating. Accordingly, the NTA should set up a technical team with the proficiency to develop, monitor, and continuously strengthen these tools.
    1.  The Committee was informed by the NTA that the risk of a CBT examination would be that the computer system is vulnerable to hacking by malicious agents and that such hacks are also hard to track. The Committee was informed that such an attempt occurred and was investigated by the CBI during the IIT JEE-Mains Examination of 2021. The Committee notes that the transition to CBT therefore presents new challenges which the NTA must anticipate and be prepared for. In addition to live CCTV monitoring, the Committee recommends the establishment of a robust, in-house cybersecurity team within the NTA which can develop and implement secure examination software that prevents remote access, screen-recording, and the use of virtual machines. Further it must adopt AI-based analytical tools to detect and flag anomalous response patterns that may indicate malpractice.
    1.  The Committee notes that the Director General is the key executive officer in the NTA. However, between 23.06.2024 and 01.04.2026, the position was held as an additional charge by officers who had substantial primary responsibilities as CMD, ITPO and Commissioner, NVS. The Committee discourages the practice of appointing officers to key positions in the NTA as an additional charge.
    1.  While the number of sanctioned posts has increased since 2024, the Committee notes that even at full strength of 39 officers, the NTA will have to rely on third-party private contractors. The Committee recommends that the NTA must eventually grow its operations to be able to conduct the logistics of all examinations by itself. The use of non-NTA employees must be limited to the setting of papers and other academic functions for which reliance on outside academic expertise is critical.
    1.  The Committee notes that the NTA has a substantial annual revenue surplus, and in total has acquired a total revenue surplus of Rs. 590 crores between FY 2018-2019 and FY 2024-2025. The Committee was informed that the surplus funds available with NTA from time to time are being invested in Fixed Deposits for optimal utilization until they are required for operational purposes. The Committee notes that this corpus can be used for investment and upgradation in government-owned CBT centers and the conduct of the mock examinations to familiarize students with the CBT interface.
    1.  The Committee notes that the NEET-UG results are generally not published in a publicly accessible manner. However, in 2024, the NTA published the details on the instance of the Honourable Supreme Court and it sparked a larger public conversation on how student performance across cities and test centers varies. Consequently, the NTA cracked down on the ability of students to choose their own test centers. The Committee has noted that this is a progressive measure which has reduced scope for misuse. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the NTA should follow the practices adopted by the UPSC of transparency in results. The Committee notes that such transparency can enable the NTA to identify any anomalous patterns in the performance of candidates and test centers and enhance the public trust in the NEET examination.
    1.  The Committee envisions that the NTA should have in-house capabilities that can detect, trace, and determine prima facie irregularities in the examination system. Such in-house capabilities can strengthen the NTA’s ability to rapidly respond to crises. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Ministry consider building some of these abilities within the NTA.
    1.  The Committee notes that there is presently no official public record of paper leaks, the FIRs registered on paper leaks, and how these cases are being investigated and prosecuted by the CBI and other investigative agencies. The Department of Higher Education stated to the Committee that although examination malpractices/disruptions have occurred, no paper leak has occurred in an exam conducted by the NTA since its formation in 2017 till 2025. The Committee noted that the Ministry’s assertion is at variance with the opinion of some Members of the Committee. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the NTA work with the Department of Higher Education and other Government agencies and departments to issue a publicly-available report documenting all relevant details relating to the exams that have been conducted by the NTA and any investigations pertaining to them.
    2. The Committee notes that the Expert Committee chaired by Dr. K Radhakrishnan had recommended that the NTA's mandate be confined to the conduct of entrance examinations, with the NTA taking on additional functions only after demonstrating expanded institutional capacity. The Committee notes that the NTA continues to conduct recruitment examinations that are not connected to admission into higher education institutions. The Committee recommends that the NTA immediately refocus its priorities to the conduct of admission tests to higher education institutions alone. The Committee notes that such a refocusing would be in line with the NTA’s mission statement – “[T]o improve equity and quality in education by administering research based valid, reliable, efficient, transparent, fair and international level assessments.”
    3. The Committee recommends that the NTA should bring out a clear duty of care owed by it to candidates. It may include the provision of financial compensation for candidates affected by administrative cancellations and prescribe timelines for grievance redressal. This will reduce the financial and psychological burden that such events place on candidates.
    4. The Committee also recommends a secure channel for receipt of information and grievance redressal related to all aspects of examination.
    5. The Committee recommends the creation of an independent mechanism for Educational Examinations, functioning independently of the NTA, with powers to audit examination security protocols, investigate candidate grievances, and submit its report directly to the Ministry.
    6.  The Committee recommends that the NTA invest in the training and capacity-building of all relevant stakeholders – including those from State Governments and other agencies – who are actually responsible for the conduct of examinations at the district and test center-level, so that reforms are internalised rather than merely complied with.

10.32 The Committee notes that the implementation of the Dr. Radhakrishnan Committee’s 101 recommendations to strengthen the examination process is ongoing. The Committee was informed that the majority of reforms have been implemented, since 60 of the 101 recommendations pertained to the year 2025 and 2026. The Committee recommends the expedited implementation of the pending reforms, including for any of the 60 reforms relating to 2025 and 2026 that are yet to be implemented.

10.33 The Committee recommends that the NTA also develop a protocol for exam administration for students with disabilities who have distinct requirements and needs. The NTA should strengthen support for students with disabilities by ensuring accessible examination centres, the possibility of adequate scribes and compensatory time, accessible digital platforms, and a dedicated grievance-redressal mechanism. Such a provision can help enhance the accessibility of higher education to students.

10.34 The Committee recommends that to the extent that any printing is required post the transition to CBT-exams, it should be conducted only in NTA-owned and operated printing presses. There must be no reliance on private printers for the same.

10.35 The Committee recognizes that education remains a fundamental pillar of national progress and social development, with the potential to empower individuals and strengthen the nation’s future. The Committee believes that continued reforms in the examination system is now a national imperative, with a view to eliminating unfair means, reducing undue stress, and encouraging a more holistic assessment of students’ abilities. The Committee resolves to stay apprised of the matter and encourages all stakeholders to contribute ideas for this shared national mission of a better examination and education system.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
India Welcomes ITU Proposal for Joint Trials to Combat Cross-Border Telecom Fraud: Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani
Over 82 Lakh Fraudulent Mobile Connections Disconnected Through ASTR; Sanchar Saathi App Records Around 25 Million Downloads
Financial Fraud Risk Indicator helps Prevent Suspected Losses of Over ₹5,000 Crore in 15 Months
Technology, Regulation and Global Cooperation Key to Combating Fraudulent Communications: Dr Pemmasani
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani today, delivered the keynote address at the ITU Roundtable on “Implementing ITU Standards to Combat Fraudulent Communications.” The Roundtable was held on the sidelines of the ongoing India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 which was formally inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 08 October 2026, at Yashobhoomi.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Pemmasani stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has connected more than a billion people, and the next task is to ensure that connectivity comes with trust. Emphasising the need for international cooperation, he stated, “Fraud is a network problem. It needs a network answer. And because networks are global, the answer must also be global.”

Highlighting the growing threat of organised, cross-border fraud, including impersonation, digital arrest scams, AI-generated voice cloning and deepfakes, Dr Pemmasani noted that Indians lost over ₹22,800 crore to such fraud in 2024. He further added that the government had learnt what works and has now built its defences in layers.

Dr Pemmasani outlined India's five-layered approach to combating fraudulent communications, including real-time blocking of spoofed international calls, identification of fraudulent mobile connections through C-DOT's AI-based ASTR tool, citizen participation through Sanchar Saathi, intelligence sharing through the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP), and measures addressing emerging fraud channels.

The Union MoS highlighted that ASTR has helped disconnect over 82 lakh fraudulent connections, while the Sanchar Saathi app has recorded around 25 million downloads. The Digital Intelligence Platform connects over 1,600 organisations, including telecom operators, banks and law-enforcement agencies. The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator has helped prevent suspected financial losses exceeding ₹5,000 crore in 15 months.

Acknowledging the limitations of national solutions in addressing cross-border fraud, Dr Pemmasani highlighted the importance of ITU standards for digital verification of caller identity across international networks. He welcomed the ITU's proposal for joint trials involving governments, regulators, operators and technology companies, and affirmed India's readiness to contribute.

The Union MoS suggested beginning trials between willing countries on selected international routes, ensuring participation of different network technologies and incorporating lessons into the continued improvement of ITU standards. He further emphasised that as 6G networks are developed, trust must be designed in from the beginning.

Concluding his address, Dr Pemmasani emphasised that technology, regulation and collaboration must work together to combat fraudulent communications. “At home, India has moved from reaction to prevention. Now, with ITU, let us move from national solutions to global trust,” he stated.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Launches Special Campaign 6.0 Nationwide to Enhance Cleanliness and Reduce Pendency
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has launched Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd October 2026, with 610 of its offices across the country participating in the campaign. The campaign aims to enhance cleanliness in government offices and reduce pendency. Emphasis is also being laid on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

During the Preparatory Phase, all Media Units, along with their field formations, including the Main Secretariat, were directed to finalise targets, identify pending references and plan for space management.

Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting, Railways and Electronics & IT, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, interacted with senior officers of the Ministry and Media Units during the Preparatory Phase. He urged all concerned to cover every office, down to the lowest unit of the Ministry, and instructed that the campaign should continue beyond 31st October 2026 and become a year-round drive. Public dealing offices are to be given high priority, and good work needs to be publicised through various social media platforms.

Secretary (I&B), Shri Chanchal Kumar, reviewed the preparations for and implementation of the campaign with all Heads of Media Units and their Nodal Officers. He issued directions for taking appropriate and timely action to achieve the targets set for this year's campaign.

The Ministry has performed well in previous Special Campaigns, demonstrating a consistent commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring the timely disposal of pending matters. The efforts made during earlier campaigns have not only contributed to improving the cleanliness of offices but have also resulted in significant outcomes in revenue generation, space management and the disposal of physical files.

Since the inception of the Special Campaign in 2021, the Ministry has generated a total revenue of ₹36.20 crore. During this period, approximately 13.89 lakh kilograms of scrap was disposed of, 13.98 lakh square feet of space was freed, and 2.71 lakh physical files were weeded out. A total of 6,642 outdoor campaigns were conducted, and 15,496 spots were cleaned. The cumulative achievements, along with their year-wise details, are presented below.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches Citizen-First, Multilingual DST and MoST Websites to Make Science More Accessible to All
New redeveloped portals embody PM Sh Narendra Modi’s vision of citizen-first governance and the principle of “Science by the People, Science for the People”: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Redeveloped Websites offer a single-window platform for research grants, fellowships, scientific schemes and opportunities for students, researchers, start-ups and citizens, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
DBIM 3.0-compliant portals provide multilingual access in 22 languages, universal accessibility tools and seamless use across devices
Redevelopment aligns government digital platforms with common standards for branding, accessibility, security and citizen-centric service delivery
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said that the new redeveloped websites of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) launched today reflect Prime Minister Sh Narendra Modi’s vision of citizen-first governance by making scientific information accessible, inclusive and useful to people across the country.

Emphasising the public value of the initiative, he said that its guiding principle is “Science by the People, Science for the People”, with science made available, accessible and affordable. He also stressed the importance of enabling the flow of technologies across scientific domains and industries, allowing users to identify information and opportunities according to their requirements through a common digital platform.

Dr. Jitendra Singh launched the redeveloped official websites of DST, www.dst.gov.inand www.most.gov.in, developed in accordance with the Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM) 3.0 and the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps (GIGW) 3.0. Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, was present on the occasion, along with senior DST officials and representatives associated with the website development initiative. The redevelopment was undertaken jointly by DST, the National Informatics Centre (NIC), the project management team and the development agency, with content curated and validated by the department’s internal divisions.

The Minister said the platform would serve students, research fellows, researchers, academic institutions, innovators, start-ups, entrepreneurs, media professionals and citizens by providing single-window access to DST schemes, grants, fellowships, scientific programmes and other opportunities. The redesigned information architecture enables users to locate relevant information more efficiently, including eligibility criteria, application guidelines, calls for proposals, awards, results and official notifications. By bringing these resources together in a structured format, the portals aim to reduce the effort required to navigate government information and strengthen public participation in India’s science and technology ecosystem.

The websites feature a standardised information architecture covering major sections such as About DST, divisions, programmes and schemes, services, opportunities, documents, and news and updates. A structured scheme and opportunity finder facilitates the discovery of research and development funding, calls for proposals, awards and application forms, while a centralised document repository provides access to guidelines, policy documents, notifications, reports and administrative forms.

Reorganised listings of DST divisions, the organisational hierarchy and officers’ contact details support easier navigation and access to relevant institutional information. The platform also provides dedicated information on bilateral and multilateral science and technology cooperation for international stakeholders.

A key feature of the new websites is the integration of Bhashini, enabling access to content in 22 languages and widening the reach of scientific information among diverse audiences. The portals incorporate universal accessibility features, including adjustable font sizes, high-contrast display modes, link highlighting, letter-spacing and line-height adjustments, and screen-reader compatibility.

Their responsive design enables access across desktops, tablets and mobile devices while maintaining readability and usability. These features are intended to make government science and technology information more accessible to students, researchers, innovators and citizens with diverse needs.

The redevelopment follows the launch of DBIM 3.0 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) in March 2025. The manual provides a common framework for the visual identity, information architecture, content presentation and overall digital presence of government ministries and departments. Complementing this framework, GIGW 3.0 establishes requirements relating to website quality, accessibility, cybersecurity, usability and lifecycle management.

The initiative forms part of the Government of India’s broader effort to harmonise its digital footprint, bringing greater consistency to government websites through standardised branding, navigation and content presentation. The redevelopment therefore extends beyond visual redesign to encompass content restructuring, improved user experience and sustainable mechanisms for digital content governance.

The websites are supported by a modular Content Management System (CMS), facilitating content updates, future expansion and integration with external science and technology applications. Security measures include SSL/TLS encryption, cybersecurity assessments and adherence to applicable CERT-In guidelines. Content Delivery Network (CDN) integration supports faster loading, system stability and service availability during periods of high traffic, including scheme-result announcements and application deadlines. The redesigned news and updates section brings together press releases, calls for proposals, results and announcements, helping users access relevant scientific information and opportunities more conveniently.

Through improved discoverability, multilingual access, universal accessibility and a standardised digital framework, the redeveloped websites seek to strengthen transparency and public access to government science and technology resources. The initiative advances a more inclusive and citizen-centric digital environment in which students, researchers, institutions, entrepreneurs and citizens can engage more easily with scientific programmes, research opportunities and technological developments.

The guideline is being released and uploaded on the official website of MoSPI (link…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Release of Draft Guideline for Compilation Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates by Expenditure Approach with Base Year 2022-23
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi

The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, has prepared the draft guideline for Compilation of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) Estimates from Expenditure Side with Base Year 2022-23. The guideline is being released and uploaded on the official website of MoSPI (link attached below).

The draft guideline provides a uniform and comprehensive framework for compilation of GSDP estimates from the expenditure side across States and Union Territories, with the objective of ensuring consistency, comparability and methodological standardization under the revised base year framework.

The draft guideline elaborates the concepts, coverage, data sources, estimation procedures and methodologies for compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side, covering the major expenditure components, including Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE), Government Final Consumption Expenditure (GFCE), Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF), Changes in Inventories, Valuables and Net Exports. At present, some States/UTs are compiling estimates of GFCF and GFCE; however, PFCE estimates are not being compiled by any State/UT. The document, therefore, provides a comprehensive framework and methodological guidance to facilitate the compilation of these expenditure components at the State/UT level.

The guideline emphasizes the use of State-specific data sources and appropriate allocation indicators for estimation of various expenditure components, to the extent feasible. In cases where direct State-level data are not available, suitable allocation methodologies and relevant indicators have been recommended for deriving State-wise estimates in a consistent and comparable manner.

The compilation of GSDP from the expenditure side provides an important complementary approach to the production/income-side estimation of GSDP and would facilitate a comprehensive assessment of economic activity at the State/UT level. The estimates would also contribute towards strengthening the State-level national accounts framework and improving the consistency of State estimates with the methodology followed at the national level.

The release of draft guideline is an important step towards harmonization of estimation practices across States/UTs and strengthening the statistical capacity of State Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DESs) for the compilation of expenditure-side GSDP estimates.

The draft Guideline is available on the official website of MoSPI (https://www.mospi.gov.in/product/more/6-Documents) for wider dissemination and feedback from stakeholders by 28th October, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI to Install Retrofit Emission Control Devices on 25 DG Sets at Dwarka Expressway
Initiative aimed at strengthening compliance with air-quality norms and reducing emissions from diesel generator sets in Delhi-NCR
RECDs to be installed on DG sets used for the Expressway lighting and other associated operations, thereby strengthening emission-control measures during their operation
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi

In order to strengthen environmental protection measures on National Highway corridor in National Capital Region (NCR), National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has taken the initiative to install Retrofit Emission Control Devices (RECDs) on 25 Diesel Generator (DG) sets deployed at the 8.7 km long Package-IV of the Dwarka Expressway that connects Basai to Kherki Dhaula/Delhi-Gurugram Expressway cloverleaf intersection.

The initiative is being implemented in compliance with the directions of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) concerning the regulation of Diesel Generator (DG) sets in the NCR, with the objective of mitigating air pollution, particularly during the winter season under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). Dwarka Expressway Package IV falls within the Delhi NCR region, which experiences severe air pollution during the winter months. To improve ambient air quality during this critical period, CAQM has mandated regulation and emission control measures for DG sets operating in the area.

The RECDs will be installed on DG sets used for the Expressway lighting and other associated operations, thereby strengthening emission-control measures during their operation. The implementation involves installation, testing and commissioning of the RECDs, along with comprehensive maintenance support.

The RECD installation is part of NHAI's broader approach towards integrating environmental protection into National Highway construction and operation, particularly for projects located in the NCR. The initiative will help to ensure that DG sets required for essential National Highway-related operations are equipped with appropriate emission-control systems in line with the applicable regulatory framework. NHAI has also specified that GPS-tagged photographs of RECD installations at each DG-set/locations will be maintained for verification and compliance purposes.

NHAI’s environmental initiative for National Highway projects in the Delhi - NCR are aligned with the broader objective of ensuring that the expansion and operation of National Highway infrastructure is in line with strengthening compliance for air-quality norms.

item.dc:creator: Prime Minister's Office
item.description: Prime Minister's Office PM interacts with Team India representatives at 48th WorldSkills Competition Emphasising the importance of Skill training institutions, PM says they are no less than IITs and IIMs PM suggests that as technology evolves, young people must continuously acquire new skills and upgrade their existing capabilities PM emphasises the need for coordinated efforts to establish India as a global hub of skilled human resources Participants share their experiences of adapting to new tools, software, technical systems and work processes Posted On: 09 OCT 2026…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM interacts with Team India representatives at 48th WorldSkills Competition
Emphasising the importance of Skill training institutions, PM says they are no less than IITs and IIMs
PM suggests that as technology evolves, young people must continuously acquire new skills and upgrade their existing capabilities
PM emphasises the need for coordinated efforts to establish India as a global hub of skilled human resources
Participants share their experiences of adapting to new tools, software, technical systems and work processes
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with the representatives of Team India at WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026 at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, earlier today.

During the interaction, the participants shared their experiences during the competition. They expressed pride in representing their country at the world stage. The participants discussed adapting to new tools, software, technical systems and work processes during the international competition. They also spoke about the work being done by the government towards skill development which is helping youth.

Prime Minister congratulated the participants for representing India on the global stage. He urged them to become ambassadors of skill development. He said that practical skills are as important as academic degrees.

Highlighting the importance of specialised skills, Prime Minister said as technology evolves rapidly, young people must continuously acquire new skills, upgrade their existing capabilities and adapt to emerging technologies. He urged the participants to develop skills in line with the requirements of the international market and contribute to improving India's skill training ecosystem through their experiences and suggestions. He emphasised the need for coordinated efforts by youth, the Government and training institutions to establish India as a global hub of skilled human resources.

Prime Minister underlined the objective behind establishing a separate Ministry for Skill Development and said that the importance of skill training institutions is no less than IITs and IIMs. He encouraged the participants to share their experiences and suggestions with the Government to help improve India's skill training system.

WorldSkills is the world's leading international skills competition, bringing together young professionals from participating countries and regions to demonstrate excellence across a wide range of vocational and technical skills. WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, the 48th WorldSkills Competition, was held from 22 to 27 September 2026 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai. Team India secured 10th position at the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026, winning 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence. India was represented by its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors participating across 63 skills.

The interaction was also attended by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Minister of State for Education and senior officials of Government of India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
15th Meeting of ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Joint Committee held during 6-9 October 2026
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi

ASEAN hosted the 15th AITIGA Joint Committee and related meetings to review the progress and negotiations of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) at the ASEAN Secretariat, Jakarta, Indonesia, during 6th to 9th October 2026 along with other sub-committee meetings. The event was conducted in a hybrid format. The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Nitin Kumar Yadav, Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, and Ms. Mastura Ahmad Mustafa, Deputy Secretary General (Trade), Ministry of Investment, Trade & Industry, Malaysia. The meeting saw participation from delegates representing ASEAN countries, including Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Viet Nam.

Three out of eight Sub-Committees (SCs) under the AITIGA JC also held hybrid meetings on the sidelines of the 15th AITIGA JC, namely the Sub-Committee on Legal and Institutional Issues (SC-LII), the Sub-Committee on National Treatment on Market Access (SC-NTMA), and the Sub-Committee on Rules of Origin (SC-ROO). The meetings provided a valuable forum to deepen collaboration, enhance mutual understanding, and sustain constructive dialogue between both sides.

The Joint Committee (JC) directed all Sub-Committees to expedite pending chapters under the AITIGA Review, establishing firm, time-bound deliverables and urging close coordination to ensure measurable progress. Concluding on a productive note, India and ASEAN reaffirmed their shared commitment to a balanced, constructive, and forward-looking Agreement. Both sides underscored their shared commitment to resolve outstanding policy issues, deepen economic integration, and modernize the Agreement into a mutually beneficial framework that strengthens bilateral trade.

The next meeting of the AITIGA Joint Committee will be held in January 2027 in India in hybrid mode to review the progress made by the Sub-Committees and provide further guidance for the timely conclusion of the negotiations.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Garima Singh/Anushka Pandey

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

Rooted in India’s rich cultural heritage, Khadi combines traditional craftsmanship with sustainable…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Khadi and Village Industries: Weaving the Fabric of an Inclusive and Sustainable India
Khadi emerges as a symbol of sustainable livelihoods, women’s empowerment and India’s rich cultural heritage
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

Khadi and Village Industries (KVI) have continued to play a significant role in promoting rural livelihoods, generating employment and strengthening the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat. Rooted in India’s rich cultural heritage, Khadi combines traditional craftsmanship with sustainable production practices and provides livelihood opportunities, particularly in rural areas.

Khadi, being hand-spun and hand-woven, is based on the use of natural fibres and local production systems. Its labour-intensive and decentralised nature provides employment opportunities at different skill levels and contributes to sustainable rural development. The sector also supports the objectives of SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

Hand spinning remains the key differentiator between Khadi and handloom. Over the years, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has supported Khadi institutions through skill development, capacity building and upskilling initiatives. Measures such as enhancement of spinning and weaving wages from April 2025, support for improved working tools and infrastructure, and strengthened marketing interventions have further contributed towards improving artisan incomes and making traditional livelihoods economically sustainable.

Khadi has also evolved into a contemporary fashion and lifestyle choice. New product categories such as Khadi denim, designer saris, bridal wear, contemporary shirts and trousers have expanded its appeal among new-age consumers. The Centre of Excellence for Khadi at NIFT, Delhi has developed 2,129 Khadi design collections across multiple categories. The launch of Navyug Khadi, featuring 710 new products, and the wellness and yoga wear collection ‘Svadha’ have further contributed to the contemporary positioning of Khadi.

The Government has been supporting employment generation in the Khadi and Village Industries sector through schemes including Khadi Vikas Yojana, Gramodyog Vikas Yojana and PMEGP. Assistance is provided through financial support, working capital facilitation, quality raw materials, training, toolkits, wage support, marketing interventions, promotion of digital payments and social security measures. An evaluation study conducted by EDII, Ahmedabad, reported that more than 75 per cent of artisans across the schemes experienced a measurable increase in income following the interventions.

Khadi has also emerged as an important avenue for women’s economic empowerment and inclusive development. Around 80 per cent of approximately half a million Khadi artisans are women. Women’s participation has been particularly significant in areas such as Agarbatti, Handmade Paper, Honey Mission and Service Industries, providing them with greater opportunities for financial independence and sustainable livelihoods.

With growing global demand for handmade, traceable, natural and environmentally responsible products, Khadi and handmade products offer significant export potential. KVIC has registered as an Export Promotion Council (EPC) on the Trade Portal of the Consulate General of India in New York and has initiated efforts to facilitate greater international exposure for Khadi institutions.

The Government has also taken steps to strengthen the branding and market positioning of Khadi products. The GI tag awarded to Ponduru Khadi is expected to enhance the value realisation of its distinctive cotton and traditional spinning and weaving processes. Ponduru Khadi, Bharat Kasturi Cotton, Bengal Muslin and naturally coloured cotton products were also showcased at the inaugural BRICS MSME Forum held in Agra.

Technology upgradation and quality enhancement are being pursued alongside preservation of traditional practices. KVIC’s Central Sliver Plants are being modernised, with the plants at Chittadurga, Karnataka, and Kuttur, Kerala, having completed modernisation and becoming operational. The Chittadurga plant utilises solar energy for 50 per cent of its requirement, while wind power is being explored to further strengthen environmental sustainability. Technology upgradation of Khadi institutions and technology-based Common Facility Centres are also proposed to strengthen Village Industries clusters.

Khadi’s inherent environmental sustainability further enhances its relevance in the context of climate action and responsible consumption. Its energy-efficient and water-efficient production process, based on natural fibres and colours, contributes to a lower environmental footprint. KVIC, in collaboration with ICAR-CIRCOT, is exploring initiatives for developing naturally coloured cotton varieties aimed at reducing water use, chemical pollution and energy consumption associated with conventional dyeing processes.

Khadi also offers potential for recycling and upcycling through hand spinning, including the conversion of fibres and filaments that may not be suitable for mechanised spinning. Such initiatives have the potential to create additional employment opportunities while contributing to SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

The journey of Khadi—from a symbol of Swadeshi and the freedom movement to a contemporary fashion and lifestyle choice—reflects its ability to adapt to changing consumer preferences while retaining its traditional character. By bringing together heritage and innovation, employment and entrepreneurship, women’s empowerment and social inclusion, and economic activity and environmental responsibility, Khadi continues to contribute to the broader vision of inclusive and sustainable development.

The continued evolution of Khadi demonstrates that sustainable solutions can emerge not only from modern technologies but also from traditional practices that have been preserved and refined over generations. Through its artisans, spinners and rural entrepreneurs, Khadi continues to represent a distinctive model of inclusive growth, sustainable livelihoods and responsible production.

***

Sunil Kumar Tiwari

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal Highlights Need for Rigorous Legal Thinking at CTIL’s 9th Anniversary Celebration CTIL Releases 9th Anniversary Magazine on Trade and Sustainability, Launches Special Edition of Investment Law Compass Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal, in his video address at the 9th Anniversary Celebration of Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), held at the Prime Minister’s Museum and Library in New Delhi, on 7 October 2026, said that established rules were…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal Highlights Need for Rigorous Legal Thinking at CTIL’s 9th Anniversary Celebration
CTIL Releases 9th Anniversary Magazine on Trade and Sustainability, Launches Special Edition of Investment Law Compass
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi

Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal, in his video address at the 9th Anniversary Celebration of Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), held at the Prime Minister’s Museum and Library in New Delhi, on 7 October 2026, said that established rules were being questioned, while emerging issues such as sustainability-linked trade measures and digital trade were reshaping the global trade agenda. He noted that rigorous legal thinking was more important than ever and that CTIL, as a leading institution in the field, was well placed to contribute to it.

Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal, congratulated CTIL on completing nine years and noted that the Centre had earned the trust of the Government, industry and the wider trade law community through its sustained and rigorous work. He recalled CTIL’s contributions to the Department of Commerce through legal analysis and specialised support in free trade agreement negotiations, dispute settlement and institutional memory building.

India needs institutions like CTIL that do more than follow developments in international economic law and are capable of shaping them, noted Justice P. S. Narasimha, Judge, Supreme Court of India.

Justice Narasimha observed that international investment law has evolved from an initial focus on the protection of foreign investment towards greater recognition of the regulatory freedom of States. He noted that the field is now entering a phase in which questions of institutionalisation, legitimacy and the long-term balance between investment and public power have assumed greater significance. He underscored the need for a durable international investment law framework that balances investment protection with the regulatory authority of States.

Head, CTIL, Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), and WTO India Chair, Prof. James J. Nedumpara, highlighted that CTIL was established to strengthen India’s trade capacity as a broader element of economic statecraft. He noted that CTIL had provided more than 4,000 legal opinions, participated in negotiations concerning nearly 10 free trade agreements, and contributed to WTO negotiations, submissions, notifications and dispute settlement.

Additional Secretary, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Yashvir Singh, delivered the Special Address and highlighted CTIL’s contributions to India’s major trade engagements, including support for major free trade agreements and engagements such as the G20 and BRICS over the past several years. He also highlighted CTIL’s work in WTO negotiations, notifications and dispute settlement, along with its contributions to India’s economic diplomacy and the development of human capital in international economic law.

Vice Chancellor, IIFT, Dr. K. Rangarajan, in his address, recalled the evolution of specialised trade-policy institutions at IIFT. He highlighted CTIL’s growing role in providing timely expertise for international trade negotiations and policy interventions.

Joint Secretary, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Smt. Kapil Chaudhary, highlighted CTIL’s expanding research in emerging areas, including critical minerals, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, supply chains, climate and sustainability. She also emphasised the need for institutional knowledge management and greater capacity building within the Department of Commerce.

On the occasion, the ninth anniversary issue of the CTIL Magazine, titled “The Emerging Sustainability Landscape: Responding to Shifting Winds”, was released. The magazine examines the future opportunities and challenges that developing countries may face as they seek to participate in the evolving intersection of trade and sustainability. A special anniversary edition of Investment Law Compass, CTIL’s monthly newsletter on developments in investment law and policy, was also launched.

The formal proceedings concluded with the presentation of Distinguished Long Service Awards to members of the CTIL faculty and staff.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Ishita Biswas

item.title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Tighter Curbs on Advertising of Prescription Drugs by Retailers and Wholesalers
item.category: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Health Ministry Proposes Tighter Curbs on Advertising of Prescription Drugs by Retailers and Wholesalers Draft amendment seeks to extend existing restrictions on advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X medicines to drug retailers, wholesalers and distributors Move aims to curb unauthorised promotion of prescription medicines and strengthen safeguards for public health Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 11:10AM by PIB Delhi The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to strengthen…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Proposes Tighter Curbs on Advertising of Prescription Drugs by Retailers and Wholesalers
Draft amendment seeks to extend existing restrictions on advertisements of Schedule H, H1 and X medicines to drug retailers, wholesalers and distributors
Move aims to curb unauthorised promotion of prescription medicines and strengthen safeguards for public health
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 11:10AM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to strengthen regulation of advertisements relating to prescription-only medicines. The proposed amendment seeks to extend the existing requirement of prior Central Government sanction for advertising drugs specified under Schedule H, Schedule H1 and Schedule X to entities holding licences for the sale and distribution of drugs.

The draft amendment has been notified through Gazette Notification G.S.R. 861(E), dated 28 September 2026, following consultations with the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB).

Under the existing regulatory framework, pharmaceutical manufacturers are prohibited from advertising drugs covered under Schedule H, Schedule H1 and Schedule X without prior sanction of the Central Government. However, corresponding provisions have not explicitly covered entities engaged in the retail and wholesale sale and distribution of these medicines.

To address this regulatory gap, the Ministry has proposed the insertion of sub-rule (22) under Rule 65 of the Drugs Rules, 1945, extending the advertisement restriction to holders of licences to sell, stock, exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute drugs, including retail and wholesale drug licence holders.

Under the proposed provision, no advertisement of drugs specified in Schedule H, Schedule H1 or Schedule X shall be made except with the previous sanction of the Central Government.

The proposed amendment is intended to strengthen regulatory oversight across the pharmaceutical supply chain, discourage unauthorised promotion of prescription medicines and reduce risks associated with inappropriate self-medication.

The measure is expected to reinforce safeguards relating to medicines that require appropriate medical supervision, including certain antibiotics, psychotropic medicines and other prescription-only drugs.

The proposal follows the recommendations of the 93rd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board, held on 16 February 2026, which considered the need for appropriate provisions governing advertisements by drug sale and distribution licence holders.

The Ministry has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the draft rules are made available to the public. Submissions received within the prescribed period will be considered by the Central Government before finalisation of the amendment.

Link to the Official Gazette: https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2026/276941.pdf

***

SR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Coal supply to power plants gathers pace in October
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 10:54AM by PIB Delhi

Some recent media reports flag growing risk of Power shortages in India as coal inventories at power plants fall to low levels. In this context, the Ministry of Coal would like to clarify the following.

The "critical stock" tag is a norm-based trigger (plants holding less than the prescribed threshold of normative stock) and is designed to flag plants early, well before actual fuel shortage or generation loss occurs. A plant appearing on this list is, by design, an early-warning entry and not an indication that it has run out of coal or is at imminent risk of shutting down.

Coal stock position needs to be viewed alongside the improvement since the September trough in supplies. Daily supplies to the power sector have risen by around 36% from the September low, with October averaging about 9% higher than September. The rate of stock depletion has also moderated significantly (Figure 1). Rail loading has strengthened correspondingly, averaging over 465 rakes per day in October, with the 470-rake target achieved on three consecutive days (Figure 2). Supplies through other modes, including road, have also improved.

Figure 1: Depletion/Accretion in DCB Plants (MT)

Figure 2: Total rake loading trend, October 2026

Stock depletion has slowed sharply, with the daily drawdown falling by more than half from 0.243 MT/day in September to 0.116 MT/day in October. The position is therefore stabilising, although stock rebuilding is yet to commence.

The rise in plants with critical stocks is being closely monitored, with requirement-based redistribution of coal to vulnerable stations to ensure adequate supplies and uninterrupted power generation. With the monsoon receding and peak demand expected to moderate by mid-October (as per historical trends) sustained loading of 465–475 rakes per day should support further stabilisation and enable stock rebuilding ahead of the festive, winter and subsequent summer demand periods, thereby reducing the number of plants in the critical category.

The Ministry of Coal, in close coordination with the Ministries of Railways and Ministry of Power, is actively monitoring supplies and logistics to ensure that coal availability does not constrain power generation anywhere in the country.

****

Shuhaib T

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam emphasizing on virtues of dignity and humility
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 9:26AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam emphasizing on the virtues of dignity and humility: 

"वत्सराजोऽपि तं प्राप्तं प्रदत्तोपायनं नृपम्।

प्रीत्या सम्मानयामास शूरा हि प्रणतिप्रियाः॥"

The verse underscores the noble tradition of welcoming others with dignity and extending respect and warmth to those who approach with humility.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
India and Mali commemorate World Cotton Day at United Nations Headquarters in New York
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 8:10AM by PIB Delhi

The Permanent Missions of India and Mali to the United Nations jointly organized an event on the theme “Cotton for Sustainability: Livelihoods, Value Addition and Partnership” at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 7 October 2026, commemorating World Cotton Day. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 7 October as World Cotton Day through resolution 75/318. The observance draws attention to cotton’s role in economic development, international trade and poverty alleviation, particularly in developing and least developed countries. The event brought together Members of Parliament from India, representatives of Member States and international organizations to discuss cotton’s contribution to livelihoods, value addition and the Sustainable Development Goals.

In his welcome remarks, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations, recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s association of cotton and the spinning wheel with self-reliance, dignity and India’s freedom struggle. He highlighted four priorities: supporting producers’ livelihoods; expanding value addition and access to markets; promoting sustainability; and strengthening technology and partnerships. He emphasized the need for affordable inputs and finance, support for smaller enterprises, and South-South and triangular cooperation to help cotton-producing countries retain more value and advance the SDGs.

Ambassador Issa Konfourou, Permanent Representative of Mali to the United Nations, highlighted cotton’s importance to Mali’s economy and rural livelihoods. He underscored the challenges posed by limited processing capacity, input costs, market access and trade-distorting support. Outlining Mali’s efforts to expand domestic processing and create employment, he welcomed mutually beneficial partnerships, including South-South cooperation, and acknowledged India as a key partner.

Asit Kumar Mal, Member of Parliament, drew on the experience of Kantha embroidery in Bolpur, West Bengal, to highlight how traditional craftsmanship adds value to cotton, supports women’s livelihoods and promotes reuse and resource efficiency. He emphasized the importance of fair remuneration, affordable credit, design support and market access for artisans.

L. K. Sudhish, Member of Parliament, highlighted Tamil Nadu’s experience in cotton knitwear and garment manufacturing, including the contribution of smaller enterprises, shared infrastructure and skilled workers. He referred to the integrated textile park being developed under the PM MITRA initiative and wastewater recovery and reuse in textile processing.

Ms. Padmini Singla, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, highlighted India’s role as a major producer and consumer of cotton and the sector’s importance to small and marginal farmers. She outlined the Mission for Cotton Productivity and the Kasturi Cotton Bharat initiative, emphasizing improved productivity, quality and traceability. She also highlighted investments in textile infrastructure, support for artisans and small enterprises, and the importance of open, predictable trade and market access for sustainable cotton value chains.

The Permanent Representatives of Côte d’Ivoire, Uzbekistan, Chad, the Netherlands, Burkina Faso and Egypt, and the Deputy Permanent Representatives of Cameroon and Peru; Ms. Angélica Jácome, Director, Food and Agriculture Organization Liaison Office with the United Nations in New York; and Dr. Keshav R. Kranthi, Chief Scientist, International Cotton Advisory Committee, spoke on the occasion. The discussion focused on opportunities to strengthen cotton value chains, support smallholders and artisans, improve processing capacity and market access, encourage use of technology and advanced science in the sector and deepen international partnerships.

Participants also enjoyed a hands-on experience of Pen Kalamkari on cotton, guided by a master artisan from India, celebrating India’s rich craft traditions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Union Finance Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman on visit to Singapore for high-level meetings with Singapore Leadership and CEOs of business firms in Singapore
FM Smt. Sitharaman to participate in Business Roundtable with Hedge Fund and Portfolio Fund Managers
Posted On: 09 OCT 2026 7:46AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman is on an official visit to Singapore from 9th to 11th October 2026. During the official visit, FM Smt. Sitharaman will hold a series of high-level engagements with the leadership of Singapore, senior members of the business and investment community, and global institutional investors.

During the visit, Smt. Sitharaman will call on H.E. Mr. Tharman Shanmugaratnam, President of Singapore; H.E. Mr. Lawrence Wong, Prime Minister of Singapore; Mr. Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore; and Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan, Foreign Minister of Singapore.

The discussions will cover key areas of the India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and take forward the outcomes of the ISMR, including cooperation in trade and investment, digital financial connectivity, capital markets, taxation, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, skilling and aviation.

Singapore is India’s largest source of FDI, with cumulative FDI inflows of around USD 194.68 billion during April 2000–March 2026. Singaporean institutional investors, including GIC and Temasek, have significant investments across the Indian economy.

As part of her engagements with the investment community in Singapore, the Union Finance Minister will engage with leading Singaporean and international investors, financial institutions and business leaders through a Roundtable with Hedge Fund and Portfolio Fund Managers and a series of Government-to-Business (G2B) meetings. The interaction will provide an opportunity for an exchange of views with leading global investors on India’s growth trajectory, investment opportunities and the evolving global economic and financial landscape.

FM Smt. Sitharaman will also hold a series of one-to-one meetings with senior business leaders and heads of leading global financial institutions, investment firms and healthcare companies. These will include meetings with the Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) of the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC); Temasek Holdings (P) Limited (Temasek);  DBS Bank Ltd. (DBS); Standard Chartered Bank; British International Investment (BII);  IHH Healthcare Berhad (IHH); Asia-Pacific, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Inc. (MUFG); B Capital; HPS Investment Partners (HPS); Chairperson, Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB (SEB); Director, Board of Directors, Mitsui & Co., Ltd.; and Executive Chairman and Founding Partner, TPG.

Platforms such as the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and GIFT City can provide avenues for greater participation by Singaporean capital, including through investment vehicles and funds.

The Ministry of Finance, in coordination with relevant Ministries and industry bodies, will facilitate connections between interested Singaporean investors and Indian companies, financial institutions and State Governments, and provide necessary handholding to take identified investment opportunities forward.

The visit underscores India’s commitment to deepening its Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Singapore, with a particular focus on leveraging the strong political relationship to promote greater investment, business partnerships and concrete economic outcomes.
