item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs observes Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 10:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance, along with its attached/subordinate offices and organisations under its administrative control, is undertaking Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. The Campaign is being implemented across Government under the coordination of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) with the objective of institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, improving record management and enhancing the experience of citizens in Government offices.

A key focus of Special Campaign 6.0 is “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste”, building upon the emphasis on scientific management of e-waste in previous campaigns. The Campaign seeks to ensure responsible handling and disposal of e-waste in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, while also promoting cleanliness, efficient use of office space and improved workplace experience. Particular attention is being given to field and outstation offices providing public services or having direct public interface.

During the Campaign, DEA is undertaking focused action on the identification and disposal of pending references from Members of Parliament, State Governments, inter-Ministerial references, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, Public Grievances and grievance appeals. The Campaign also provides an opportunity to strengthen record management through review, categorisation, recording and weeding out of physical records and closure of e-files, in accordance with extant Government guidelines.

As part of the Campaign, DEA is also undertaking cleanliness drives, space management, disposal of scrap and redundant materials, and identification and implementation of process simplification measures. The Department is coordinating with its concerned offices and organisations for effective implementation and monitoring of the identified targets. The Campaign also encourages adoption and documentation of best practices, including initiatives relating to e-waste management, digitization, efficient management of space, environment-friendly practices, citizen-centric initiatives and innovative practices.

The implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 is being monitored through the SCDPM portal, with progress being reviewed on a regular basis. DEA remains committed to achieving tangible outcomes through the Campaign and to sustaining the gains achieved in Swachhata, e-waste management, pendency reduction, record management, efficient use of office space and citizen-centric service delivery.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
As part of ‘Khadi Festival-2026’ at I.N.A. KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel inaugurated a special Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition at Delhi Haat
A glimpse of Mini India seen as India’s diverse heritage adorned in 115 stalls of Khadi and PMEGP unit products; Exhibition to continue til October 15th
The prime objective of the exhibition is to convey Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call of ‘Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi’ to the masses and Gen-Z : KVIC Chairman
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 10:24PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the vibrant confluence of India’s diverse cultural heritage, traditional craftsmanship and indigenous entrepreneurship, The distinct Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition organized by Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India was inaugurated by Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, KVIC at Delhi Haat, I.N.A. The exhibition, which will be held till October 15, 2026 has a total of 115 stalls. Of these, 48 stalls belong to Khadi while the remaining stalls belong to entrepreneurs and artisans belonging to Gramodyog & PMEGP units. Artisans, Khadi institutions, village industries units and entrepreneurs from almost every part of the country have displayed their products here. The exhibition at Delhi Haat appears as a MINI INDIA of sorts. The inaugural function was attended by the CEO of KVIC, Joint Secretary (ARI) of the Ministry of MSME, Financial Advisor of KVIC, officers, employees, representatives of Khadi institutions and artisans.

On the occasion of the inauguration, Chief Guest,  Chairman KVIC Shri Manoj Goel, said that KVIC has organized this exhibition to convey the call of the Swadeshi movement  of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to the masses and Gen-Z. He added that Khadi and village industries are not just a medium for selling products but transmit a story of hard work and self-reliance of millions of artisans, weavers and rural entrepreneurs of the country. The exhibition, held at Delhi Haat, presents the same vibrant tradition of different parts of the country on one platform. He said that marketing local products and providing quality indigenous alternatives to consumers is important for comprehensive expansion of Khadi and village industries. He appealed to Delhiites and tourists visiting Delhi to visit the exhibition of Delhi Haat, see the products of Indian artisans and rural entrepreneurs and give priority to indigenous products in their purchases.

Chairman KVIC Shri Goel said that Khadi and village industries are not just a medium of selling products but inherit a saga of hard work, skill and self-reliance of millions of artisans, weavers and rural entrepreneurs. “The Modi government is not only preparing a whole ecosystem of employment by connecting the youth with not just employment but also skills, entrepreneurship, finance and markets. Khadi and Village Industries are becoming strong medium of new opportunities for rural youth in this direction,” he said.

The speciality of the exhibition is that specific Khadi, textile and village industry products of different geographical regions of India can be seen and purchased at one place. Participants from Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Kerala in South India have arrived with special Khadi and silk products. The silk products of Karnataka, the traditional weaving and silk of Tamil Nadu, the kalamkari products of Andhra Pradesh, the Ikkat tradition of Telangana and the traditional textile craft style of Kerala are attracting visitors here. From East India, the fine muslin and handloom tradition of West Bengal, silk and tusser products of Bihar and traditional weaving and ikat crafts of Odisha can be seen. Attractive products made of Khadi as well as bamboo and natural materials from Northeast India are major attraction of the exhibition. Traditional silk products of Assam as well as handicraft and bamboo craft products of the Northeast are also presented here.

A large number of participants have also arrived from North and West India with their distinctive products. Traditional textile and handicraft traditions of Gujarat, colorful handicrafts and traditional prints of Rajasthan, woolen products of Himachal Pradesh, traditional weaving and handicrafts of Uttar Pradesh, rural products of Haryana and natural and tribal crafts of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh are being displayed here. Additionally, participants from other states of the country have also arrived with Khadi textiles, silks, handicrafts, natural products, food processed materials, herbal products and village industry products associated with the traditional identity of their respective regions.

During an interaction with the media, Chairman KVIC  Shri Manoj Goel said that as a result of the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and Village Industries sector has also made unprecedented progress. The turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector stood at over Rs 1.87 lakh crore in the financial year 2025-26, while more than 2.04 crore people are getting employment through this sector. He expressed confidence that the sector will also achieve the turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore in the coming time.

***

These margins will be limited to 30% of the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) . The measure is expected to reduce medicine prices by up to 70% and help cancer patients save ₹2,500 crore…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Government Expands Cancer Medicine Price Controls; Cancer Patients Expected to Save ₹2,500 Crore Annually
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

 1. Extending price protection to more cancer medicines

Government has approved a cap on the margins charged in the supply and sale of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.

These margins will be limited to 30% of the Maximum Retail Price (MRP). The measure is expected to reduce medicine prices by up to 70% and help cancer patients save ₹2,500 crore annually, significantly reducing the amount they pay from their own pockets.

Essential cancer medicines included in the scheduled list are already subject to strict government-set ceiling prices. The new decision extends price protection to non-scheduled cancer medicines, which are outside that list, by limiting the margins added before they reach patients.

An expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) will finalise the list of medicines to be covered. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) will then take a decision and issue the notification.

2. Reducing the heavy cost of cancer treatment

Cancer incidence is rising in India, with approximately 60 people per one lakh population affected by cancer. Treatment places a heavy financial burden on patients and their families, who often have to pay substantial amounts from their own pockets.

NPPA’s analysis of market data found that non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines carry an average price mark-up of approximately 170%, reaching 700% or more in some cases. In simple terms, the price rises sharply as the medicine moves through the supply chain before reaching the patient.

Prices also vary significantly depending on whether the medicine is bought from a retail pharmacy, a hospital pharmacy or an online pharmacy.

State authorities, including those in Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Karnataka, along with patients and civil society, have raised serious concerns about excessive medicine prices. These concerns have also been voiced on public platforms, particularly over the large gap between the price at which medicines are purchased for sale and the MRP charged to consumers.

Such high margins, especially on expensive cancer medicines, substantially increase patients’ treatment costs. The new cap will curb excessive profiteering, address unfair pricing practices in the market and help ensure fairer prices for patients. 

3. Building on the relief delivered by the 2019 decision

The Government’s earlier intervention shows how limiting these margins can bring substantial relief to patients.

In February 2019, on the Government’s direction, NPPA capped trade margins on 42 selected non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.

That decision reduced MRPs by up to 91%, with reported annual savings of ₹984 crore across 526 brands. It significantly reduced the financial burden on cancer patients and improved their ease of living.

Building on that experience, and addressing the pricing problems identified in the supply chain, the Government has now approved the wider cap. The expected annual savings of ₹2,500 crore will bring further relief to patients undergoing cancer treatment.

4. Maintaining production and ensuring continued availability

To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels.

The intervention will cover non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines across categories: branded and generic, domestically produced and imported, and patented and non-patented. This will help patients significantly benefit from lower prices while ensuring continued availability of the medicines they need.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister welcomes GST Council’s recommendations for simpler, trust based tax administration
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 9:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister,  Shri Narendra Modi has welcomed the new round of GST reforms approved by the GST Council, describing the recommendations as a significant step towards making the Goods and Services Tax regime simpler, more efficient and citizen-friendly. Shri Modi highlighted the Council’s recommendations relating to the removal of arrest provisions, greater decriminalisation and simplification of procedures, noting that these measures would have a positive impact on taxpayers and businesses.

Shri Modi posted on X:

I welcome the new round of GST reforms approved by the GST Council.  

The Council’s recommendations on removal of arrest provisions, greater decriminalisation and simpler procedures will have a very positive impact. 

The focus is clear:

Faster decisions. 

Lower compliance costs. 

Automated refunds. 

Trust-based administration.

These are in line with our constant efforts to make GST more efficient, transparent and citizen-friendly.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026
Bharat 6G Alliance Signs 5 MoUs and Unveils 9 White Papers on 6G Technology
Joint Report on the Progress of the New Delhi 6G Declaration Also Released
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi

The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026, being organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, was inaugurated today by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Government of India.

The Symposium brings together policymakers, global technology alliances, telecom operators, industry leaders, academia, research institutions and other stakeholders from across the world to advance collaboration towards the development of next-generation communication technologies and India’s 6G ambitions.

The inauguration marked a significant milestone in India’s journey towards building a globally competitive, indigenous and trusted 6G ecosystem, with the exchange of five new Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and the release of nine Working Group white papers by the Bharat 6G Alliance.

Five New MoUs to Strengthen Global and Industry Collaboration

During the inaugural ceremony, the Bharat 6G Alliance exchanged MoUs with:

  1. GSMA
  2. one6G Association
  3. GTI Alliance Ltd
  4. 6G Industry Forum (6GIF)
  5. VoICE

These collaborations further strengthen the Bharat 6G Alliance’s engagement with leading global and industry stakeholders and reinforce India’s commitment to international cooperation in research, innovation, standards, technology development and deployment for next-generation networks.

With these new collaborations, the Bharat 6G Alliance builds further upon its existing international and domestic partnerships. The Alliance already has 10 global and 2 domestic MoUs/MoI collaborations, taking its broader partnership network to 17 collaborations.

Nine New White Papers Released

The Bharat 6G Alliance also released nine Working Group white papers, reflecting the collective technical contributions of its industry, academia, research and technology ecosystem.

  1. 6G Technology Landscape Survey and Roadmap for R&D, Platforms and Trials in India
  2. Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) for 6G: Technologies, Architectures, Applications, and Future Directions
  3. Fixed Wireless Access: Bharat’s Broadband Backbone from 5G to 6G
  4. Role of Optical Technologies for 6G
  5. A Perspective on IMT Spectrum Readiness towards 2030 and Beyond
  6.  Sustainable 6G: Designing Networks for a Carbon Net Zero Future
  7. Cellular and WiFi Synergy: Global Pathways to Inclusive Connectivity
  8. Captive Non-Public Network (CNPN)
  9. Security for 6G

The publications address critical technological and policy dimensions of India’s 6G journey, including technology development and trials, spectrum readiness, sensing and communications, broadband connectivity, optical technologies, sustainability, enterprise networks, Wi-Fi–cellular convergence and security.

One-Year Progress on the New Delhi Declaration

A key highlight of the inaugural ceremony was the release of the Joint Report: “Progress towards the 6G Principles of the New Delhi Declaration: Actions, Outcomes and Outlook – First Edition, October 2026.”

The report marks the completion of one year since the New Delhi Declaration was endorsed at the International Bharat6G Symposium 2025 and captures the progress, actions and outcomes reported by the participating MoU partners towards advancing the principles articulated in the Declaration.

The New Delhi Declaration provides a common framework for advancing 6G as a secure, resilient, open, interoperable, inclusive and sustainable technology ecosystem, with emphasis on international collaboration in research, innovation and standardisation.

The progress report provides an important mechanism for taking stock of the collective efforts of the participating partners and identifying the outlook for continued cooperation towards the realisation of these principles.

India’s Growing Role in the Global 6G Ecosystem

The initiatives announced at the Symposium reaffirm the Bharat 6G Alliance’s role as a platform bringing together Indian and international stakeholders to shape the technological, standards and ecosystem dimensions of 6G.

The Alliance continues to facilitate collaboration across industry, academia, research institutions and government stakeholders, while supporting India’s participation in global standardisation, technology development, trials, intellectual property creation and international partnerships.

The release of the white papers, the expansion of the MoU network and the one-year progress report on the New Delhi Declaration collectively demonstrate the growing momentum of India’s engagement with the global 6G ecosystem.

The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026, being held from 7–9 October 2026 at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, features discussions on global 6G vision, standards and technology leadership, trials and testbeds, AI-native and sustainable networks, spectrum, industry applications and international cooperation.

The Bharat 6G Alliance will continue to work with its members and international partners towards building a secure, inclusive, sustainable and globally interoperable 6G ecosystem, strengthening India’s contribution to the global development of next-generation telecommunications.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi chaired the two-day Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 9:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi chaired the two-day Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development in New Delhi today. Minister of State, Smt. Savitri Thakur also participated in the Summit.

On X, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi wrote that “Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, this summit will further strengthen Centre-State coordination and the effective implementation of initiatives aimed at empowering women and ensuring the holistic development of children.”

The Minister said that the summit will bring together Ministers of Women and Child Development from various states, along with senior officials from the Central and State Governments. She also wrote that key discussions will focus on women’s empowerment, child development, nutrition, safety, and welfare.

On X, Minister of State, Smt. Savitri Thakur wrote that “Under the able leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, the Central Government is continuously working towards a safe, healthy, and dignified future for women and children.”

She also wrote that experiences were shared between states and Union Territories on three important topics – strengthening Anganwadi centres further for better nutrition and early education, fortifying security arrangements for children living in vulnerable conditions, and the effective implementation of institutional and legal provisions related to women's safety.

The Minister also wrote that better coordination between the Centre and the states in the interest of women and children, exchange of experiences, and effective implementation of schemes at the grassroots level will further strengthen efforts.

Chaired the two-day Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development in New Delhi today. The summit will bring together Hon’ble Ministers of Women and Child Development from various states, along with senior officials from the Central and State Governments. Key discussions will focus on women’s empowerment, child development, nutrition, safety, and welfare. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji, this summit will further strengthen Centre-State coordination and the effective implementation of initiatives aimed at empowering women and ensuring the holistic development of children.

— Annpurna Devi (@Annapurna4BJP) October 8, 2026

item.dc:creator: National Human Rights Commission
item.description: National Human Rights Commission NHRC, India concludes its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp Sitting in Patna More than 70 cases including bonded labour heard in the presence of complainants, victims and officers concerned More than Rs 1 crore paid as relief to the victims on NHRC recommendations; more than Rs. 50 lakh as relief in other cases Senior officers sensitised on the issues pertaining to crime against women, children and timely submission of reports The Commission also interacted with the representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations and human rights defenders to strengthen…
item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India concludes its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp Sitting in Patna
More than 70 cases including bonded labour heard in the presence of complainants, victims and officers concerned
More than Rs 1 crore paid as relief to the victims on NHRC recommendations; more than Rs. 50 lakh as relief in other cases
Senior officers sensitised on the issues pertaining to crime against women, children and timely submission of reports
The Commission also interacted with the representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations and human rights defenders to strengthen coordination
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India led by Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian today concluded its two-day Bihar Open Hearing and Camp sitting in Patna. The Chairperson and Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard more than 70 alleged cases of human rights violations in the presence of victims and concerned officers. The State Chief Secretary, Shri Pratyaya Amrit and DGP, Ms. Preeta Verma, NHRC Secretary General, Shri Piyush Goyal, DG (I), Smt. Anupama Nilekar Chandra, Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar and other senior officers were present.

On Day-1, the Commission heard 30 cases and closed 19 cases after hearing the parties and finding the recommendations complied with. The State submitted proof of payment in 10 cases as recommended by the Commission, thereby providing relief for victims and their families. Altogether, compensation exceeding Rs. 1 crore was reported as disbursed, marking a significant step in ensuring justice and redress for human rights violations.

Various cases of serious human rights violations were taken up. In a case pertaining to a woman victim, the Commission directed the Bihar DGP to provide her protection and a dedicated helpline number she can call in case of any threat or when in need. The DGP was further directed to constitute an SIT as directed by the Commission.

In another case involving the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl in Maner area of District Patna, the Commission recommended payment of Rs. 5 lakh as relief to the next of kin (NoK) of the victim. In two other cases of death in judicial custody, the Commission observed negligence of jail/ medical officials and recommended relief of Rs.15 lakh.

On Day-2 of the hearing today, the NHRC Chairperson heard 10 cases of alleged bonded labour. The Secretary, Labour, Labour Commissioner and other officers of Bihar Government were present. In one bonded labour case, the Commission expressed its displeasure over a Prison official representing the District Magistrate. In two cases pertaining to child labour, the Commission has directed the Labour Secretary to submit a detailed report as per the format given by the Commission.

In a case of alleged practice of multi-generation bonded labour, the Commission directed the Director General of Investigation, NHRC to conduct an on-the-spot enquiry.

On the same day, the Division Bench of the Commission comprising the Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani heard 33 cases, which included compliance matters and other complaints of alleged violation of human rights. Three cases not included in the list were taken up out of turn on a mention made by the complainant. During the proceedings, the Commission closed 10 cases after hearing the parties and reviewing compliance reports along with proof of payment of compensation of Rs. 40 lakh to the NoK of the deceased. In five other cases of death in judicial/ police custody wherein the Commission observed negligence of jail/ police officials, monetary relief of Rs. 30 lakh has been recommended. In other matters, further reports have been sought from the authorities.

After the hearing, the Commission interacted with representatives of NGOs, civil society organisations and Human Rights Defenders on important issues pertaining to the State of Bihar. The Chairperson accepted their suggestion for better coordination with the NHRC.

The Commission also held a meeting with senior officers of the State Government. Important issues like non/ delayed submission of reports to the Commission, lack of information among authorities about laws and Supreme Court judgments, issues pertaining to identification, rescue, release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, violation of human rights by police, crimes against women and children including human trafficking, lack of proper implementation of the prohibition laws and resultant loss of lives, protection of children including child labour, school safety and child welfare, monitoring of shelter homes, correctional institutions and other residential care facilities were discussed. Concluding the Open Hearing and Camp Sitting, the NHRC Chairperson appreciated the officers for their cooperation, which helped in providing relief to the victims.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
CDS Extends Greetings on Indian Air Force Day
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force (IAF), General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) & Secretary, Department of Military Affairs (DMA), extended his greetings and felicitations to all personnel of the IAF, veterans, civilians and their families. Paying tribute to the rich legacy of valour, professionalism and selfless service, he lauded the IAF for its sustained operational excellence and ability to employ air power decisively in an increasingly contested and technology-driven battle space. He said that the theme of this year’s Air Force Day- “Indian Airforce: Infallible, Impervious and Precise”- captured the true essence and ethos of the IAF.

 The CDS outlined that from the skies of conflict to the skies of humanitarian assistance, the IAF has always demonstrated that air power is not merely about air combat, it is about national power, national resilience and national service. The IAF’s performance in various operations is testament to India’s strategic prowess and unwavering commitment to safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty and security. He equally commended IAF’s dependable role as first responder during Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) operations, both within the country and overseas, earning the trust and gratitude of all.

Acknowledging the IAF’s steady progress towards Jointness, Aatmanirbharta and Innovation (JAI), he appreciated the induction of indigenous platforms, advanced weapon systems and emerging technologies, along with the continuous evolution of operational concepts and doctrines. He also appreciated IAF’s participation in bilateral and multinational exercises, including the ongoing Exercise Tarang Shakti that has helped strengthening interoperability, operational preparedness and strategic partnerships.

In his message to all air warriors, the CDS exhorted them to remain steadfast in their commitment, remain unwavering in the face of adversity and remain purposeful in every mission.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Union minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated various new facilities of ICAR-IIAB in Ranchi through video conferencing
Shri Chouhan appreciates the efforts of scientists in taking technologies from “Lab to Land” 
Shri Chouhan highlights the importance of scientific agriculture, improved seeds, integrated farming, balanced nutrient management and location-specific agricultural technologies for Jharkhand
ICAR-IIAB organises Pre-Rabi Kisan Goshti for 1,500 Farmers
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

The ICAR–Indian Institute of Agricultural Biotechnology (ICAR-IIAB), Garhkhatanga, Ranchi, organized a Pre-Rabi Kisan Goshti-cum-Agricultural Input Distribution Programme under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP) and Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) on 8th October, 2026. The programme brought together around 1,500 farmers from Ranchi, Khunti, Gumla and Ramgarh districts to facilitate direct interaction between farmers, scientists and policymakers and to promote the adoption of scientific and sustainable agricultural practices.

On this occasion, the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated various new facilities of ICAR-IIAB through video conferencing. The facilities inaugurated included the Admin-cum-School Building, Birsa Munda Multipurpose Hall, Jaipal Singh Munda Sports Complex, NEXTGEN Breeding Facility and laid the foundation for a new Guest House facility at ICAR-IIAB worth Rs 119 Crore rupees.

In his address, Shri Chouhan highlighted the importance of scientific agriculture, improved seeds, integrated farming, balanced nutrient management and location-specific agricultural technologies for Jharkhand. He also appreciated the institute’s efforts towards taking research and technologies to farmers and called for sustained farmer awareness and field-level extension.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan highlighted the rich natural and traditional heritage of Jharkhand and described ICAR-IIAB as an important confluence of agricultural research, innovation and self-reliance. He emphasized that while traditional knowledge remains valuable, contemporary agricultural challenges require farmers to increasingly adopt scientific and technology-driven farming practices suited to local resources and agro-climatic conditions. He stressed the importance of ensuring timely availability of improved seeds and taking appropriate agricultural technologies from research institutions to farmers’ fields.

The Union Minister emphasized the importance of integrated farming, including vegetables, cereals and livestock, along with proper knowledge of balanced fertilizer use. He particularly stressed the need to protect farmers from fake seeds, counterfeit fertilizers and substandard pesticides. He also called for effective implementation of farmer welfare schemes and ensuring that their benefits reach every village. Highlighting the importance of preparing farmers for the forthcoming Rabi season, he appreciated the efforts of scientists in taking technologies from “Lab to Land” and urged them to undertake a nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyan in the coming days.

Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, highlighted the central role of farmers in the country’s food security and development. He emphasized the adoption of modern agricultural technologies, value addition, stronger Farmer Producer Organisations and Krishi Vigyan Kendras, soil testing and balanced fertilizer use. He also encouraged farmers to experiment with natural farming on a part of their cultivated area and stressed the need to protect farmers from spurious seeds, counterfeit fertilizers and substandard pesticides. He called for effective implementation of farmer welfare schemes and stronger efforts to take agricultural technologies from Lab to Land.

Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, highlighted the potential of eastern India for a new agricultural transformation and emphasized the importance of strengthening agricultural research and knowledge institutions in Jharkhand. He called for wider adoption of Rice-Fallow Intensification, location-specific crop and variety selection, improved livestock productivity and research addressing challenges such as acidic soils and phosphorus deficiency. He also stressed the importance of natural and organic farming and appropriate planning for the forthcoming Rabi season.

Addressing the programme, Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR, emphasized the need to align agricultural research with farmers’ requirements and ensure that technologies reach the last mile. He also highlighted the importance of student development, appropriate guidance and strengthening opportunities in agricultural research.

Earlier, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, accompanied by Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR; Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR; Dr. Sujay Rakshit, Director, ICAR-IIAB; and Dr. Vijay Pal Bhadana, Joint Director (Research), ICAR-IIAB, visited various facilities of the institute. The visit included the Dairy Farm, Crop Research and Training Centre, NEXTGEN Breeding Facility and Integrated Farming System (IFS) Unit. At the Dairy Farm, the Minister was briefed on Embryo Transfer technology for genetic improvement of livestock. At the IFS Unit, the dignitaries interacted with farmers and were briefed on integrated farming, agricultural waste recycling and resource-efficient practices. The Minister also participated in a plantation drive and interacted with progressive farmers. An exhibition showcasing crop varieties, livestock and dairy technologies, research achievements, agricultural schemes and farmer-oriented innovations by ICAR institutes and Government agencies of Jharkhand was also organized.

The Kisan Goshti focused on Farmer Producer Organisations and opportunities in Jharkhand, ethno-veterinary medicines and dairy farming, fruit crop production technologies, Integrated Pest Management in Rabi crops, crop diversification and Integrated Farming Systems, organic and natural farming, livestock feeding management, and lac cultivation. Farmers interacted with scientists and technical experts and received practical guidance on improved agricultural and livestock practices. Various agricultural and livestock inputs, including Nano Urea, Nano DAP, mineral mixture, improved seed varieties, wheat, pea, mustard and vegetable seed kits, a milk can cooler, and high-yielding tomato and brinjal seed varieties, were distributed to participating farmers. Publications and technologies developed by ICAR institutes were also released on the occasion.

On the occasion, Dr. R. Ramani, former Officer on Special Duty; Dr. K. K. Sharma, former Director (In-charge); Dr. Tilak Raj Sharma, former Acting Director and Joint Director (Research); and Dr. Arunnava Patanayak, first regular Director, ICAR-IIAB, were honoured for their contributions to the institute.

The programme concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Dr. Sujay Rakshit, Director, ICAR-IIAB, who expressed gratitude to the dignitaries, farmers, scientists, officials, staff, students and all stakeholders for their participation and support. The event reaffirmed ICAR-IIAB’s commitment to strengthening farmer–scientist–policy linkages and translating agricultural research and innovation into practical technologies for farmers of Jharkhand.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Chairs CEO Round Table on the Future of Telecom at India Mobile Congress 2026
“India Moving Towards End-to-End Telecom Value Chain, Shaping the Rules, Equipment and Innovation”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia
Telecom and Technology Leaders Explore New Frontiers in AI, Advanced Networks and Digital Innovation
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 8:28PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, participated in a high-level CEO Round Table on The Sovereign Inflection & The Future of Telecom during the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.

The leadership dialogue brought together senior representatives from the telecommunications, digital infrastructure, network equipment, technology and consulting sectors to deliberate on emerging opportunities and strategic priorities shaping the future of India’s telecom sector. The session was part of IMC 2026, organised under the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”, with a focus on translating innovation into scalable, resilient and globally relevant digital capabilities.

The Round Table witnessed the participation of senior industry leaders from leading telecom service providers, network equipment manufacturers, technology companies, digital infrastructure firms and industry advisory organisations. The discussions reflected strong industry engagement and focused on advancing telecom infrastructure, fostering innovation, strengthening indigenous capabilities and supporting the next phase of India’s digital growth. Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, also participated in the deliberations along with senior officials from the Department.

The discussions centred on the rapidly evolving telecom value chain and the convergence of Artificial Intelligence, cloud and compute, advanced connectivity, intelligent networks and next-generation communication technologies. The participants also deliberated on strengthening domestic capabilities, fostering innovation, building resilient digital infrastructure and creating an enabling policy environment to support sustained investment and technological advancement.

Shri Scindia also said “I think we have been meeting quite regularly and therefore this is not an annual meeting for any of us. But having said that, what has come out very clearly in this year's IMC is that we have achieved a lot in the last decade. Both in terms of coverage, penetration, affordability, inclusivity, innovation and really providing the foundational layer for a lot of application platforms to be innovated in our country. We are the second largest telecom market, we are the second largest mobile phone producer. Now end to end value chain is going to be produced in India thanks to the vision of our Prime Minister with 8-9 semiconductor fabs coming up in India. And therefore the fundamental inflection point today is going to be based on who writes the rules, who makes the equipment, who designs innovation, who builds the technology.”

Addressing the industry leadership, Shri Scindia emphasised the importance of a partnership-based approach between the Government and industry in shaping the next phase of India’s telecom journey. He underlined the role of the Department of Telecommunications as an enabler and facilitator in fostering an ecosystem in which all stakeholders could contribute to the growth and development of the sector.

The Minister highlighted that the telecom ecosystem encompassed network equipment and optical fibre manufacturers, telecom service providers, internet service providers, applications, platforms and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence. He emphasised that the collective strength of these interconnected segments would play an important role in determining the future competitiveness and resilience of India’s digital economy. Importance of moving beyond connectivity towards technologies and digital infrastructure that created wider economic and social value. He highlighted India’s expanding digital ecosystem and the growing role of telecommunications as an enabling foundation for digital public infrastructure, emerging technologies, innovation and economic growth.

The Round Table provided an opportunity for industry leaders to share their perspectives on sectoral developments, technology adoption, investment opportunities and policy and regulatory priorities required to support the next phase of telecom growth. The interaction reflected the Government’s continued commitment to maintaining an open and constructive dialogue with industry and ensuring that policy frameworks remained responsive to technological and market developments.

The deliberations at the CEO Round Table reinforced the vision of “Scale Without Boundaries” by bringing the Government and industry together to shape a future-ready telecom ecosystem based on innovation, resilience, trusted infrastructure, indigenous capabilities and global competitiveness.

The Department of Telecommunications reiterated its commitment to continued engagement with industry stakeholders, innovators, technology companies and other partners for the development of a robust and inclusive digital communications ecosystem and for strengthening India’s position as a global hub for telecom innovation and technology.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA receives Rs 9.68 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Framework during April–September 2026
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 8:18PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) received Rs 9.68 crore from users of India's biological resources during the period from 01.04.2026 to 30.09.2026, in accordance with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, and the ABS Regulations. Of the total receipts, Rs 9.56 crore was received towards access to biological resources from various sectors as given below.

Sector-wise Contributions

The Agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts, with Rs 7.16 crore, followed by Food & Beverages at Rs 1.59 crore and Animal Husbandry at Rs 62.01 lakh. Receipts classified under IPR-related applications amounted to Rs 11.24 lakh. Other receipts were from AYUSH, Red Sanders wood, Cosmetics and others.

Sector

ABS Receipts (in Crores)

Agriculture

7.16

Food & Beverages

1.59

Animal husbandry

0.62

0.21

0.06

0.04

Total

9.68 crore

Key Contributions

M/s East West Seeds India Ltd was the largest ABS contributor, with around Rs 2.01 crore across multiple payments. The single largest ABS payment was Rs 1.17 crore from M/s Synergia Life Science Ltd. Other significant ABS contributions included M/s Tata Chemicals Pvt Ltd (Rs 52.06 lakh), M/s Indena India Pvt Ltd (Rs 45.89 lakh), M/s Grow Indigo Ltd (Rs 45.79 lakh), M/s Novozymes South Asia (Rs 44.11 lakh), and M/s Nongwoo Seed India (Rs 40.53 lakh).

M/s Nunhems India Ltd made upfront payments of around Rs 1.64 crore. Contributions were received from both domestic and international entities, including entities from Sri Lanka, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea and Bhutan.

Diversity of Biological Resources

The receipts reflect the utilisation of a diverse range of biological resources across agriculture, food, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medicinal plants, microorganisms and livestock. These include agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd.

The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium. The range further includes livestock genetic resources such as Mithun (Bos frontalis), Jersey cattle (Bos taurus) and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material.

Linking Benefit Sharing with Biodiversity Conservation

Since 2008, the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country.

The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits. Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers.

The ABS mechanism provides a framework through which India is progressively translating the utilisation of its biological diversity into tangible outcomes for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and benefit of local communities. The receipts generated during the period reflect the continued implementation of India's ABS framework and the fulfilment of benefit-sharing obligations by users of biological resources.

Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Puts Global Partnerships, Youth & Women at the Heart of India's Maritime Future

India's maritime future will be written by its young people: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal
Minister of State Shantanu Thakur Held Bilateral Talks with Greece, Lithuania, Mozambique & Myanmar on Ports, Shipbuilding & Seafarer Skills
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal held bilateral meetings with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan on Day 2 of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026, carrying India's maritime partnerships across the Gulf, Europe and the neighbourhood. He also placed young people and women at the centre of India's maritime journey.

With a delegation from the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), Sarbananda Sonowal discussed Saudi participation in Indian port projects such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay. The two sides also discussed cooperation in shipbuilding, seafarer training and resilient supply chains. Saudi Arabia expressed their interest to invest in India’s port projects and in the Maritime Development Fund (MDF).

With Flemish Minister for Mobility, Public Works, Ports and Sport, Annick De Ridder, Sonowal proposed exploring a green shipping corridor linking Indian ports with Antwerp-Bruges. Both sides discussed green fuels, smart port technology, and dredging. VOC Port has signed an agreement with Port of Antwerp Port for training in capacity building in green shipping, and green fuel. 

With Lyonpo Chandra Bahadur Gurung, Minister of Infrastructure and Transport of Bhutan, Sonowal highlighted National Waterway-2 and the Jogighopa terminal as Bhutan's gateway to global trade. The ministers discussed the potential of the Manas and Sankosh rivers, and the connectivity with the national waterways for improved cargo movement. Both the ministers discussed maritime training for Bhutanese youth at the Centre of Excellence in Dibrugarh which is being developed.

"Our talks with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan show how India's maritime partnerships are growing across regions," said Sarbananda Sonowal. "With Saudi Arabia, we are exploring investment in ports, shipbuilding and resilient supply chains. With Belgium, we are working towards a green shipping corridor and smarter ports. With Bhutan, we are opening the Brahmaputra as a gateway for our neighbour to reach global markets and build skills for its youth. Under the leadership of our visionary Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is a trusted partner for a connected, green and prosperous maritime future."

At The Future is Blue: The Next Maritime Generation and Ocean Changemakers: Women, Youth and India's Maritime Journey, Sarbananda Sonowal heard from young Indians and women about their aspirations for the sector. The session had the participation of an all-women tri-service sailing expedition which inspired the women cadets.

Indian seafarers have grown from 1.27 lakh to 3.23 lakh in twelve years, taking India from fifth place in 2015 to world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, with over 12% of the global workforce. Active women seafarers have risen from 1,599 in 2021 to 7,033 in 2025, supported by the Sagar Mein Samman initiative. India aims to raise that share through Mission 20% by 2030. Shipyard–ITI partnerships now provide 150 hours of on-the-job training, and a structured six-month onboard programme for GP Rating and Maritime Catering trainees bridges pre-sea training and life at sea.

"India's maritime future will be written by the youth," said Sarbananda Sonowal. “Today, our seafarers are trusted and respected on every ocean, and more women than ever are choosing careers at sea. Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we are building the skills, institutions and opportunities so that every young Indian who dreams of the sea can help lead the world's maritime economy."

Day 2 also featured plenaries on securing global trade chokepoints, the Global South at the maritime table, AI in maritime, green ports, equity in ocean futures, BRICS+ connectivity and green shipbuilding.

Union Minister of State of MoPSW, Shantanu Thakur held bilateral meetings with Greece, Lithuania, Mozambique and Myanmar on the sidelines of Sagarmanthan 2026. Thakur held a bilateral meeting with Stefanos Gkikas, Deputy Minister of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy of the Hellenic Republic (Greece), on strengthening India–Greece maritime cooperation. With Lithuania's Minister of Transport and Communications, Juras Taminskas, the minister proposed a work plan for the MoU between Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and the Port of Klaipėda, and discussed direct shipping links and green port cooperation. With Mozambique's Minister of Transport and Logistics, João Jorge Matlombe, he offered India's expertise in ports, shipbuilding, ship repair and seafarer training. With Myanmar's Deputy Minister of Transport, U Tun Lu, he discussed the next phase of Sittwe Port, cross-border inland water trade and maritime safety in the Bay of Bengal.

"From the Baltic to the Bay of Bengal, India is ready to share its strengths in ports, shipbuilding and seafarer skills so that we can grow together with our partners," said Shantanu Thakur. "Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has emerged as a trusted maritime partner for nations across regions. Through cooperation in green shipping, connectivity and capacity building, we are working towards safe, open and prosperous seas for all,” added Thakur.

Addressing a press conference at Sagarmanthan, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has moved from maritime potential to maritime performance. The Union Minister of State Shantanu Thakur along with the Secretary of MoPSW, Vijay Kumar also accompanied the Union Minister during the press conference.

Over the last twelve years, port capacity has risen from 1,561 to 2,817 MTPA, cargo handled from 1,052 to 1,668 million tonnes and inland waterways cargo from 29 to 218 million tonnes, while median container vessel turnaround has fallen from 35 to 23 hours. He noted that Sagarmanthan has grown from 1,700+ delegates from 61 countries in 2024 to participation from more than 70 countries this year, including 10 visiting Ministers, and has produced 100+ publications that strengthen India's role as Vishwaguru for the global maritime order. Highlighting India's push to build green hydrogen, ammonia and methanol capacity so that Indian ports become green fuel bunkering hubs, in line with the Net Zero 2070 commitment, he called for turning dialogue into joint research, investment and technology partnerships. "India is ready to work with the world for safer seas, greener shipping and shared prosperity," Sonowal said.

item.title: 9th National Review Workshop begins in Bastar, focusing on translating the vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ into tangible grassroots outcomes
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation 9th National Review Workshop begins in Bastar, focusing on translating the vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ into tangible grassroots outcomes Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, emphasis on accelerating cooperative transformation, institutional strengthening and inclusive growth Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani calls for strengthening democratic governance, transparency, accountability and good governance…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
9th National Review Workshop begins in Bastar, focusing on translating the vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ into tangible grassroots outcomes
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, emphasis on accelerating cooperative transformation, institutional strengthening and inclusive growth
Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani calls for strengthening democratic governance, transparency, accountability and good governance across cooperative institutions
Autonomy of cooperative banks must be accompanied by accountability and effective supervision; State Registrars must play a more proactive role: Dr. Bhutani
Recent amendment to the NCDC Act opens new avenues of financial assistance for institutions engaged in promoting cooperative development
States to be consulted on developing a common digital marketing platform for cooperative products and a model cooperative banking framework
Special focus on strengthening value chains in exports, organic products and seeds through national cooperative institutions NCEL, NCOL and BBSSL
Workshop reviews successful State-level initiatives and three-month action plans covering PACS, dairy cooperatives, cooperative banking, digitalisation and business diversification
Two-day Workshop emphasises developing practical models and future strategies for the cooperative sector through exchange of State experiences, challenges and innovations
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

In furtherance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, sustained efforts are being undertaken to make India’s cooperative sector stronger, more transparent, accountable and economically vibrant. As part of these efforts, the Ministry of Cooperation is organising the 9th National Review Workshop on 8–9 October 2026 in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, under the theme ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi — The Road Ahead: Scaling Impact through Cooperative Transformation’. The workshop aims to review progress under major cooperative initiatives, facilitate the exchange of successful practices and grassroots experiences among States, and develop outcome-oriented action plans for the next three months. The workshop brings together senior officials from various States, Registrars of Cooperative Societies, representatives of national cooperative institutions and federations, and key stakeholders from across the cooperative ecosystem. The two-day Workshop has been designed as an important platform for State-led deliberations and knowledge-sharing, with detailed discussions focusing on the revival of cooperative institutions, financial strengthening, business diversification, digitalisation, capacity building and improved market access.

Addressing the inaugural session, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani said that the suggestion to organise this workshop on cooperative development in Bastar, a district that has long been affected by Left Wing Extremism, had come from Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah himself, making the initiative particularly significant and meaningful. He emphasised that the objective of the workshop was not merely to discuss various schemes and initiatives, but to translate the experiences and insights gained into concrete action on the ground. Stronger coordination among cooperative institutions, greater institutional collaboration and wider adoption of successful practices would further strengthen the cooperative movement, he said.

Underscoring the need to uphold democratic governance, transparency and the fundamental principles of cooperation at every level, Dr. Bhutani highlighted the vital role played by cooperative institutions in the economic empowerment of small businesses and ordinary citizens, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. Referring to the cooperative banking sector, Dr. Bhutani said that cooperative banks serve as an important channel for delivering financial services to sections of society that often find it difficult to access adequate credit and other banking facilities from commercial and private banks. He stressed that institutional autonomy must go hand in hand with accountability and effective supervision.

Highlighting shortcomings in the administration and governance of cooperative banks, he called for a more systematic and strategic monitoring framework. He urged Registrars of Cooperative Societies across States to exercise greater vigilance and play a more proactive role in strengthening supervision. Weaknesses in oversight, he cautioned, could have consequences extending beyond individual institutions and adversely affect the credibility of the cooperative sector as a whole.

The Secretary said that the Ministry of Cooperation is working in close coordination with the Reserve Bank of India to strengthen the resource-mobilisation capabilities of cooperative banks and enhance opportunities for providing financial assistance at concessional rates to farmers and other stakeholders associated with the cooperative sector. He also emphasised the need to make cooperative banking more competitive through the adoption of modern technologies, stronger risk management practices and measures to enhance customer confidence.

Highlighting the importance of financial resources for cooperative development, Dr. Bhutani said that the participation of NABARD's team in the Workshop would provide an opportunity for meaningful deliberations on financing various schemes and institutions. He informed participants that a dedicated session with the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) had also been scheduled to examine the availability of financial assistance for cooperative initiatives and the specific requirements of States. He noted that NCDC has emerged as a major institution providing financial and institutional support to the cooperative sector over the past two to three years. Referring to the recent amendment to the NCDC Act, he said that it has paved the way for extending financial assistance even to institutions that are not themselves cooperatives but are engaged in promoting cooperative development. This could open new opportunities for various State-level institutions to access financial assistance directly from NCDC. He urged States to make effective use of these opportunities and pursue financing initiatives through stronger coordination.

Highlighting the potential of the dairy sector, Dr. Bhutani said that the workshop would hold detailed deliberations on initiatives undertaken by dairy institutions, opportunities for developing them into cooperative institutions and measures to strengthen associated value chains. Discussions would also cover human resource policies, institutional capacity building, innovation and the emerging requirements of the cooperative sector. The Cooperation Secretary urged all States to share new experiments, successful models and innovations being undertaken in their respective cooperative sectors. He observed that several noteworthy initiatives are being implemented across States, but information about these efforts does not always reach other States. Citing initiatives undertaken by some States in activities related to electric vehicles, he said that sharing such experiences would help build a strong national knowledge base of successful practices and encourage other States to undertake similar innovations.

Referring to the proposal to develop a common cooperative digital platform for more effective marketing of cooperative products and agricultural produce, Dr. Bhutani said that the workshop would examine the progress made under the initiative and the potential role of States in taking it forward. He informed participants that the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) had also offered its support for the initiative. He said that the Ministry would seek suggestions and guidance from States before proceeding further, with the objective of developing a practical and effective mechanism to connect cooperative institutions with wider markets.

Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani emphasised that the deliberations at the workshop had been designed to be more participatory, allowing the Ministry to listen closely to the experiences, concerns and suggestions of States. These inputs would help in developing practical models, guidelines and circulars suited to ground-level requirements. He encouraged States to openly raise challenges relating to the functioning, financing, administration and business expansion of cooperative institutions.

Highlighting the role of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and tribal cooperative institutions, the Secretary Cooperation said that visits to selected cooperative institutions had also been included in the Workshop programme. These visits would provide participants with an opportunity to observe their functioning first-hand and understand practices being adopted at the local level. He stressed the need to link PACS and tribal cooperatives with State and national cooperative federations to improve market access for their products and produce and enable members to secure remunerative prices.

Calling for a closer assessment of government procurement activities undertaken through PACS, Dr. Bhutani said that States where PACS are involved in government procurement should undertake a detailed evaluation of their actual experiences. He urged States to share information on the commissions received by PACS, their real economic gains, delays in payments and the overall financial viability of such activities. He said that successful practices from different States could be consolidated into practical models for wider adoption across the country.

During the inaugural session, Chief Secretary of Chhattisgarh Shri Vikas Sheel welcomed representatives of all participating States and institutions and assured full support from the Government of Chhattisgarh for the development of the cooperative sector. He expressed confidence that the workshop in Bastar would provide fresh impetus to cooperation among States, the exchange of experiences and the development of practical solutions. He said that the suggestions and outcomes emerging from the Workshop would help advance efforts to make cooperative institutions stronger, more transparent, accountable and effective.

On the first day of the workshop, the achievements under major initiatives of the Ministry of Cooperation during the preceding three months were reviewed and progress against national priorities and action plans for the next three months were discussed in detail. These included the formation of multipurpose PACS, computerisation of PACS, the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector, business diversification, cooperative banking and initiatives associated with NCEL, NCOL, BBSSL and NCDC.

During the workshop, thematic sessions were held on ‘Cooperative Growth Story — North Eastern States and Eastern Frontier’ with special attention to cooperative development in Left Wing Extremism-affected districts of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, ‘Cooperative Banking sector and measures to strengthen credit delivery, promote business diversification, adopt new technologies, improve risk management and enhance customer confidence, empowering primary cooperative institutions through national cooperative institutions like National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL), National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) and Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL). Discussions also covered strengthening the administrative and business capabilities of cooperative institutions, enhancing benefits for members and creating opportunities for sustainable development, emerging value chains through Multipurpose Primary Cooperatives (MPP) and Multipurpose Cooperative Committees (MCC).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Successfully Completes Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
4,710 Activities organised across the country, Achieving 160% of Target with participation of over 74,000 people
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting successfully completed the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, held from 17th September to 2nd October 2026, with the campaign culminating on Swachh Bharat Diwas. The campaign, undertaken on the theme “Swachhata Mein Sabki Bhagidari; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, underscored the collective role and responsibility of every individual in advancing the vision and Sankalp of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. It also aimed to promote awareness of Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, strengthen youth participation in Swachhata, and foster collective ownership and Jan Bhagidari.

The Ministry, along with all its Media Units and their field offices, conducted 4,710 events across the country under different pillars of the Campaign, against a target of 2,943, thereby achieving 160 per cent of the finalised target. A total of 74,483 people participated in these activities.

Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting, Railways, and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, interacted with senior officials of the all three Ministries on 1 October as part of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign.

Addressing the officials, Shri Vaishnaw stressed that cleanliness must go beyond a campaign and become a lasting habit, woven naturally into everyday life and work. He urged that the message of Swachhata reach every office and every unit on the ground, down to the smallest field establishment.

Dr. L. Murugan, Hon’ble Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting, participated in “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” and other activities at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), Delhi, and called upon all to make cleanliness a people’s movement.

During the Campaign, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, reviewed the progress with Media Heads and Nodal Officers of the Media Units and directed them to optimise participation and ensure achievement of the targets finalised for the Campaign.

The activities covered different aspects of cleanliness and public participation. Under Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places, difficult and dirty spots and high-footfall public places were identified, mapped and cleaned in a time-bound manner. A total of 2,864 CTUs were transformed and public places were cleaned.

Under Swachh Paathshala: Yuva for Swachhata, students and youth were engaged and sensitised towards Swachhata through activities such as ‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’, exposure visits to Solid Waste Management facilities and ‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’, including interactions, debates and conversations on Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management. A total of 219 events were organised under this pillar.

Under Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir, single-window camps were organised for Safai Mitras/ Swachhagrahis/ Sanitation Workers, including linkages with eligible beneficiaries under various Central and State welfare schemes, preventive health check-ups and distribution of PPE kits/safety gear. Local-level felicitation was also undertaken to recognise their contribution towards Swachhata. 139 events were organised under this pillar.

The Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata pillar focused on door-to-door awareness drives and citizen engagement initiatives, including awareness on Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, promotion of four-way source segregation and composting, and activities such as Sports for Swachhata, Swachh Parv, Harit Parv, plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’.  A total of 1,418 events were organised under this pillar.

Under Swachhata Se Samriddhi, activities focused on promoting and strengthening the circular economy through initiatives such as “Kabaad se Jugaad – Waste to Wealth” and “Kabaad se Kala – Waste to Art”, along with old books, toys and clothes donation drives etc. 70 events were organised under this pillar.

The Ministry also organised special activities on World Tourism Day on 27th September 2026, and “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” on 1st October 2026, to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service, besides undertaking special cleanliness activities on Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2nd October 2026, with officers and staff stepping out to participate in Swachhata drives.

The Ministry, through its Media Units and field offices, reaffirmed its commitment to promoting Swachhata as a collective responsibility and a sustained public movement, with active participation of officers, staff, youth, Safai Mitras and citizens across the country.

****

item.title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Chairs Ministerial Programme in India Mobile Congress; Highlights Global Cooperation to Connect the Next Billion
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Chairs Ministerial Programme in India Mobile Congress; Highlights Global Cooperation to Connect the Next Billion “Our goal must be connectivity without boundaries and, ultimately, opportunity without boundaries”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia “Scale Without Boundaries” dialogue focuses on investment, inclusive connectivity and resilient digital infrastructure Global leaders deliberate on investment and next-generation connectivity at the Ministerial Programme Posted On: 08…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Chairs Ministerial Programme in India Mobile Congress; Highlights Global Cooperation to Connect the Next Billion
“Our goal must be connectivity without boundaries and, ultimately, opportunity without boundaries”: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia
“Scale Without Boundaries” dialogue focuses on investment, inclusive connectivity and resilient digital infrastructure
Global leaders deliberate on investment and next-generation connectivity at the Ministerial Programme
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, hosted the Ministerial Programme at India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 under the theme “Scale Without Boundaries: Investing in the Next Billion Digital Connections.” The high-level programme brought together ministers, international organisations, global telecommunications leaders and industry stakeholders to deliberate on strategies for expanding meaningful digital connectivity and accelerating investment in next-generation digital infrastructure.

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in his address, emphasised the importance of sustained investment, stronger international cooperation and enabling policy frameworks to expand affordable and meaningful digital connectivity.

“Scale Without Boundaries is not merely about expanding telecommunications networks; it is about expanding human opportunity. The next billion people we connect will be the hardest to reach, but they will also be the most transformative by bringing new learners, entrepreneurs, innovators and creators into the global digital economy. India’s experience demonstrates that connectivity can be scaled with affordability, innovation and public purpose. As we look towards 5G-Advanced, 6G, satellite networks and AI, our shared responsibility is to ensure that geography, income or circumstance never becomes a barrier to opportunity. Our goal must be connectivity without boundaries and, ultimately, opportunity without boundaries.” said Shri Scindia.

The programme provided a platform for discussions on policy, regulation, investment and international cooperation, with a focus on advancing affordable, reliable, resilient and inclusive digital connectivity and strengthening the foundations of the global digital economy.

The Ministerial Programme featured H.E. Ms. Liisa-Ly Pakosta, Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs, Estonia, and H.E. Mr. Hideo Fuseda, Vice-Minister for International Affairs, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan.

The programme further brought together leading voices from the global telecommunications ecosystem, including Mr. Seizo Onoe, Director, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, International Telecommunication Union (ITU), and Mr. John Giusti, Chief Regulatory Officer and President of the GSMA Foundation.

Focus on the Next Billion Digital Connections

The discussions highlighted the need for stronger collaboration among governments, industry and international organisations to respond to the rapidly evolving digital ecosystem. Participants deliberated on approaches to mobilise investment, strengthen enabling policy frameworks and expand affordable and meaningful connectivity, particularly as emerging technologies continue to transform the global communications landscape.

The Ministerial Programme also underscored the importance of future-ready and resilient networks, international standards, innovation and strategic partnerships in advancing digital connectivity towards 2030.

Strengthening Global Partnerships for Inclusive Digital Growth

The deliberations reaffirmed the importance of coordinated efforts to ensure that the benefits of next-generation digital technologies reach a wider population. Participants emphasised the need for stronger international cooperation and partnerships to create an enabling environment for investment, innovation and sustainable digital development.

The programme reinforced the vision of “Scale Without Boundaries”, highlighting the role of technology, investment and international collaboration in advancing a more connected, inclusive and digitally empowered future.

For the Department of Telecommunications, the Ministerial Programme served as an important platform for bringing together global perspectives on the future of connectivity and identifying shared priorities for expanding digital access and strengthening resilient digital infrastructure.

The programme at IMC 2026 reaffirmed the collective commitment to advancing inclusive, affordable, reliable and meaningful connectivity, while fostering partnerships that can help connect the next billion people and support a more digitally empowered world.
